Family Cookbook

Breakfast

★ Glazed Cinnamon Rolls (Tangzhong Version)

One dozen round rolls | Cook: 15-17 minutes

This dough uses a tangzhong (a pre-cooked flour-and-milk paste) for a softer, more tender roll and better keeping quality.
The filling here is doubled from the original for a more generous swirl, the glaze includes optional cinnamon and food coloring.

Source: The Breakfast Book, by Marion Cunningham, adapted to use a tangzhong (see https://www.theperfectloaf.com/how-to-make-tangzhong/)

Ingredients

Tangzhong

  • 1/4 cup (30g) all-purpose flour
  • 2/3 cup (160g) milk

Yeast

  • 1/4 cup warm water
  • 1 package active dry yeast
  • 1 teaspoon sugar

Dough

  • 3 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 cup sugar
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 pound (2 sticks) butter, chilled
  • 3 egg yolks
  • 1/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons milk (the reserved 1/3 cup from the tangzhong step, plus 2 tablespoons extra)

Filling

  • 1/2 cup (1 stick) butter, melted
  • 3/4 cup (12 tablespoons) sugar
  • 2 teaspoons cinnamon

Glaze

  • 1 1/2 cups confectioners' sugar
  • 2 tablespoons butter, room temperature
  • 2 tablespoons water
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon (optional)
  • Food coloring (optional, to taste)

Steps

  1. Tangzhong: In a small saucepan, whisk together the 1/4 cup (30g) flour and 2/3 cup (160g) milk until smooth. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened to a paste, about 2 minutes. Scrape into a small bowl; reserve 1/3 cup for the dough and discard the rest (or save for another use).
  2. Yeast: Put the warm water in a small bowl and sprinkle the yeast over. Stir in the 1 teaspoon sugar and let stand until foamy, about 5 minutes.
  3. Dry mix: In the bowl of a food processor, combine the flour, sugar, and salt; pulse briefly to blend. Add the chilled butter and pulse until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
  4. Dough: Transfer the flour-butter mixture to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment. Add the yeast mixture, the tangzhong, the egg yolks, and the 1/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons milk. Mix on medium speed until a smooth dough forms.
  5. Filling:
    • Combine the melted butter, sugar, and cinnamon in a small bowl to make a spreadable filling.
    • On a clean, floured countertop, roll out the whole batch of dough into one large, thin rectangle about 18-20 inches by 24 inches.
    • Spread the filling mixture evenly over the rectangle.
    • Using a pizza cutter, cut the rectangle lengthwise into 12 long strips. Roll each strip up individually into a spiral and place in a greased pan.
  6. Cover loosely and let rise for 1 hour. Meanwhile, make the glaze: Sift the confectioners' sugar into a small bowl, then stir in the butter, water, and optional cinnamon until smooth. Tint with food coloring if desired.
  7. Bake in a preheated 400°F oven for 15-17 minutes. Remove the rolls and set them on a rack over a piece of waxed paper.
  8. Spoon the prepared glaze over each roll while still hot.

★ Homemade Biscuits

8 large biscuits | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 15 to 20 minutes

Cut into 8 big squares rather than small rounds, so these come out extra generous.
Whole milk plus a splash of white vinegar stands in for buttermilk here — no need to track down real buttermilk.

Source: Adapted from Inspired Taste (inspiredtaste.net), by Adam and Joanne Gallagher

Ingredients

Soured milk

  • 1 3/4 cups whole milk
  • 1 tablespoon white vinegar

Dry ingredients

  • 4 cups (520 g) all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
  • 10 teaspoons (3 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon) aluminum-free baking powder, leveled
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
  • 2 tablespoons sugar
  • 2 teaspoons fine sea salt

Butter

  • 12 tablespoons (1 1/2 sticks; 170 g) cold butter

Steps

  1. Make the soured milk: Stir the vinegar into the whole milk. Let stand at least 5 minutes while you prepare the dough (it will look slightly curdled — that's fine).
  2. Heat the oven to 425°F. Set aside an oven-safe 10- to 12-inch skillet, preferably cast iron, or a cookie sheet lined with parchment.
  3. Dry ingredients: In a food processor, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt. Pulse 3 to 4 times to combine.
  4. Cut the cold butter into small cubes or thin slices; scatter over the flour mixture. Pulse 5 to 7 times, just until the butter is broken into pea-sized pieces.
  5. Transfer to a large bowl. Make a well in the middle; pour in the soured milk and stir gently with a fork or spatula just until the dough comes together (some dry bits are fine — don't overmix).
  6. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured work surface. Sprinkle a little flour over the top and gently bring the dough together with your hands.
  7. Fold the dough:
    • Without overworking the dough, gently pat it into a rough rectangle about 3/4 inch thick.
    • Fold the dough into thirds, envelope-style — bring one short side over the center, then fold the opposite side over it, like a letter.
    • Rotate the dough 90 degrees, then repeat the pat-and-fold two more times to build flaky layers.
  8. Pat the dough into a rough 3/4-inch-thick rectangle. Cut into 8 squares — no need to cut rounds or reroll scraps.
  9. Arrange the squares close together on the skillet (or parchment-lined cookie sheet) to help them rise tall.
  10. Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the tops are deeply golden brown and the biscuits have risen tall.

Raised Waffles

About 8 waffles

The batter keeps well in the refrigerator for several days.

Source: The Breakfast Book, by Marion Cunningham (originally from an early Fannie Farmer cookbook)

Ingredients

Yeast

  • 1/2 cup warm water
  • 1 package dry yeast

Batter (overnight)

  • 2 cups milk, warmed
  • 1/2 cup (1 stick) butter, melted
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon sugar
  • 2 cups all-purpose flour

Morning additions

  • 2 eggs
  • 1/4 teaspoon baking soda

Steps

  1. Yeast: In a large mixing bowl (the batter will rise to double its volume), put the warm water and sprinkle the yeast over. Let stand until foamy, about 5 minutes.
  2. Add the milk, butter, salt, sugar, and flour to the yeast mixture; beat until smooth and blended (a hand-rotary beater works well). Cover tightly and leave overnight at room temperature.
  3. Just before cooking, beat in the eggs and baking soda; stir until well mixed. The batter will be very thin.
  4. Pour about 1/2 to 3/4 cup batter into a very hot waffle iron. Bake until golden and crisp.

Baked German Pancake (or Dutch Babies)

One 12-inch pancake, or four 6-inch Dutch babies | Cook: 15-25 minutes

Source: The Breakfast Book, by Marion Cunningham

Ingredients

For the pan

  • Butter, for greasing the pan(s)

Batter

  • 3 eggs, room temperature
  • 1/2 cup milk
  • 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons butter, melted

To finish

  • 2 tablespoons lemon juice
  • Confectioners' sugar, for dusting

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 450°F. Butter one 12-inch ovenproof skillet, or four 6-inch skillets or pans with ovenproof handles.
  2. Beat the eggs in a mixing bowl until thoroughly combined, then add the milk and blend well.
  3. Sift the flour and salt over the egg mixture, whisking steadily until smooth. Add the melted butter and mix briskly until combined.
  4. Pour the batter into the pan(s). Bake for 15 minutes at 450°F for small pancakes; for one large pancake, bake 15 minutes at 450°F then reduce to 350°F and bake 10 minutes more.
  5. Sprinkle the lemon juice over the pancake(s) and dust with confectioners' sugar. Serve at once, while puffed and hot.

Egg Strata

Assemble the night before — ideal for brunch.
The amount of cheese is flexible; generous layers of cheddar work best.

Source: Family recipe card

Ingredients

Bread base

  • 8 slices bread (any kind)
  • Butter or margarine, for spreading

Custard

  • 4 eggs
  • 2 1/2 cups milk
  • 1/4 teaspoon dry mustard
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Cheese

  • Grated cheddar cheese, to taste (cheddar is best)

Steps

  1. Butter each slice of bread. Cut off crusts and cut into quarters. Butter a deep 9x13 Pyrex dish.
  2. Layer alternating bread and cheese in the dish.
  3. Beat together eggs, milk, mustard, and salt. Pour over bread and cheese. Let stand overnight in the refrigerator.
  4. Bake at 350°F for about 45 minutes.

Appetizers

General

Barbara Glabman's Cheese Ball

1 large cheese ball (12–16 as an appetizer)

Old English Sharp Cheddar Spread (Kraft) is still available. Smokelle tube cheese (Kraft) is no longer produced — substitute any smoked cheese spread, such as Kaukauna Smoked Cheddar Spread.
Best if refrigerated overnight before serving.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Barbara Glabman

Ingredients

Cheese mixture

  • 2 — 8 oz. packages cream cheese, softened
  • 1 glass (about 5 oz.) Old English or nippy cheddar cheese spread
  • 1 tube Smokelle processed cheese (Kraft) or substitute: any smoked cheese spread such as Kaukauna Smoked Cheddar Spread
  • 1 — 3 oz. package blue cheese, crumbled
  • 1/8 teaspoon onion salt
  • 3 small cloves garlic (or 2 medium), minced

For rolling

  • Chopped nuts and/or minced parsley

Steps

  1. Let all cheeses soften to room temperature.
  2. Combine cream cheese, cheddar spread, smoked cheese, and blue cheese in a large bowl. Mix until thoroughly blended.
  3. Add onion salt and garlic; mix well.
  4. Shape the mixture into a ball (or log) on a sheet of plastic wrap. Roll in chopped nuts, minced parsley, or a combination to coat the outside.
  5. Wrap tightly and refrigerate at least 2 hours (overnight is better) before serving. Serve with crackers.

Shrimp Dip

Makes about 2 cups

Source: Family recipe card (Grandmother Brenda)

Ingredients

  • 1 — 8 oz. block cream cheese, softened
  • 1 — 4.5 oz. can small shrimp, drained and mashed
  • 2 tablespoons mayonnaise
  • 2 tablespoons chili sauce
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 1/4 teaspoon curry powder

Steps

  1. Beat cream cheese until smooth and fluffy.
  2. Drain canned shrimp and mash well with a fork.
  3. Mix in mashed shrimp, mayonnaise, chili sauce, lemon juice, and curry powder until well combined.
  4. Taste and adjust seasoning.
  5. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving. Serve with crackers or sliced bread.

Central/Eastern European

Chopped Eggplant

A classic Jewish-style eggplant spread. The card gives only an ingredient list — steps are reconstructed from traditional method.

Source: Family recipe card (Grandmother Brenda; card reads "Recipe from Mother")

Ingredients

Eggplant

  • 1 large eggplant

Mix-ins

  • 1 medium onion, diced and fried in oil until golden
  • 3 hard-boiled eggs, finely chopped
  • Vinegar to taste (start with 1–2 teaspoons)
  • Mayonnaise to taste (start with 2–3 tablespoons)
  • Salt, pepper, and paprika to taste

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Pierce eggplant several times with a fork. Roast on a baking sheet until very soft and collapsed, 45–60 minutes. Let cool.
  2. While eggplant roasts, fry diced onion in a little oil over medium heat until golden and sweet, about 15 minutes. Set aside.
  3. Peel roasted eggplant and drain in a colander to remove excess liquid. Chop finely (do not puree).
  4. Combine chopped eggplant, hard-boiled eggs, and fried onion in a bowl.
  5. Add vinegar and mayonnaise to taste; season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of paprika.
  6. Refrigerate at least 1 hour. Serve as a spread with crackers, matzo, or rye bread.

Charoset (Ashkenazic Style)

Serves 6–8

Traditionally served at Passover Seder as a spread on matzah. Texture is a matter of preference — either chunky or finely chopped throughout.

Source: "Celebration: The Book of Jewish Festivals," ed. Naomi Black (Jonathan David Publishers, 1989)

Ingredients

  • 1 apple, preferably tart
  • 1/4 cup walnuts, pecans, or almonds, chopped
  • 1 teaspoon honey
  • Dash cinnamon
  • Dash orange zest
  • 1 tablespoon kosher red wine

Steps

  1. Chop the apple to your preferred texture. If making a fine mixture, chop the nuts finely as well.
  2. Mix together with the honey, cinnamon, orange zest, and wine. Serve immediately or refrigerate until the Seder.

Mediterranean/Greek

Gazpacho

Serves 6

From a recipe card kept by the family, compliments of Restaurant Laurent — a classic New York restaurant. Serve in chilled bowls with condiments passed at the table.

Source: Restaurant Laurent, 111 East 56th Street, New York (family recipe card)

Ingredients

Soup base

  • 3 cloves garlic, mashed
  • 1 medium onion, peeled and chopped
  • 5 very ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
  • Small bunch flat-leaf parsley, chopped fine
  • 2 T wine vinegar
  • 3 T olive oil
  • 1/4 tsp paprika
  • 1 cup beef stock or consommé
  • Salt and pepper to taste

To serve

  • 1 cucumber, peeled, seeded, and diced
  • 1 green pepper, finely diced
  • 1/2 onion, finely diced
  • Croutons

Steps

  1. Put garlic and onion in a blender; blend until liquified.
  2. Add remaining soup base ingredients; blend 2–3 minutes.
  3. Season with salt and pepper. Chill thoroughly in refrigerator.
  4. Serve in chilled bowls. Pass cucumber, green pepper, onion, and croutons separately at the table for guests to add.

Salads

Greens

Butter Lettuce and Citrus Salad

Serves 2–3

"Supreming" citrus means cutting away the peel and pith, then slicing between the membranes to release clean segments.

Source: The Gourmandise School (The Pizza Class)

Ingredients

  • 1 head butter lettuce
  • 1 shallot
  • Salt & pepper to taste
  • 1 grapefruit or orange
  • 2 Tbsp lemon juice
  • ¼ cup olive oil

Steps

  1. Remove any wilted leaves from the butter lettuce. Tear into bite-sized pieces and place in a medium bowl.
  2. Mince the shallot and place in a small bowl with a pinch of salt and pepper.
  3. Supreme (segment) your grapefruit right over the small bowl to catch any juices. Set the segmented citrus aside.
  4. Add lemon juice to the shallot bowl, then whisk in the olive oil. Dress the butter lettuce with the citronette. Plate and tuck the segmented citrus into and on top of the greens.

Charred Broccoli and Cauliflower Salad

6 to 8 | Total: 30 min | Active: 25 min

Great as a side at a barbecue with grilled seafood or meat, or to take to a potluck.

Source: https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/ree-drummond/charred-broccoli-and-cauliflower-salad-19673188

Ingredients

Vegetables

  • 1 medium crown broccoli, broken into large florets
  • 1 medium cauliflower, broken into large florets
  • 3 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

Dressing

  • 2/3 cup mayonnaise
  • 1/3 cup Greek yogurt
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
  • Zest and juice of 1 lemon
  • Pinch kosher salt
  • Pinch freshly ground black pepper

Salad

  • 1 cup arugula
  • 1/2 cup dried blueberries, plus extra for garnish
  • 1/4 cup pickled red onions, plus extra for garnish
  • 2 tablespoons sunflower seeds, plus extra for garnish

Steps

  1. Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
  2. Toss the broccoli and cauliflower with the olive oil, salt, and pepper. Grill, turning as needed, until tender and well charred, 8–10 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl.
  3. Make the dressing: whisk together the mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, dill, parsley, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
  4. Spread the dressing onto a serving platter, leaving a well in the middle.
  5. Add the arugula, blueberries, pickled red onions, and sunflower seeds to the bowl with the charred vegetables and toss to combine.
  6. Mound the vegetable mixture into the well. Garnish with extra blueberries, pickled red onions, and sunflower seeds. Serve.

Coleslaw Salad

Source: Family recipe card (Grandmother Brenda)

Ingredients

Dressing

  • 1/4 cup vinegar
  • 1/2 cup oil
  • 1/2 cup sugar
  • 3/4 teaspoon pepper
  • 2 teaspoons salt

Salad

  • 1 package coleslaw mix
  • Dried cranberries, to taste
  • Slivered almonds, toasted, to taste

Steps

  1. Toast slivered almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, about 3–4 minutes. Let cool.
  2. Whisk together all dressing ingredients until sugar dissolves.
  3. Combine coleslaw mix, dried cranberries, and toasted almonds in a large bowl.
  4. Pour dressing over salad and toss. Let sit at least 15 minutes before serving so the cabbage softens slightly.

Joan's on Third Butter Lettuce Salad (Copycat)

Serves 4

Original recipe uses French feta; family uses goat cheese in oil instead. Shallot is in the original but was skipped. Dressing recipe from CopyKat Recipes.

Source: Copycat recipe based on Joan's on Third, Los Angeles

Ingredients

Dressing

  • ¼ cup white wine vinegar (or champagne vinegar)
  • 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
  • 2–3 cloves garlic, minced
  • ¼ tsp lemon juice
  • Dried oregano, to taste
  • Dried basil, to taste
  • 9 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Salad

  • 1–2 large heads butter lettuce, washed, dried, and torn
  • ½ cup goat cheese, crumbled
  • ⅓ cup dried cranberries

Steps

  1. Make the dressing:
    • Whisk together the white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, lemon juice, oregano, and basil in a small bowl.
    • Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified.
    • Season with salt and pepper to taste.
  2. Place the torn butter lettuce in a large serving bowl.
  3. Sprinkle the crumbled goat cheese and dried cranberries evenly over the lettuce.
  4. Drizzle the vinaigrette lightly over the top just before serving and toss gently to combine.

Summer Salad

The dressing makes more than needed for one salad — leftovers keep refrigerated for 1–2 weeks.

Source: Family recipe card (Grandmother Brenda)

Ingredients

Dressing

  • 1 cup vinegar
  • 1/2 cup oil
  • 1/2 cup sugar
  • 1/2 cup ketchup
  • 2 cloves garlic, crushed
  • 1/2 teaspoon paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon mustard (dry or prepared)
  • 1 teaspoon salt

Salad

  • 1 bag romaine lettuce
  • 5–6 mushrooms, diced
  • 1 container cherry tomatoes
  • 1/2 to 1 mango, cubed
  • 1/2 avocado, cubed
  • Handful of salted cashews
  • Handful of sunflower seeds

Steps

  1. Whisk together all dressing ingredients. Refrigerate until ready to use.
  2. Tear romaine into a large bowl. Add mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, mango, and avocado.
  3. Top with cashews and sunflower seeds.
  4. Drizzle dressing over salad just before serving and toss.

Pasta Salads

General

Chuck Wagon Barbecued Pasta Salad

Serves 10

Source: Printed clipping

Ingredients

Pasta

  • 4 oz wagon wheel pasta

Salad

  • 1 (15-oz) can garbanzo beans, rinsed and drained
  • 1/3 cup chopped green sweet pepper
  • 1/3 cup chopped red sweet pepper
  • 8 oz smoked turkey breast, cubed
  • 4 oz mozzarella, cubed
  • 4 oz cheddar, cubed
  • 1 small red onion, thinly sliced into rings
  • 3 tablespoons sliced pitted ripe olives

Dressing

  • 1/3 cup bottled barbecue sauce
  • 3 tablespoons Dijon-style mustard

To serve

  • 1 head green and/or red-tip leaf lettuce
  • 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
  • Thin sweet pepper strips (optional)

Steps

  1. Cook pasta in boiling water until al dente; rinse and drain.
  2. Combine garbanzo beans, peppers, turkey, cheeses, onion, and olives in a large bowl. Whisk barbecue sauce and mustard together; add to turkey mixture. Add pasta and toss. Cover and refrigerate 2 to 24 hours.
  3. To serve: line a platter with lettuce leaves; shred remaining lettuce and mound in center. Spoon pasta mixture over lettuce. Sprinkle with pine nuts and garnish with pepper strips if desired.

Chinese

Asian Pasta Salad

Dressing must be made the night before.
The dressing uses a raw egg yolk — if preferred, substitute 1 tablespoon mayonnaise.

Source: Family recipe card

Ingredients

Noodles and protein

  • 1 lb cappellini (thin spaghetti), cooked and drained
  • 1 package firm tofu, cubed

Vegetables

  • 1 handful fresh snow peas
  • 1 can water chestnuts, sliced
  • 1 bunch scallions, chopped

Toppings

  • 1 small package sesame seeds, slightly toasted
  • 1 package pine nuts (pignoli)

Dressing (overnight)

  • 4 tablespoons dry sherry
  • 1 egg yolk
  • 3 tablespoons lemon juice
  • 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
  • 2 tablespoons soy sauce (or teriyaki sauce)
  • 2 tablespoons sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • Basil and Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes to taste
  • 1/2 cup olive oil
  • 1/2 cup vegetable oil

Steps

  1. Combine all dressing ingredients except oil and hot pepper. Refrigerate overnight.
  2. Before serving, stir oil and Aleppo pepper (or red pepper flakes) into dressing.
  3. Toss cappellini with tofu, snow peas, water chestnuts, and scallions.
  4. Add dressing and toss. Top with toasted sesame seeds and pine nuts.

Holly's Spicy Noodle Salad with Peanut Dressing

Serves 10 as appetizer, 6 as main

Asparagus, broccoli, or snow peas all work well in place of each other.

Source: Pacific Flavors by Hugh Carpenter; shared by Holly Arledge

Ingredients

Noodles

  • 1/4 lb dried Chinese spaghetti noodles (or thin spaghetti)
  • 2 tablespoons safflower oil (to toss after cooking)

Vegetables

  • 1 cup shredded iceberg lettuce
  • 1 cup fresh bean sprouts
  • 1 cup thinly sliced mushrooms
  • 1 lb pencil-thin asparagus (or broccoli or snow peas)
  • 1 large red bell pepper, sliced or julienned

Dressing

  • 1/4 cup white sesame seeds
  • 1/2 cup chicken stock, heated to boiling
  • 1/2 cup peanut butter
  • 1/4 cup red wine vinegar
  • 2 tablespoons dark soy sauce
  • 2 tablespoons sesame oil
  • 1 tablespoon dry sherry
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons Chinese chili sauce (optional)
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup minced green onions
  • 2 tablespoons finely minced ginger
  • 1 large garlic clove, minced

Steps

  1. Combine all dressing ingredients; mix well.
  2. Cook noodles in lightly salted boiling water about 4 minutes until firm. Drain; toss with safflower oil to prevent sticking.
  3. Combine noodles and vegetables, add dressing, and toss.

Meat Mains

Chicken

General

Baked Crunchy Hot Honey Chicken

6 | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 25 minutes | Total: 40 minutes

Source: Half Baked Harvest, by Tieghan Gerard

Ingredients

Crumb coating

  • 6 cups cornflakes (gluten-free if needed)
  • 1/4 cup grated parmesan cheese
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder

Egg wash

  • 2 large eggs, beaten
  • 2 tablespoons hot sauce

Chicken

  • 2 pounds chicken breast tenderloins
  • Extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling

Hot honey sauce

  • 1/2 cup honey
  • 2 to 3 tablespoons hot sauce
  • 1 to 3 teaspoons cayenne pepper
  • 3/4 teaspoon chipotle chili powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon onion powder
  • Sea salt

To finish

  • Fresh thyme, cilantro, or parsley

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Pulse the cornflakes, parmesan, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt in a food processor until fine crumbs form. Transfer to a shallow bowl.
  3. Beat the eggs with the hot sauce in a bowl; add the chicken and toss well to coat.
  4. Dredge the chicken through the crumbs, covering fully. Place on the baking sheet. For a thicker coating, dip back through the egg wash and crumbs a second time.
  5. Drizzle the chicken with olive oil. Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until crisp all around.
  6. Just before the chicken is done, warm the honey, hot sauce, cayenne, chili powder, onion powder, and garlic powder with a pinch of salt in a small saucepan over low heat until combined.
  7. Drizzle the warm sauce over the chicken. Top with fresh herbs.

Brown Butter Sage Skillet Chicken

4 | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 20 minutes | Total: 30 minutes

Thin-sliced chicken breasts cook fastest; if starting with standard breasts, slice horizontally through the middle for thinner cutlets.
Great served over egg noodles, orzo, or a light pasta.

Source: Nourish and Fete, by Monica

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, sliced or pounded thin
  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • 1/4 cup all-purpose flour

Oil and butter

  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter (of the 6 tablespoons below)
  • 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

Brown butter sauce

  • 4 tablespoons unsalted butter (the remainder of the 6 tablespoons total)
  • 1/3 cup fresh sage leaves
  • Juice of 1/2 lemon (reserve the other half for serving)
  • 1/2 cup white wine or low-sodium chicken broth

To serve

  • Lemon wedges

Steps

  1. Season both sides of the chicken generously with salt and pepper. Place the flour in a shallow bowl or plate and dredge each cutlet, shaking off the excess.
  2. Add 2 tablespoons of the butter and the olive oil to a large skillet over medium-high heat. When the butter melts, add the chicken and cook until golden brown, about 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
  3. Add the remaining 4 tablespoons butter to the skillet. When melted, add the sage leaves. Let the butter brown and bubble until it smells nutty and the sage is crispy, about 2 minutes.
  4. Add the lemon juice and wine (or broth) to the skillet. Simmer 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Return the chicken to the skillet and warm through. Serve with lemon wedges.

★ Company Baked Chicken

Marked "v. good!" on the original card.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Grandmother Brenda

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 2 chickens or equivalent amount of chicken parts
  • Black pepper
  • Garlic powder

Marinade

  • 1/2 cup honey
  • 1/2 cup soy sauce
  • 3 tablespoons oil

To finish

  • Sesame seeds

Steps

  1. Season the chicken pieces all over with pepper and garlic powder.
  2. Combine the honey, soy sauce, and oil to make the marinade.
  3. Add the chicken to the marinade, turning to coat. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator 24 hours, turning frequently.
  4. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
  5. Place the chicken skin-side down in a baking dish with the marinade. Bake uncovered 45 minutes.
  6. Turn the chicken pieces over, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and continue baking another 30 minutes, basting occasionally with the pan juices.

Creamy Spinach-Artichoke Chicken Stew

4 to 6 | Total: 50 minutes

Source: NYT Cooking, by Sarah DiGregorio

Ingredients

Aromatics

  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 1 large yellow or red onion, finely chopped
  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • 3 celery stalks, chopped
  • 8 garlic cloves, smashed and chopped

Braise

  • 2 cups chicken stock
  • 3/4 cup white wine
  • 2 to 2 1/4 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs
  • 1/2 lemon, juiced (about 1 1/2 tablespoons)
  • 1 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes

Spinach and artichokes

  • 1 (10-ounce) package frozen cut spinach
  • 1 (12-ounce) jar marinated artichoke hearts, drained (about 1 heaping cup)

To finish

  • 1/2 cup cream cheese (about 4 ounces)
  • 1/2 cup finely chopped fresh dill
  • 4 to 6 scallions, thinly sliced
  • Grated Parmesan cheese

Steps

  1. Aromatics:
    • In a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat, melt the butter. Add the onion, season lightly with salt, and cook, stirring, until softened, about 5 minutes.
    • Add the celery and cook, stirring, until softened, about 5 minutes, adjusting the heat as needed to avoid scorching. Stir in the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
  2. Pour in the stock and wine, and bring to a bubble. Add the chicken thighs, lemon juice, and Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes.
  3. Reduce the heat to maintain a low simmer and simmer, uncovered, 20 minutes.
  4. Add the frozen spinach and artichoke hearts. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook, stirring, to help the spinach defrost and the liquid reduce slightly, about 5 minutes.
  5. Add the cream cheese in dollops, stirring to melt it into the stew. Add the dill. Using two forks, coarsely break or shred the chicken into pieces. Taste and adjust seasoning.
  6. Divide among bowls and top with scallions and Parmesan.

Crispy Chicken With Lime Butter

4 | Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 35 minutes | Total: 40 minutes

The rendered chicken fat (schmaltz) can be saved to pan-fry vegetables, enrich a soup or sauce, or spread on toast.

Source: NYT Cooking, by Eric Kim

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 4 large bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 2 pounds)
  • Salt and pepper
  • 1 tablespoon peanut or canola oil

Aromatics

  • 2 garlic cloves, crushed

Pan sauce

  • 1/2 cup chicken stock or 1/4 cup water
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice, plus wedges for serving
  • 2 teaspoons maple syrup
  • 3 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into pats

To serve

  • Parsley, cilantro, basil, or mint leaves (optional)

Steps

  1. Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. If you have time, let sit at room temperature 10 to 30 minutes.
  2. Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the oil and swirl to coat the pan. Place the chicken skin side down and cook undisturbed until the skin is deeply golden and crispy, about 20 to 25 minutes.
  3. Add the garlic to the pan. Flip the chicken and cook until the bottom is lightly browned and the meat is cooked through, about 5 to 8 minutes more. Transfer to a plate.
  4. Pan sauce: Add the chicken stock, lime juice, and maple syrup to the skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook until slightly reduced, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and whisk in the cold butter a pat at a time until the sauce is glossy.
  5. Serve the chicken with the pan sauce, lime wedges, and the optional fresh herbs (lightly spritzed with lime juice and seasoned with flaky salt, if using).

★ Crispy Spice Rubbed Chicken Thighs

3 to 4 | Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 30 minutes | Total: 35 minutes

Source: Fifteen Spatulas

Ingredients

Spice rub

  • 1 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1 teaspoon ground chipotle pepper
  • 2 teaspoons yellow curry powder
  • 1 teaspoon paprika
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
  • 1/8 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cayenne pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons sea salt

Chicken

  • 2 to 3 pounds skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (about 5 pieces)
  • Olive oil

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F.
  2. Combine the ginger, chipotle pepper, curry powder, paprika, garlic powder, coriander, cardamom, cloves, cayenne, cumin, and salt in a small bowl.
  3. Trim excess fat from the chicken thighs. Rub the thighs all over with the spice mixture.
  4. Heat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat with enough olive oil to coat the bottom (about 2 tablespoons). Cook the thighs skin-side down, undisturbed, until the skin is deeply golden brown and crispy, about 10 minutes.
  5. Flip and cook 5 more minutes, then transfer the skillet to the oven. Bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until cooked through (internal temperature 165°F).

Grilled Buffalo Wings

6 to 8 | Total: 35 minutes

Crowding the wings close together on the grill is intentional — it creates steam that helps render the fat and keep the meat moist before crisping.

Source: Food Network, by Katie Lee Biegel, from The Kitchen

Ingredients

Dry rub

  • 1 tablespoon kosher salt
  • 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder

Wings

  • 3 pounds whole chicken wings

Buffalo sauce

  • 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 1/3 cup hot sauce
  • 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon honey

Steps

  1. Dry rub: In a small bowl, combine the salt, pepper, and garlic powder. In a large bowl, toss the wings with the rub to coat evenly.
  2. Preheat a gas grill to medium heat (about 350°F).
  3. Place the wings on the grill, crowding them close together so they're all touching. Grill, covered, 20 minutes, turning every 5 minutes.
  4. Meanwhile, heat the butter, hot sauce, vinegar, and honey in a saucepan over low heat, whisking to combine.
  5. In a clean large bowl, toss the wings with the sauce. Turn the grill up to medium-high. Use tongs to return the wings to the grill and cook, uncovered, turning once, until charred in spots, about 5 minutes more.

Skillet Chicken and Zucchini With Charred Scallion Salsa

4 | Total: 40 minutes

Any seasonal, quick-roasting vegetable can stand in for the zucchini — cherry tomatoes or asparagus both work well.
If cilantro isn't your thing, basil is a good substitute, or use a mix of the two.

Source: NYT Cooking, by Colu Henry

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 4 medium bone-in, skin-on chicken breasts (about 3 to 3 1/2 pounds), at room temperature
  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons canola or grapeseed oil

Zucchini

  • 1 1/2 pounds zucchini (3 to 4 medium), quartered lengthwise, then halved crosswise

Salsa

  • 1/4 cup fresh lime juice (about 2 limes)
  • 1 medium jalapeño, thinly sliced, seeded if you prefer
  • 1 bunch scallions (about 7 or 8), trimmed and halved crosswise
  • 1 cup roughly chopped fresh cilantro
  • 1/4 cup olive oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon light brown sugar
  • Flaky sea salt (optional)

Steps

  1. Heat the oven to 400°F. Pat the chicken very dry and season generously all over with salt and pepper.
  2. Heat the oil in a 12-inch cast-iron pan or other large, ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, add the chicken skin-side down and cook undisturbed until the skin is deeply golden, about 5 minutes. Transfer skin-side up to a plate.
  3. Remove the pan from the heat. Add the zucchini and toss to coat in the chicken fat; season with salt and pepper and arrange in an even layer. Nestle the chicken, skin-side up, on top of the zucchini. Roast until the chicken is cooked through, 20 to 25 minutes.
  4. Salsa:
    • In a medium bowl, stir together the lime juice and jalapeño; set aside.
    • Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the scallions and cook, tossing frequently, until they begin to brown and char slightly, about 5 minutes.
    • Finely chop the scallions and toss with the lime mixture.
    • Stir in the cilantro, olive oil, and brown sugar until the sugar dissolves. Season to taste with salt.
  5. Remove the chicken from the oven and let rest on a plate or cutting board about 5 minutes (return the zucchini to the oven to keep warm). Spoon the salsa over the chicken and zucchini.

Spring Chicken Paillard

4 | Total: 1 hour 25 minutes (includes marinating)

Inspired by the chicken paillard at Pastis in New York City.

Source: Food Network, by Katie Lee Biegel

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 4 small/medium boneless, skinless chicken breasts

Marinade

  • 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
  • 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
  • 2 teaspoons chopped fresh rosemary
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Green olive tapenade

  • 1 cup fresh parsley leaves
  • 1/2 cup pitted Castelvetrano olives
  • 2 tablespoons thinly sliced fresh chives, plus more for garnish
  • 1 teaspoon capers, drained
  • 1/2 teaspoon honey
  • 2 anchovies
  • 1 small shallot, roughly chopped
  • 1/2 lemon, zested and juiced
  • Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper

Sautéed greens

  • 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1 (8-ounce) bunch Swiss chard, stems trimmed, roughly chopped
  • 1 (8-ounce) bunch lacinato kale, stems removed, roughly chopped
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
  • Freshly ground black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar

To serve

  • Lemon wedges

Steps

  1. Chicken: Place a chicken breast on a cutting board, cover with plastic wrap, and pound with a meat mallet or rolling pin to an even 1/4-inch thickness. Repeat with remaining breasts.
  2. Whisk together the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, rosemary, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, thyme, oregano, and pepper in a shallow dish. Add the chicken and turn to coat.
  3. Cover and marinate in the fridge at least 30 minutes, up to 3 hours.
  4. Green olive tapenade: Meanwhile, in a food processor, combine the parsley, olives, chives, capers, honey, anchovies, shallot, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Pulse until finely chopped but not pureed. Season with salt and pepper.
  5. Let the chicken sit at room temperature while you preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
  6. Grill the chicken until charred and cooked through (165°F), 3 to 4 minutes per side.
  7. Remove to a platter and immediately spread the tapenade over the chicken so it soaks in the flavors.
  8. Sautéed greens: Heat the olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat until shimmering. Add the Swiss chard and kale and season with salt and pepper.
  9. Cook just until wilted (still some body), 3 to 4 minutes.
  10. Remove from the heat and drizzle with the red wine vinegar. Serve warm on top of the chicken. Garnish with more chives and lemon wedges.

Sweet and Sour Chicken

Flexible — same sauce works for a few pieces or a large batch

Sauce amounts stay the same whether cooking a few pieces or a large batch — it's very forgiving.
Russian dressing can be hard to find; regular French dressing (not creamy) works just as well.
Marcie's note: "You can't mess-up with this recipe — last night it was in the oven for 2½ hours!"

Source: Family recipe, credited to Marcie (in a letter to Lauren)

Ingredients

Sauce

  • 1 envelope dry onion soup mix
  • 1 bottle Russian salad dressing (regular French dressing works if Russian isn't available; NOT creamy French)
  • 1 bottle (about 18 oz) apricot preserves

Main

  • Chicken parts (any amount — see Comments)

Steps

  1. Spread chicken parts out in a baking dish. Cover with the Russian dressing, apricot preserves, and onion soup mix.
  2. Bake covered at 350°F for 1 hour, then uncover and continue baking for 30 minutes to 1 hour more. Check occasionally — if the chicken starts to look burned from the apricot preserves, re-cover.

Weeknight Fancy Chicken and Rice

4 to 6 | Total: 50 minutes

Garnish is flexible — dried cranberries, hazelnuts, or pine nuts can stand in for or join the apricots and almonds.

Source: NYT Cooking, from Asha Gomez and Martha Hall Foose, adapted by Sara Bonisteel

Ingredients

Aromatics

  • 1/4 cup ghee (or unsalted butter)
  • 1 large yellow onion, halved and thinly sliced
  • 6 green cardamom pods, crushed
  • 3 whole star anise
  • 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt

Garlic and spice

  • 6 garlic cloves, finely chopped
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons turmeric powder

Chicken

  • 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 3/4-inch pieces

Rice

  • 2 1/4 cups low-sodium chicken stock
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt (remaining from the 1 1/4 teaspoons above)
  • 1 1/2 cups Jasmine or Basmati rice

Garnish

  • 1/4 cup chopped dried apricots
  • 1/4 cup sliced raw almonds, toasted
  • 1/4 cup chopped cilantro leaves

Steps

  1. Aromatics and chicken:
    • Melt the ghee in a medium saucepan with a lid over medium-high heat.
    • Add the onion, cardamom pods, star anise, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring frequently, until the onion is soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
    • Add the garlic and turmeric; cook, stirring, 1-2 minutes, until very fragrant.
    • Add the chicken and cook 4 minutes, stirring to coat with the onion mixture.
  2. Rice:
    • Add the stock and remaining 1 teaspoon salt; increase the heat and bring to a boil.
    • Stir in the rice, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Simmer until the rice has absorbed the liquid, about 12 minutes.
    • Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, 12 minutes.
    • Remove the lid and fluff the rice with a fork.
  3. Transfer the chicken and rice to a bowl, removing and discarding the cardamom pods and star anise. Garnish with the apricots, almonds, and cilantro.

Latin/South American

Chicken Fajita Marinade

4 | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 1 minute | Total: 41 minutes (includes 30 minutes marinating)

This is a marinade rather than a full dish — cook the marinated chicken and vegetables however you like (grill, skillet, or oven).
Also works with other proteins, like shrimp, flank steak, or pork tenderloin.

Source: Dinner at the Zoo, by Sara Welch

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 1/4 cup olive oil
  • 1/3 cup lime juice
  • 1/4 cup water
  • 1 teaspoon sugar
  • 1 1/4 teaspoons kosher salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1 to 2 tablespoons chili powder, to taste (start with 1 tablespoon if your chili powder has real heat)
  • 1/4 teaspoon pepper

To marinate

  • 1 pound chicken, sliced
  • 1 1/2 cups sliced bell peppers
  • 1/2 cup sliced onion

Steps

  1. In a bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lime juice, water, sugar, salt, cumin, garlic, smoked paprika, onion powder, chili powder, and pepper.
  2. Add the sliced chicken, bell peppers, and onion to the bowl and toss to coat.
  3. Marinate at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours, then cook as desired — grilled, pan-seared, or baked — for fajitas.

D.L. Jardine's Fajita Marinade

Serves 4

Works for both chicken and beef; marinate all day or overnight for best results.

Source: https://www.food.com/recipe/d-l-jardines-fajita-marinade-336920

Ingredients

Liquids

  • 3/4 cup Worcestershire sauce
  • 1/4 cup light soy sauce
  • 2 tablespoons water
  • 1 tablespoon white vinegar
  • 2 tablespoons lime juice

Spice blend (combine in a small bowl)

  • 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon cumin
  • 1/2 teaspoon oregano

Steps

  1. Whisk together the liquids and spice blend until fully combined. Use immediately as a marinade, or refrigerate until ready to use.

Peruvian Roasted Chicken With Spicy Cilantro Sauce

4 | Total: 50 minutes, plus marinating

If aji amarillo/aji panca pastes aren't available, substitute a red chile paste like sriracha or sambal for the aji amarillo, and pasilla chile powder for the aji panca.

Source: NYT Cooking, by Melissa Clark

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 6 garlic cloves, finely grated or minced
  • 3 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon aji amarillo paste (or sriracha or sambal)
  • 1 tablespoon lime juice
  • 1 teaspoon aji panca paste (or 1 teaspoon ground pasilla chile powder)
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt

Chicken

  • 1 (3 1/2 to 4 1/2 pound) chicken, halved, or 4 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken parts
  • Extra-virgin olive oil, as needed

Spicy cilantro sauce

  • 1 cup cilantro leaves and tender stems
  • 3 to 4 jalapeños, seeded and diced
  • 1/4 cup (1 ounce) crumbled feta cheese
  • 1 garlic clove, chopped
  • 1 1/2 tablespoons lime juice, more to taste
  • 2 teaspoons chopped fresh oregano or basil
  • 3/4 teaspoon fine sea salt, more to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • 1/2 tablespoon aji amarillo or other chile paste
  • 1/2 teaspoon honey
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil

To serve

  • Lime wedges

Steps

  1. Whisk together the garlic, soy sauce, aji amarillo paste, lime juice, aji panca paste, mustard, cumin, pepper, and salt to make the marinade.
  2. Add the chicken, turning to coat all over. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, up to 12.
  3. Heat the oven to 450°F. Remove the chicken from the marinade and pat dry. Arrange skin-side up on a rimmed baking sheet; drizzle with olive oil.
  4. Roast until the skin is golden and the chicken is cooked through, 35 to 45 minutes (if using parts, remove the breasts earlier if they finish before the thighs).
  5. Meanwhile, make the sauce: blend the cilantro, jalapeños, feta, garlic, lime juice, oregano, salt, mustard, aji amarillo, honey, cumin, and olive oil until smooth. Taste and adjust.
  6. Carve the chicken; serve with the sauce and lime wedges.

Slow-Cooker Chicken Mole

6 | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 4 hours | Total: 4 hours 15 minutes

Makes extra sauce; keeps refrigerated up to 4 days or frozen up to 3 months. Good over rice, with pinto beans, or warm corn tortillas.

Source: Martha Stewart

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 4 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 12)
  • Coarse salt
  • 2 tablespoons oil, for browning

Mole sauce

  • 1 can (28 ounces) whole tomatoes
  • 1 medium yellow onion, roughly chopped
  • 2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed
  • 1 large chipotle chile in adobo sauce
  • 1/2 cup sliced almonds, toasted
  • 1/4 cup raisins
  • 3 ounces bittersweet chocolate, finely chopped (1/2 cup)
  • 3 garlic cloves, smashed and peeled
  • 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
  • 3/4 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon

To finish

  • Fresh cilantro leaves

Steps

  1. Season the chicken thighs with salt.
  2. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in batches, about 2 to 3 minutes per side, then transfer to the slow cooker.
  3. In a blender, puree the tomatoes, onion, ancho and chipotle chiles, almonds, raisins, chocolate, garlic, oil, cumin, and cinnamon until smooth.
  4. Add the tomato mixture to the slow cooker, cover, and cook until the chicken is tender: 4 hours on high (or 8 hours on low).
  5. Serve the chicken and sauce topped with cilantro.

Italian

Chicken Breasts and Garlic Balsamic Vinegar

Serves 4

Ingredients

Breading

  • 1/4 cup shredded wheat cereal
  • 1/2 cup ground cashews

Chicken

  • 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved (8 pieces)
  • Garlic powder to taste
  • Pepper to taste

Sauce

  • 3 tablespoons olive oil
  • 6 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 3/4 lb small-medium mushrooms, sliced, drained, and patted dry
  • 4 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
  • 3/4 cup canned chicken broth (or bouillon cube in water)
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 tablespoon butter

Steps

  1. Combine shredded wheat and ground cashews in a shallow dish to make the breading mixture.
  2. Slice mushrooms, drain, and pat dry. Set aside.
  3. Season chicken with garlic powder and pepper. Dredge in breading mixture.
  4. Heat oil in skillet over moderate heat. Cook chicken until browned, about 3 minutes per side.
  5. Add garlic cloves, turn chicken, and scatter mushrooms over all. Cook about 3 minutes.
  6. Add balsamic vinegar and broth. Add bay leaf. Cover and cook on low heat about 10 minutes, turning pieces as they cook.
  7. Transfer chicken to warm serving platter. Let sauce with mushrooms cook another 5 minutes. Stir in butter and remove bay leaf.
  8. Pour sauce over chicken and serve.

Chicken Cacciatore

4 to 5 | Total: 1 hour 45 minutes

Source: NYT Cooking, by Martha Rose Shulman

Ingredients

Dried mushrooms

  • 1/2 ounce dried mushrooms, like porcini (about 1/2 cup)

Chicken

  • 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
  • Salt and freshly ground pepper
  • 6 to 8 skinless chicken legs and/or thighs (thighs can be boneless)

Aromatics

  • 1 small onion, minced
  • 1 small carrot, minced
  • 3 ribs celery, minced
  • 2 large garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tablespoons fresh minced Italian parsley
  • 1 heaped teaspoon minced fresh rosemary, or 1/2 teaspoon crumbled dried rosemary
  • 1/4 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes

Mushrooms and wine

  • 1/2 pound mushrooms, trimmed and sliced
  • 1/2 cup red wine

Tomatoes

  • 1 28-ounce can chopped tomatoes, pulsed in a food processor

Steps

  1. Soak the dried mushrooms:
    • Place in a bowl or heat-proof measuring cup and pour on 2 cups boiling water. Let sit 15 to 30 minutes, until softened.
    • Drain through a strainer lined with cheesecloth or a paper towel, set over a bowl, reserving the liquid.
    • Rinse the mushrooms in several changes of water, squeeze out excess water, and chop coarsely.
    • Measure out 1 cup of the reserved soaking liquid; set aside.
  2. Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil over medium-high heat in a large, heavy nonstick skillet or Dutch oven. Season the chicken and brown on both sides; remove to a platter.
  3. Aromatics:
    • Turn the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil, the onion, carrot, and celery, plus a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, until softened, about 5 minutes.
    • Add the garlic, parsley, rosemary, Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, and salt to taste. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook 5 minutes.
  4. Stir in the fresh and dried mushrooms; increase the heat to medium and cook, stirring, until just tender, about 5 minutes.
  5. Stir in the wine and bring to a boil; cook, stirring, a few minutes until reduced by about half.
  6. Add the tomatoes and salt and pepper to taste. Cook over medium heat 5 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the tomatoes have cooked down somewhat.
  7. Stir in the reserved mushroom soaking liquid.
  8. Return the chicken to the pan, submerging it in the tomato mixture. Cover and simmer over medium heat 30 minutes, until cooked through.

Chicken Piccata

4 | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 25 minutes | Total: 40 minutes

Source: Food Network, by Giada De Laurentiis

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 2 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, butterflied and cut in half
  • Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • All-purpose flour, for dredging

For browning

  • 6 tablespoons unsalted butter, divided
  • 5 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided

Sauce

  • 1/3 cup fresh lemon juice
  • 1/2 cup chicken stock
  • 1/4 cup brined capers, rinsed

To finish

  • 1/3 cup fresh parsley, chopped

Steps

  1. Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Dredge in flour and shake off the excess.
  2. Brown the chicken:
    • In a large skillet over medium-high heat, melt 2 tablespoons butter with 3 tablespoons olive oil. When sizzling, add 2 pieces of chicken and cook until browned, about 3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
    • Melt 2 more tablespoons butter with 2 more tablespoons olive oil; brown the remaining 2 pieces of chicken the same way. Remove to the plate.
  3. Add the lemon juice, stock, and capers to the pan. Return to the stove and bring to a boil, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom.
  4. Remove the chicken to a platter. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons butter to the sauce and whisk vigorously. Pour the sauce over the chicken and garnish with parsley.

Chicken with 40 Cloves of Garlic and Garlic Bread

Serves 4

Source: Adapted from "France the Beautiful Cookbook," Collins, San Francisco, 1989

Ingredients

Chicken stuffing

  • 1 (3 1/2-pound) chicken
  • Kosher salt to taste
  • 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 2 sprigs fresh rosemary
  • 2 sprigs fresh sage
  • 2 tender stalks celery with their leaves
  • 2 sprigs Italian parsley

Pot

  • 40 cloves garlic, unpeeled
  • 3 tablespoons olive oil
  • Freshly ground pepper to taste

To serve

  • Toasted slices of country bread

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Sprinkle chicken inside and out with kosher salt. Stuff with half the thyme, rosemary, sage, and celery; add the parsley and 4 cloves of garlic.
  2. Place remaining herbs and celery in an oval earthenware or enameled pot just large enough to hold the chicken. Add oil, salt, pepper, and remaining garlic. Roll chicken in oil to coat.
  3. Cover pot and bake for 1 3/4 hours.
  4. Transfer chicken to serving platter and surround with the garlic cloves. Skim fat from cooking juices and pour into a sauceboat.
  5. Serve with toasted bread; each diner crushes a garlic clove to remove skin and spreads the puree on a slice.

Marry Me Chicken

4 | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 50 minutes | Total: 1 hour

To make slicing into cutlets easier, freeze the chicken breasts for 20 minutes first.
Great served over pasta, rice, or polenta, or with crusty bread and a green salad.

Source: NYT Cooking, by Naz Deravian

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 3 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts, or 6 chicken cutlets (about 2 1/4 pounds total), patted dry
  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • 1/4 cup all-purpose flour

Oil and butter

  • 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed
  • 3 tablespoons unsalted butter

Sauce

  • 3 garlic cloves, chopped
  • 1 tablespoon tomato paste
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, to taste
  • 1 cup low-sodium chicken stock
  • 1/2 to 3/4 cup heavy cream
  • 1/2 cup (1 1/2 ounces) grated Parmesan
  • 1/3 cup sliced sun-dried tomatoes, packed in oil

To finish

  • Fresh basil

Steps

  1. If using chicken breasts, slice each in half horizontally starting from the thickest end, to make 6 cutlets total. Season generously with salt and pepper.
  2. Scatter the flour on a large plate and coat the cutlets, shaking off the excess. Transfer to a sheet pan or large plate and let rest 10 minutes.
  3. Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, reduce the heat to medium and add the butter. As soon as it melts, add the cutlets and sear until golden, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
  4. Reduce the heat to low, add the garlic, and cook, stirring often, until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the tomato paste, oregano, and Aleppo pepper; stir to combine.
  5. Increase the heat to medium, add the stock, and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits, until the liquid is reduced by half, about 3 minutes.
  6. Add 1/2 cup of the cream and warm through, stirring, until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Stir in the Parmesan and sun-dried tomatoes. Taste; add more cream if desired.
  7. Place the chicken back in the pan to warm through, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and scatter basil on top.

French

Coq au Vin

Serves 6

Grandmother Brenda noted on the card that the red wine "costs about 29¢ at Muehlebach Grocery" (in Kansas City).

Source: From Grandmother Brenda's collection

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 3 tablespoons butter or margarine
  • 3 tablespoons salad oil
  • 3 chicken breasts, halved
  • 3 drumsticks and 3 thighs
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/8 teaspoon pepper
  • 1/4 cup cognac

Braised onions and mushrooms

  • 12 pearl onions, peeled
  • 1/2 lb mushrooms, whole or halved
  • 2 tablespoons butter

Braising liquid

  • 1 1/2 cups red wine (Burgundy or Bordeaux)
  • 2 chicken bouillon cubes dissolved in 2 cups water
  • 2 tablespoons tomato paste
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 1/4 teaspoon thyme
  • 1 bay leaf

Beurre manie

  • 1 tablespoon softened butter
  • 1 tablespoon flour, kneaded together with the butter

To serve

  • Fresh parsley sprigs

Steps

  1. Brown chicken in hot oil and butter over medium heat at approximately 350 degrees. Cover and cook slowly 10 minutes, turning chicken once. Season with salt and pepper.
  2. Meanwhile, in a separate skillet, saute pearl onions and mushrooms in butter until golden. Set aside.
  3. Pour cognac over browned chicken and ignite.
  4. Add wine, bouillon, tomato paste, garlic, thyme, and bay leaf to the chicken. Add the braised onions and mushrooms. Cover and simmer at approximately 150 degrees for 25-35 minutes until juices run clear.
  5. Remove chicken and vegetables to a side dish.
  6. Turn heat to high and boil sauce rapidly, reducing liquid to about 2 1/2 cups. Add beurre manie in small pieces, whisking; bring to simmer and cook 1-2 minutes until sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
  7. Return chicken to skillet, baste with sauce. Decorate with parsley sprigs and serve.

Central/Eastern European

Chicken Kiev

2 | Prep: 30 minutes | Cook: 30 minutes | Total: 1 hour, plus 1 hour freezing

Source: RecipeTin Eats, by Nagi Maehashi

Ingredients

Garlic butter

  • 6 tablespoons (90g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 teaspoons parsley, finely chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves, very finely minced
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt (skip if using salted butter)

Chicken

  • 2 (7 to 8 ounce) chicken breasts, skinless and boneless
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon pepper

Crumbing

  • 1 egg, lightly whisked
  • 1/4 cup flour
  • 1 cup panko breadcrumbs

Frying oil

  • Oil for frying (canola or vegetable, about 4 cups)

To finish

  • Parsley, finely chopped

Steps

  1. Make the garlic butter: mix the butter, parsley, garlic, and salt until combined.
  2. Shape and chill: scrape the butter onto parchment paper and shape into a 4x2.4-inch rectangle. Refrigerate until firm, then cut in half lengthwise to make 2 batons.
  3. Pound the chicken: place each breast smooth-side down between two sheets of plastic. Pound to an even 1/2-inch thickness.
  4. Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
  5. Stuff and roll: place a butter baton in the center of each breast. Fold the sides in, then roll up from the bottom, finishing seam-side down. Press firmly to seal.
  6. Wrap and partially freeze: wrap tightly in cling wrap, twisting the ends. Freeze 30 minutes, until fairly firm but not solid.
  7. Crumb: set up the egg, flour, and breadcrumbs in separate bowls. Coat the chicken in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing to adhere.
  8. Freeze again 30 minutes, until firm to handle.
  9. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Set a rack on a baking tray.
  10. Fry the chicken in oil heated to 375°F, turning once or twice, until golden, 2 to 3 minutes (it will still be raw inside).
  11. Bake on the rack 15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 149°F — pierce carefully so you don't release the butter.
  12. Rest 2 minutes, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

Chicken Paprikash

4 to 6 | Cook: 1 hour | Total: 1 hour

Use fresh Hungarian paprika if you can find it — it loses flavor quickly (within a few months) and turns dull and bitter with age.

Source: NYT Cooking, by Sam Sifton

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 3 to 4 pounds chicken thighs and drumsticks, or whole chicken legs
  • Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
  • 1 tablespoon neutral oil, like canola
  • 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, divided

Roux

  • 1 large yellow or Spanish onion, diced
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 3 tablespoons Hungarian paprika, sweet or hot
  • 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour

Braise

  • 1 cup canned crushed tomatoes or 1 large ripe tomato, chopped
  • 1 cup chicken broth

Noodles

  • 1 pound egg noodles

To finish

  • 3/4 cup sour cream

Steps

  1. Heat the oven to 400°F. Season the chicken aggressively with salt and pepper. Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large Dutch oven over high heat until the butter is melted and foamy. Sear the chicken until golden brown on both sides; remove to a plate.
  2. Pour off all but 3 tablespoons of the accumulated fat in the pot. Return to medium heat and add the onion. Cook, stirring often, until soft and beginning to brown, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika, and remaining 2 tablespoons butter; cook, stirring, 1 minute. Add the flour and stir to combine.
  3. Add the tomatoes and broth, whisking until smooth. Nestle the chicken back into the pan, skin-side up. Slide into the oven and bake, uncovered, 30 minutes.
  4. Meanwhile, bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil. Cook the noodles until almost completely tender, 7 to 8 minutes. Drain.
  5. Place the chicken on top of the noodles. Stir the sour cream into the sauce and ladle it over everything.

Mediterranean/Greek

Chicken-Zucchini Meatballs With Feta

4 | Total: 45 minutes

Made here with ground chicken; ground turkey can be substituted.
Sauce is Panning the Globe's lemony yogurt-sumac sauce, with the NYT recipe's quick-pickled shallot, feta, and remaining garnishes.

Source: Meatballs from NYT Cooking (Ali Slagle); sauce adapted from Ottolenghi's Turkey Zucchini Meatballs with Lemony Yogurt

Ingredients

Yogurt-Feta Sauce

  • 1/2 cup sour cream
  • 2/3 cup plain Greek yogurt
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 1 small garlic clove, pressed or finely minced
  • 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon sumac
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 4 ounces feta, crumbled
  • 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes

Quick-Pickled Shallot

  • Remaining shallot half (see Meatballs), coarsely chopped
  • 3 tablespoons lemon juice (from 1 large lemon)
  • Pinch of kosher salt

Zucchini

  • 2 of 3 large zucchini (about 1 pound total), cut into 1/2-inch-thick slices
  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • About 1 tablespoon olive oil

Meatballs

  • 1 large shallot, halved (grate one half here; quick-pickle the other half for the sauce)
  • 1 remaining large zucchini, grated
  • 1/2 cup panko
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cumin
  • 1/2 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1 pound ground chicken (turkey can be substituted)
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint, basil, parsley, or dill, plus more for serving
  • Extra-virgin olive oil, for greasing the pan and drizzling

Steps

  1. Quick-pickled shallot: Coarsely chop half the shallot (reserve the other half for the meatballs) and combine with the 3 tablespoons lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Let sit while you make the rest.
  2. Yogurt-feta sauce: Combine the sour cream, yogurt, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, garlic, 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, sumac, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Fold in half the feta. Spread on a platter. Top with the remaining feta, 1/4 cup olive oil, and the Aleppo pepper.
  3. Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut 2 of the zucchini into 1/2-inch-thick slices; transfer to a plate, season with salt, and set aside.
  4. Meatballs: Working over a large bowl, grate the remaining zucchini on the large holes of a box grater. Grate the remaining shallot half; add to the bowl. Add the panko, cumin, Aleppo pepper, and salt; mix. Add the ground chicken and herbs; mix until just combined.
  5. Lightly grease a baking sheet. With wet hands, form the mixture into 16 meatballs (about 2 to 3 tablespoons each) and arrange on one half of the sheet. Drizzle with olive oil. Bake 10 minutes.
  6. Meanwhile, pat the sliced zucchini dry and lightly coat with about 1 tablespoon olive oil; season with pepper.
  7. Add the sliced zucchini to the other half of the baking sheet, moving the meatballs over if needed. Bake until the meatballs are cooked through and the zucchini is golden, about 10 minutes more.
  8. Serve the meatballs and zucchini with a drizzle of the yogurt-feta sauce and more fresh herbs.

Greek Chicken and Orzo Pasta Salad

8 | Prep: 30 minutes | Total: 1 hour 15 minutes (includes marinating and cooling)

Source: Food Network, by Katie Lee Biegel, from The Kitchen

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 3 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • Juice of 1 lemon
  • 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken tenderloins

Breadcrumbs

  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs
  • Pinch of kosher salt

Dressing

  • 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1/4 cup red wine vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • 1 clove garlic, grated
  • Juice of 1/2 lemon

Salad

  • Kosher salt, for the pasta water
  • 1 pound orzo
  • 10 ounces grape tomatoes, halved
  • 1 English cucumber, diced
  • 1/4 cup minced fresh flat-leaf parsley
  • 1 1/2 cups crumbled feta cheese (from a block, not packaged crumbled cheese)

Steps

  1. Chicken marinade: In a medium bowl, whisk together the olive oil, salt, oregano, garlic powder, pepper, and lemon juice. Add the chicken tenderloins and toss to coat. Marinate at room temperature 30 minutes.
  2. Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high.
  3. Remove the chicken from the marinade and grill until cooked through, about 5 minutes per side. Slice into 1-inch-wide pieces.
  4. Breadcrumbs:
    • Preheat the oven to 400°F.
    • In a medium ovenproof skillet, heat the butter, olive oil, and garlic over low heat until the garlic begins to sizzle. Add the panko and salt; stir to coat.
    • Transfer to the oven and toast until golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes.
  5. Dressing: Whisk together the olive oil, vinegar, salt, oregano, pepper, garlic, and lemon juice in a small bowl until combined.
  6. Cook the orzo: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the orzo and cook until al dente, 7 to 8 minutes. Drain and transfer to a large bowl; toss immediately with the dressing. Let cool.
  7. When cool, stir in the tomatoes, cucumber, and parsley. Top with the feta, sliced chicken, and breadcrumbs.

Mediterranean Grilled Chicken Thighs with Dill Yogurt Sauce

8 | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 12 minutes | Total: 22 minutes, plus marinating

Source: The Mediterranean Dish, by Suzy Karadsheh

Ingredients

Dill yogurt sauce

  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 1 cup fresh dill, stems removed, chopped
  • 1 1/4 cups Greek yogurt
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1/2 lemon or lime, juiced
  • Pinch cayenne pepper, optional
  • Kosher salt, if needed

Seasoning

  • 10 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1/2 teaspoon paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon allspice
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground green cardamom
  • Salt and pepper
  • 3 tablespoons olive oil

Chicken and marinade

  • 8 boneless, skinless chicken thighs
  • 1 red onion, halved and thinly sliced
  • 2 lemons, juiced
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil

Steps

  1. Make the dill yogurt sauce: combine the garlic, dill, yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, and cayenne in a food processor; blend until smooth. Season with salt if needed. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
  2. Make the seasoning: mix the garlic, paprika, allspice, nutmeg, cardamom, and 3 tablespoons olive oil. Pat the chicken dry and rub with the seasoning on all sides.
  3. Make the marinade: in a large dish, add the onion, lemon juice, and remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil. Place the chicken in the marinade and turn to coat.
  4. If time allows, cover and refrigerate 2 to 4 hours (or overnight, adding the lemon juice only in the final 1 to 2 hours). Otherwise, proceed.
  5. Heat a gas grill to medium-high. Grill the chicken, covered, 5 minutes, then turn and grill covered another 3 to 5 minutes, until cooked through.
  6. Rest the chicken about 5 minutes before serving; internal temperature should reach 165°F.
  7. Serve with the dill yogurt sauce.

One-Pot Chicken and Rice With Caramelized Lemon

4 | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 45 minutes | Total: 55 minutes

Source: NYT Cooking, by Dan Pelosi

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 1 1/2 pounds)
  • Salt and black pepper
  • 2 teaspoons dried oregano, divided
  • Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, to taste

For browning

  • 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

Lemon

  • 2 lemons

Rice

  • 1 cup pitted Castelvetrano or kalamata olives, smashed and roughly chopped
  • 6 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 medium shallot or 1/2 medium onion, minced
  • 2 cups Jasmine or Basmati rice, rinsed
  • 4 cups (32 ounces) chicken broth

To serve

  • 1/4 cup roughly chopped fresh parsley

Steps

  1. Heat the oven to 400°F. Pat the chicken thighs dry. Season with 1 teaspoon each salt, pepper, and dried oregano, plus a pinch of Aleppo pepper.
  2. Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or other heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add the chicken skin side down and cook until deeply golden, about 5 minutes. Flip and cook 2 minutes more. Transfer to a plate.
  3. Cut 1 lemon into 1/4-inch-thick slices. Add to the pot and cook until caramelized and softened, about 2 minutes. Remove and set aside.
  4. Add the olives, garlic, shallot, and the remaining 1 teaspoon each salt, pepper, and oregano to the pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add the rice and stir to coat. Add the broth and bring to a simmer.
  5. Remove the pot from the heat. Place the browned chicken thighs on top of the rice, skin side up, then cover with the caramelized lemon slices. Cover tightly with a lid or foil and bake until the rice is cooked and the chicken is cooked through, about 30 minutes.
  6. Serve topped with the parsley and a squeeze of juice from the remaining lemon.

Roast Lemon-Garlic Chicken with Green Olives

4

The lemon-herb mixture can be made up to 4 hours ahead, covered, and kept at room temperature.
Can double the recipe; or use half black olives for a contrast of color.

Source: Seriously Simple (cookbook)

Ingredients

Lemon-herb mixture

  • 1 tablespoon finely chopped lemon zest
  • 1/3 cup fresh lemon juice
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1/4 cup finely chopped mixed fresh herbs (such as rosemary, thyme, parsley, basil, and/or oregano)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

For roasting

  • 1 (3 1/2-pound) fryer chicken, cut up
  • 25 garlic cloves, peeled

For the pan sauce

  • 3/4 cup chicken broth
  • 1/3 cup pitted French green olives, rinsed
  • 2 tablespoons finely chopped mixed fresh herbs (for garnish)

Steps

  1. Lemon-herb mixture: In a small bowl, combine the lemon zest and juice, olive oil, 1/4 cup of the herbs, and salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
  2. Preheat oven to 425°F. Arrange chicken pieces in a roasting pan and pour the lemon-herb mixture over. Arrange the garlic cloves all around the chicken, stirring them to coat with the mixture. Roast about 40 minutes, or until chicken is nicely browned and opaque throughout.
  3. Remove chicken from oven. Add broth to the pan and place over medium-high heat on the stovetop. Stir to scrape up browned bits from the bottom. Add olives and stir; cook a few minutes to heat through. Garnish with the remaining 2 tablespoons herbs and serve from the pan, or transfer to a platter. Serve immediately.

Moroccan/North African

Chicken Tagine With Olives and Preserved Lemons

4 | Total: 1 hour, plus marinating

Source: NYT Cooking, from Shallots New York, adapted by Florence Fabricant

Ingredients

Spice rub

  • 5 cloves garlic, finely chopped
  • 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, pulverized
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1 teaspoon sweet paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Chicken

  • 1 chicken, cut in 8 to 10 pieces

Braise

  • 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
  • 3 medium onions, sliced thin
  • 1 cinnamon stick

To finish

  • 8 kalamata olives, pitted and halved
  • 8 cracked green olives, pitted and halved
  • 1 large or 3 small preserved lemons
  • 1 cup chicken stock
  • Juice of 1/2 lemon
  • 1 tablespoon chopped flat-leaf parsley

Steps

  1. Spice rub:
    • Mix the garlic, saffron, ginger, paprika, cumin, and turmeric together.
    • If not using kosher chicken, add 1/2 teaspoon salt; add pepper to taste.
    • Rub the chicken with the mixture, cover, refrigerate, and marinate 3 to 4 hours.
  2. Heat the oil in a heavy skillet. Add the chicken and brown on all sides; remove to a platter. Add the onions to the skillet and cook until soft. Add the cinnamon stick.
  3. To finish:
    • Put the chicken on top of the onions and scatter with the olives.
    • Quarter the preserved lemons, remove the pulp, and cut the skin into strips; scatter over the chicken.
    • Mix the stock and lemon juice and pour over the chicken.
    • Cover the tagine or skillet, place over low heat, and cook about 30 minutes, until the chicken is done. Scatter the parsley on top and serve.

Sheet-Pan Chicken With Chickpeas, Cumin and Turmeric

4 | Total: 1 hour, plus marinating

Source: NYT Cooking, by Alison Roman

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 1 (3 1/2 to 4 pound) chicken, cut into parts (or 3 to 3 1/2 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken parts)
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper

Yogurt marinade

  • 3/4 cup full-fat Greek yogurt
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
  • 2 tablespoons water

Chickpeas

  • 2 (15-ounce) cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  • 1 tablespoon fennel seed
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
  • 1 large red onion, thinly sliced, divided
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil

Lemony onions

  • 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

Yogurt sauce

  • 3/4 cup full-fat Greek yogurt
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

To finish

  • 1/2 cup mint or cilantro leaves, torn

Steps

  1. Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
  2. Make the marinade: combine the yogurt, lemon juice, turmeric, and water in a bowl; season well with salt and pepper. Add the chicken, turning to coat. Marinate at least 1 hour (up to overnight) in the fridge.
  3. Heat the oven to 425°F, rack in the top third.
  4. Combine the chickpeas, fennel seed, cumin, turmeric, and half the onion on a rimmed baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
  5. Move the chickpeas to the edges of the sheet; scrape excess marinade off the chicken and place it in the center. Bake, tossing the chickpeas once, until the chicken is golden and cooked through and the chickpeas are crispy, 40 to 45 minutes.
  6. Meanwhile, toss the remaining onion with the lemon juice, salt, and pepper; set aside.
  7. Combine the remaining yogurt with the remaining lemon juice, salt, and pepper; set aside as the sauce.
  8. Scatter the chicken with the lemony onions and mint or cilantro. Serve with the yogurt sauce alongside.

West African

Chicken Yassa

4 | Total: 1 hour, plus marinating

Source: NYT Cooking, recipe from Pierre Thiam, adapted by Alexa Weibel

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken legs (2 1/2 to 3 pounds)
  • 4 scallions, trimmed, whites and greens finely chopped
  • 2 tablespoons fresh thyme, finely chopped (or 2 teaspoons dried)
  • 1 tablespoon white vinegar or apple cider vinegar
  • 1/4 cup lime juice
  • 1 tablespoon peanut, vegetable, or canola oil

Oil and seasoning

  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon oil

Onions

  • 3 tablespoons oil
  • 2 pounds yellow onions, halved and sliced 1/2-inch thick
  • Kosher salt and black pepper

Aromatics

  • 1 green bell pepper, halved, seeded, and cut into thin matchsticks
  • 1 whole Scotch bonnet chile, poked with a fork (or 1 whole habanero, 1 to 2 minced jalapeños, or 1/2 to 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes)
  • 4 garlic cloves, finely chopped
  • 4 teaspoons finely chopped fresh ginger
  • 3 fresh or dried bay leaves
  • 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard, optional
  • 1/4 cup lime juice
  • Kosher salt and black pepper

To finish

  • 1 cup water
  • Cooked rice or fonio, for serving

Steps

  1. Combine the chicken legs with the scallions, thyme, vinegar, 1/4 cup lime juice, and 1 tablespoon oil in a large bowl. Marinate at least 1 hour (up to overnight) in the fridge. Remove the chicken; reserve the marinade.
  2. Heat a grill, grill pan, or cast-iron skillet with 1 tablespoon oil over medium-high (if cooking indoors, pat the chicken dry first). Season with salt and pepper and grill until charred, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
  3. Meanwhile, heat the remaining 3 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium-high. Add the onions in an even layer, season with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to brown, 15 to 20 minutes.
  4. Add the bell pepper, chile, garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and mustard (if using). Continue stirring, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons of water if needed to prevent sticking. Add the 1/4 cup lime juice and the reserved marinade; cook 2 minutes.
  5. Add the grilled chicken to the pot, tucking it under the onions, then top with 1 cup water. Stir well, smooth into an even layer, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the chicken is very tender, about 20 minutes.
  6. Season to taste, adding more lime juice if desired. Serve over rice or fonio, with the onion mixture and sauce drizzled over.

Middle Eastern/Persian

Grilled Chicken Skewers with Toum (Shish Taouk)

4

Toum uses raw egg white in an emulsified sauce, as in the original recipe.

Source: Bon Appétit, by Kamal Mouzawak

Ingredients

Toum

  • 6 garlic cloves
  • 2 large egg whites
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
  • 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil
  • Salt

Marinade

  • 3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
  • 2 tablespoons tomato paste
  • 1 tablespoon ground coriander
  • 1/4 cup toum (reserved from above)
  • 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for the grill

Chicken

  • 1 1/4 pounds skinless, boneless chicken thighs
  • Salt

To serve

  • 4 pitas, warmed
  • Pickles

Steps

  1. Make the toum: pulse the garlic, egg whites, and lemon juice in a food processor until smooth. With the motor running, very slowly drizzle in the oil until fully emulsified. Season with salt. Reserve 1/4 cup for the marinade; refrigerate the rest.
  2. Make the marinade: mix the lemon juice, tomato paste, coriander, 1/4 cup of the toum, and the oil in a large bowl. Transfer to a zip-lock bag.
  3. Slice the chicken thighs in half lengthwise and season generously with salt. Add to the bag with the marinade, seal, and massage to coat. Marinate overnight in the fridge.
  4. Let the chicken sit at room temperature 1 hour before grilling.
  5. Prepare a grill for medium heat; oil the grate. Thread the chicken onto skewers, folding pieces accordion-style so they stay flat. Grill, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 12 to 15 minutes.
  6. Serve the chicken on warmed pitas, with pickles and the reserved toum alongside.

Spiced Green Meatballs with Pickle Rice and Salty Yogurt

4 | Prep: 55 minutes | Total: 1 hour 15 minutes

Made here with ground chicken; ground turkey, pork, lamb, or beef can be substituted.

Source: The Club, by Molly Baz

Ingredients

Cucumber Pickle Salsa

  • 1/2 cup finely chopped mixed tender herbs (cilantro, dill, parsley, and/or mint) — from 1 1/2 cups total chopped; reserve the other 1 cup for the meatballs
  • 1 English cucumber, diced into 1/2-inch cubes
  • 8 baby dill pickles, diced into 1/2-inch cubes
  • 2 scallions, thinly sliced (from 4 total; reserve the other 2 for the meatballs)
  • 1 garlic clove, grated
  • 1/2 cup olive oil
  • 3 tablespoons pickle brine
  • 3/4 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste

Rice

  • 2 cups Jasmine or Basmati rice
  • 2 1/2 cups cold water
  • 2 teaspoons kosher salt

Meatballs

  • 1 tablespoon coriander seeds (or 2 teaspoons ground coriander), coarsely chopped
  • 1 tablespoon fennel seeds, coarsely chopped
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 cup panko
  • 3/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons kosher salt
  • 3/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • 1 1/2 pounds ground chicken
  • 1 cup reserved chopped herbs (from the salsa prep above)
  • 2 reserved chopped scallions (from the salsa prep above)
  • Oil, for greasing the baking sheet

To serve

  • 1 cup whole milk yogurt
  • Kosher salt, to season the yogurt
  • Olive oil, for drizzling

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 450°F.
  2. Cucumber Pickle Salsa:
    • Finely chop enough herbs to yield about 1 1/2 cups chopped (lightly packed); measure out 1/2 cup for the salsa and set the other 1 cup aside for the meatballs.
    • Dice the cucumber and pickles into 1/2-inch cubes.
    • Thinly slice the scallions, setting aside 2 for the meatballs.
    • In a medium bowl, combine the 1/2 cup chopped herbs, diced cucumber and pickles, 2 sliced scallions, grated garlic, olive oil, pickle brine, Aleppo pepper, and salt.
    • Stir, taste, and adjust with more salt or pickle brine as needed.
    • Refrigerate until ready to serve.
  3. Rice:
    • Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer under cold running water until the water runs clear; drain well.
    • Combine the rice, cold water, and salt in a medium saucepan with a tight-fitting lid.
    • Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then cover, reduce the heat to very low, and cook 16 minutes.
    • Turn off the heat and let steam, covered, at least 10 minutes.
    • Fluff with a fork and keep covered until ready to serve.
  4. Meatballs:
    • Coarsely chop the coriander and fennel seeds (or use a mortar and pestle).
    • In a large bowl, lightly beat the eggs with the olive oil.
