Expertly Spiced and Glazed Roast Turkey

Serves 8–10 | Active: 45 min | Total: About 2 hrs (plus 24–48 hrs dry-brining)

Turkey is spatchcocked for more even roasting. Begin 24–48 hours ahead for the dry brine.
Option: after removing the backbone, also separate the wings and legs for even faster, more even cooking as individual pieces — see Step 1.
Requires a spice mill or mortar and pestle.

Source: https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/expertly-spiced-and-glazed-roast-turkey

Ingredients

Spice rub

  • 2 Tbsp whole black peppercorns
  • 2 Tbsp whole pink or black peppercorns
  • 1/2 cup Diamond Crystal or 1/4 cup plus 1 1/2 tsp Morton kosher salt
  • 2 Tbsp garlic powder
  • 2 Tbsp onion powder
  • 1 Tbsp smoked paprika
  • 1 Tbsp light brown sugar

Turkey

  • 1 (12-14 lb.) turkey, neck and giblets removed

Glaze

  • Small handful hardy herbs (sage, rosemary, bay leaves, and/or thyme)
  • 4 garlic cloves, crushed
  • 2 (2x1") strips orange zest
  • 1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1/3 cup sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
  • 1/3 cup (packed) light brown sugar

For roasting

  • 6 Tbsp neutral oil (vegetable, peanut, or canola)
  • 1 cup water, plus more as needed

Steps

  1. Spatchcock the turkey (preferred method):
    • Place turkey breast side down. Using kitchen shears, cut along one side of the backbone all the way through, then cut along the other side to remove the backbone entirely. Save for stock.
    • Flip turkey breast side up. Press firmly on the breastbone with the heel of your hand until it cracks and the bird lies flat.
    • Option — full breakdown: after removing the backbone, also separate the wings (grip each wing, pull outward, cut through the joint) and the legs (cut through skin, pull back until ball joint pops out, cut through joint). You'll have 5 separate pieces: 2 wings, 2 legs, 1 breast.
  2. Make the spice rub: Finely grind both peppercorns in a spice mill or mortar and pestle. Transfer to a bowl and mix in kosher salt, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and 1 Tbsp brown sugar.
  3. Place turkey on a wire rack set inside a rimmed baking sheet. Sprinkle spice rub liberally all over, patting to adhere (you may not use all of it). Refrigerate uncovered at least 24 hours and up to 2 days.
  4. Remove turkey from rack; rinse baking sheet and rack if needed. Line baking sheet with 3 layers of foil, set rack back inside, and return turkey skin side up. Let sit at room temperature 2–3 hours.
  5. Meanwhile, make the glaze: Cook herbs, garlic, orange zest, soy sauce, vinegar, and 1/3 cup brown sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sugar dissolves and glaze thickens slightly (barely coats a spoon), 10–12 minutes. Remove from heat.
  6. Place a rack in the middle of the oven; preheat to 425°F. Rub turkey all over with oil and pour 1 cup water into the baking sheet. Roast, rotating baking sheet halfway through, until skin is mostly golden brown, 20–25 minutes.
  7. Reduce oven to 300°F. Continue roasting, brushing with glaze every 20 minutes and adding more water by 1/2-cupfuls as needed to keep some liquid in the pan, until an instant-read thermometer reads 150°F in the thickest part of the breast and 170°F in the thickest part of the thigh, 50–70 minutes more (total time 1–1 1/2 hours; fully broken-down pieces may finish faster). Skin should be deep golden brown and shiny.
  8. Transfer to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 30–60 minutes before carving.

★ Turkey and Quinoa Meatloaf

Serves 4 | Total: 1 hr 10 min

Best served with Joan's on Third Chili Aioli.

Source: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/213211/turkey-and-quinoa-meatloaf/

Ingredients

Quinoa

  • 1/4 cup quinoa
  • 1/2 cup water

Aromatics

  • 1 tsp olive oil
  • 1 small onion, chopped
  • 1 clove garlic, chopped

Meatloaf

  • 1 (20 oz) package ground turkey
  • 1 Tbsp tomato paste
  • 1 Tbsp hot pepper sauce
  • 2 Tbsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 egg
  • 1 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 tsp black pepper

Glaze

  • 2 Tbsp brown sugar
  • 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 tsp water

Steps

  1. Bring quinoa and 1/2 cup water to a boil in a small saucepan. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until quinoa is tender and water is absorbed, 15–20 minutes. Set aside to cool.
  2. Preheat oven to 350°F.
  3. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion; cook, stirring, until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more. Remove from heat and let cool.
  4. In a large bowl, mix together ground turkey, cooled quinoa, sautéed onion and garlic, tomato paste, hot pepper sauce, Worcestershire sauce, egg, salt, and pepper until well combined. Transfer to a loaf pan.
  5. Spread the glaze evenly over the top of the meatloaf.
  6. Bake until no longer pink in the center and an instant-read thermometer reads at least 160°F, about 50 minutes. Let cool 10 minutes before slicing.

Indian

Turkey Tikka Masala

Serves 6 | Total: 1 1/2 hrs, plus 4 hrs marinating

A great way to use leftover Thanksgiving turkey.
Marinate the turkey for at least 4 hours, or overnight, for best results.

Source: Samin Nosrat, NYT Cooking (November 22, 2016)

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 2 tsp garam masala
  • 2 tsp ground coriander
  • 2 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 Tbsp paprika
  • 4 tsp ground turmeric
  • 1 tsp kosher salt
  • 6 cloves garlic, finely grated
  • 4 tsp finely grated fresh ginger
  • 1 cup whole-milk yogurt
  • 4 cups cooked turkey (about 1 lb), cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces

Masala — first addition

  • 3 Tbsp ghee or neutral-tasting oil
  • 1 large onion, thinly sliced
  • 6 cardamom pods, crushed
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 1 tsp garam masala
  • Pinch kosher salt

Masala — second addition

  • 1 Tbsp ghee or neutral-tasting oil
  • 2 Tbsp finely grated fresh ginger
  • 4 cloves garlic, finely grated
  • 2 serrano peppers, finely chopped

Tomatoes

  • 2 Tbsp tomato paste
  • 1 (28-oz) can whole peeled tomatoes

Cream and seasoning

  • 2 cups heavy cream
  • 3/4 cup coarsely chopped fresh cilantro, plus sprigs for garnish
  • 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste

Finish

  • Juice of 1 small lemon
  • Jasmine or Basmati rice, for serving

Steps

  1. Make the marinade: Stir together garam masala, coriander, cumin, paprika, turmeric, salt, garlic, ginger, and yogurt in a medium bowl. Fold in turkey. Cover and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
  2. Make the masala: Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add 3 Tbsp ghee or oil, then add onion, cardamom, bay leaf, paprika, Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, garam masala, and a pinch of salt. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are brown and tender, 10–15 minutes.
  3. Make space in the center of the pot; add 1 Tbsp ghee or oil. When shimmering, add ginger, garlic, and serrano peppers and sizzle about 10 seconds. Stir into the spiced onions. Stir in tomato paste. Add whole peeled tomatoes with their juices, crushing them with your hands as you add them. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, stirring often, until liquid is almost gone, 8–10 minutes.
  4. Add heavy cream and cilantro. Season with 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt; taste and adjust. Simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, about 40 minutes. Discard bay leaf.
  5. Line a baking sheet with foil; position an oven rack about 6 inches from the broiler; turn on broiler. Lay marinated turkey in a single layer on the foil. Stir any remaining marinade into the sauce. Broil until turkey begins to blacken in spots, 6–8 minutes.
  6. Using a hand blender (or blender), purée the sauce. Add broiled turkey and return to a simmer for 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until just warmed through. Just before serving, stir in lemon juice. Taste and adjust salt.
  7. Serve hot, garnished with cilantro sprigs, alongside Jasmine or Basmati rice. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months.

Pork

General

★ Sloppy Moes

Serves 6 | Active: 20 min | Total: 45 min

Source: Molly Baz, Cook This Book

Ingredients

Prep

  • 2 ears fresh corn
  • 1 lb cherry tomatoes, halved

Ragu

  • 1 lb spicy Italian sausage, casings removed
  • 1 medium yellow onion, chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, chopped
  • 1/4 cup tomato paste
  • 3 Tbsp red wine vinegar
  • 1 Tbsp honey
  • 2 Tbsp sambal oelek
  • 2 sprigs fresh basil
  • 1/3 cup water

Herb salad

  • 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  • 1 cup fresh basil leaves
  • Splash red wine vinegar
  • Drizzle olive oil

For serving

  • 6 brioche hot dog buns
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • Parmigiano-Reggiano, for grating

Steps

  1. Using the large holes of a box grater, grate the corn kernels from the cobs into a bowl.
  2. Heat a large skillet over medium-high. Add sausage and cook, breaking into pieces, until browned, 4–5 min.
  3. Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and cook, stirring, until softened, about 3 min. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 1 min.
  4. Add tomato paste and stir to coat. Cook, stirring, until it begins to stick to the pan, 1–2 min.
  5. Add red wine vinegar, honey, sambal, basil sprigs, water, grated corn, and halved cherry tomatoes. Stir to combine. Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until thickened, about 15 min. Remove basil sprigs.
  6. Meanwhile, toss scallions and basil leaves in a small bowl. Dress with a splash of red wine vinegar and a drizzle of olive oil.
  7. Toast brioche buns in a skillet with butter until golden.
  8. Serve sausage ragu in toasted buns, topped with herb salad. Grate Parmigiano-Reggiano generously over the top.

Latin/South American

Slow Cooker Pork Mole

Serves 8 | Total: 8–10 hours (plus 30 min prep)

Source: Adapted from Muy Bueno (Yvette Marquez-Sharpnack) and Food Network Kitchen

Ingredients

Pork

  • 1 bone-in pork butt (5–6 lbs)
  • Salt and pepper

Dried chiles

  • 4 dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed
  • 3 dried California or New Mexico red chiles, stems and seeds removed

Sauce aromatics

  • 2 corn tortillas, torn into pieces
  • 1/3 cup sesame seeds
  • 1/4 cup raisins
  • 1 medium yellow onion, roughly chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, smashed
  • 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  • 1 tsp ground cumin

Sauce

  • 3 chipotle chiles in adobo
  • 1 Tbsp adobo sauce
  • 1 28-oz can crushed fire-roasted tomatoes
  • 1 cup fresh cilantro
  • 1 cup chicken broth
  • 2 oz Guittard bittersweet chocolate (or other good-quality bittersweet), roughly chopped
  • Salt

For serving

  • Warm corn tortillas
  • Sliced radishes, chopped white onion, fresh cilantro, lime wedges, crumbled queso fresco (optional)

Steps

  1. Season pork butt all over with salt and pepper and place in a slow cooker.
  2. Toast dried ancho and California/NM chiles in a dry cast-iron skillet over medium heat, pressing with a spatula, until fragrant and slightly darkened, about 1 minute per side. Transfer to a bowl, cover with boiling water, and soak 20 minutes. Drain, reserving 1/2 cup soaking liquid.
  3. In the same cast-iron skillet over medium heat, add tortilla pieces, sesame seeds, raisins, onion, and garlic. Toast, stirring frequently, until sesame seeds are golden, raisins are plump, and tortillas are crisp, 4–5 min. Add cinnamon and cumin and stir 30 seconds.
  4. Transfer toasted mixture to a blender. Add soaked chiles, chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, fire-roasted tomatoes, cilantro, chicken broth, chocolate, and reserved chile soaking liquid. Blend until very smooth. Taste and season generously with salt.
  5. Pour sauce over pork in slow cooker. Cook on Low 8–10 hours, until pork is very tender and pulls apart easily.
  6. Using two forks, shred the pork directly in the slow cooker, pulling the meat apart into pieces. Remove and discard the bone. Skim any excess fat from the surface if desired, and stir the shredded pork into the sauce.
  7. Serve with warm tortillas and toppings.

★ Haitian Pork Griot

Serves 6 | Total: 3 hours, plus overnight marinating

Best served with Pikliz.

Source: Patrick Celestin, adapted by Melissa Clark (NYT Cooking)

Ingredients

Marinade + pork

  • 1 small Scotch bonnet or habanero chile
  • 1 medium onion, diced
  • 1 small green bell pepper, diced
  • 1 small red bell pepper, diced
  • 1/4 cup fresh Italian parsley, chopped, plus more for serving
  • 1 Tbsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
  • 1 Tbsp coarsely ground black pepper
  • 6 sprigs fresh thyme, plus more leaves for serving
  • 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped
  • 1/4 cup cane vinegar or cider vinegar
  • Juice of 1 orange
  • Juice of 1 lemon
  • Juice of 1/2 lime
  • 1 Tbsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 3 lbs pork shoulder, not too lean, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks

Finish

  • 2 Tbsp coconut oil (melted) or olive oil, plus more as needed

For serving

  • Cooked rice
  • Pikliz (see recipe)

Steps

  1. Quarter chile and remove seeds and membranes. Finely chop one quarter; leave the rest in whole pieces. Handle carefully, preferably wearing gloves — they are extremely hot.
  2. Combine all marinade ingredients (chiles, onion, bell peppers, parsley, salt, pepper, thyme, garlic, vinegar, citrus juices, Worcestershire) with pork in a large Dutch oven. Toss well. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
  3. The next day, remove from refrigerator 1–3 hours before cooking. Heat oven to 325°F. Place pot over high heat and bring to a simmer; cover and transfer to oven. Cook, stirring occasionally, until meat is very tender, 1 1/2–2 hours.
  4. Using a slotted spoon, remove meat, letting all excess liquid drip back into the pot and removing any vegetable or herb bits. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet. Drizzle with 2 Tbsp oil and salt to taste; toss gently.
  5. Strain braising liquid, discarding solids. Return sauce to pot and simmer over high heat until reduced by half, 25–30 min.
  6. Meanwhile, heat the broiler. Broil meat, tossing occasionally, until evenly browned, 5–10 min — nicely browned in spots but not dried out.
  7. Drizzle meat with additional oil and top with sauce, parsley, and thyme leaves. Serve on rice with pikliz.

Carnitas

Serves 10–12 | Total: 10 hrs 15 min

Source: Nagi Maehashi, RecipeTin Eats

Ingredients

Pork + rub

  • 4 lbs boneless pork shoulder (pork butt), skinless
  • 2 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 tsp black pepper
  • 1 Tbsp dried oregano
  • 2 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 Tbsp olive oil

Slow cooker aromatics

  • 1 medium onion, chopped
  • 1 jalapeño, deseeded and chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 3/4 cup fresh orange juice (from 2 oranges)

To crisp

  • 1 Tbsp vegetable oil

For serving

  • Warm corn or flour tortillas
  • Diced avocado, pico de gallo, grated cheese, sour cream (optional toppings)

Steps

  1. Combine salt, pepper, oregano, cumin, and olive oil to form the rub. Pat pork dry and rub all over. Place fat-side up in slow cooker; top with onion, jalapeño, and garlic. Pour orange juice over.
  2. Cook on Low 10 hours or High 7 hours, until pork is fall-apart tender.
  3. Transfer pork to a cutting board; let cool slightly and shred with two forks. Skim fat from juices. If you have more than 2 cups of juice, simmer on the stove to reduce. Reserve.
  4. Heat 1 Tbsp vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over high heat. Working in batches, spread pork in a single layer and drizzle with some juices. Let the juices evaporate and the bottom brown and crisp, then briefly sear the other side. Repeat for remaining batches.
  5. Serve immediately in warm tortillas with toppings, drizzled with more juices.

Korean-inspired

Crispy Pork Lettuce Wraps With Spicy Cucumbers

Serves 2 | Total: 3 hours (including marinating and roasting)

Source: Alison Roman, Bon Appétit (October 2015)

Ingredients

Pork + rub

  • 1 12-oz piece skin-on pork belly (about 4x3 1/2x1 1/4 inches)
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
  • 2 Tbsp light brown sugar, divided

Braise

  • 4 chiles de árbol
  • 2 star anise pods
  • 2 Tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 1/4 cups water

Spicy cucumber salad

  • 2 Persian or kirby cucumbers, thinly sliced
  • 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  • 1/2 red chile (Fresno or jalapeño), thinly sliced
  • 2 Tbsp unseasoned rice wine vinegar

Gochujang-miso sauce

  • 3 Tbsp gochujang
  • 3 Tbsp white miso

For serving

  • 1 small head lettuce (Little Gem or romaine hearts), torn
  • 1/2 bunch mint
  • 1/2 cup kimchi (optional)

Steps

  1. Diagonally score the fat side of the pork belly, cutting through the fat but stopping at the flesh, about 1/4 inch apart. Season with salt, pepper, and 1 Tbsp brown sugar. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 2 hours or up to 2 days.
  2. Preheat oven to 400°F. Unwrap pork and nestle into the smallest baking dish you have. Add chiles de árbol, star anise, soy sauce, remaining 1 Tbsp brown sugar, and 1 1/4 cups water. Roast until most fat has rendered, meat is tender, and top is browned and crisp, 2–2 1/2 hours.
  3. Meanwhile, toss cucumbers, scallions, red chile, and vinegar in a small bowl. In a separate small bowl, mix gochujang and miso.
  4. Transfer pork to a cutting board and rest 10 min. Pour off pan juices into a measuring glass; skim fat from surface.
  5. Slice pork into 1/2-inch slices and arrange on a platter. Pour pan juices over. Serve with lettuce, cucumber salad, mint, kimchi (if using), and gochujang-miso sauce.
  6. Do ahead: Pork can be cooked 2 days ahead. Cool, cover, and chill. Reheat before serving.

Chinese

Moo Shu Mushrooms

Serves 4 | Total: 45 min

If you can't find dried day lily buds, substitute 4 oz canned sliced bamboo shoots and skip the soaking step.

Source: J. Kenji López-Alt, NYT Cooking (January 28, 2020)

Ingredients

Dried mushrooms and lily buds

  • 1/3 cup dried Chinese wood ear mushrooms (about 10 grams)
  • 1/4 packed cup dried day lily buds (about 15 grams)

Pork marinade

  • 2 oz pork loin or pork sirloin, cut into 1 1/2- to 2-inch slivers
  • 1/2 tsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
  • 1/2 tsp light soy sauce or shoyu
  • 1/2 tsp cornstarch
  • 1/4 tsp white pepper
  • Pinch kosher salt

Stir-fry sauce

  • 2 1/2 tsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
  • 2 1/2 tsp light soy sauce or shoyu
  • 1/2 tsp cornstarch
  • 1/4 tsp white pepper

Stir-fry

  • 4 Tbsp roasted sesame oil, divided
  • 3 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
  • 2 slices fresh ginger
  • 1/2 lb mixed sliced fresh mushrooms (shimeji, shiitake, enoki, oyster or maitake)
  • 2 scallions, thinly sliced on a sharp bias
  • 1/4 tsp MSG (optional)
  • Kosher salt and white pepper, to taste

For serving

  • Mandarin pancakes or warm flour tortillas
  • Hoisin sauce or sweet bean sauce

Steps

  1. Rehydrate dried ingredients: Place wood ear mushrooms and day lily buds in separate bowls. Cover with very hot water and soak until rehydrated, about 15 min. Drain well. Remove tough centers from wood ears, then thinly slice. Cut day lilies into 2-inch pieces.
  2. Prepare pork marinade: Whisk together Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, cornstarch, white pepper, and a pinch of salt. Add pork and stir vigorously for 10 seconds. Set aside 15 min at room temperature.
  3. Make stir-fry sauce: Whisk together remaining Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, cornstarch, and white pepper in a small bowl until no lumps remain.
  4. Cook eggs: Heat wok over high until lightly smoking. Add 2 Tbsp sesame oil, swirl to coat. Pour in beaten eggs and cook without moving 10 seconds. Break up eggs with a spatula until barely set, 30–45 seconds. Transfer to a large bowl.
  5. Wipe out wok, return to high heat until smoking. Add 1 Tbsp oil, swirl. Add 1 ginger slice, let sizzle 5 seconds. Add pork and stir-fry until just cooked through, about 1 min. Discard ginger; transfer pork to bowl with eggs.
  6. Wipe out wok, return to high heat. Add remaining 1 Tbsp oil, swirl. Add remaining ginger slice, sizzle 5 seconds. Add fresh mushrooms and stir-fry until lightly browned, 2–3 min. Add scallions, sliced wood ears, and day lilies; stir-fry until softened, about 30 seconds.
  7. Return pork and eggs to wok. Stir sauce and add to wok with MSG (if using). Stir-fry to combine; season with salt and white pepper. Discard ginger. Serve immediately with Mandarin pancakes and hoisin sauce.

Lamb

Mediterranean/Greek

★ Garlic & Rosemary Grilled Lamb Chops

Serves 4 | Prep: 15 min | Cook: 10 min | Total: 25 min (plus 1 hr to overnight marinating)

Source: Jannese, Delish D'Lites

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 Tbsp fresh rosemary, chopped
  • 1 1/4 tsp kosher salt
  • 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • 1/4 cup olive oil

Chops

  • 2 lbs lamb loin or rib chops, thick cut

Steps

  1. Combine garlic, rosemary, salt, pepper, lemon zest, and olive oil in a measuring cup.
  2. Pour marinade over lamb chops, flipping to coat completely. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
  3. Grill on medium-high heat for 7–10 minutes, until internal temperature reads 135°F.
  4. Transfer to a plate, cover loosely with foil, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

Middle Eastern/Persian

Lula Kebabs

Serves 6 | Prep: 30 min | Cook: 10 min | Total: 40 min

Source: Janelle Leatherwood, The Stuffed Grape Leaf

Ingredients

  • 1 lb ground lamb
  • 1 lb ground beef
  • 1/2 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
  • 1/4 cup fresh mint, finely chopped
  • 1/2 yellow onion, grated or very finely minced
  • 1/2 Tbsp ground cumin
  • 2 tsp allspice
  • 1/2 tsp ground coriander
  • 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  • 2 tsp fresh lemon juice
  • 1 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • 2 Tbsp tomato paste
  • Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

Steps

  1. Combine both ground meats, parsley, mint, onion, cumin, allspice, coriander, garlic powder, lemon juice, olive oil, and tomato paste in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper and mix until evenly combined.
  2. Shape mixture into long, flattened patties and thread onto skewers if desired.
  3. Grill over medium-high heat until cooked through but not dried out, about 10 minutes total, turning once.

Indian

Luscious Tandoori Lamb Chops

Serves 4 | Active: 30 min | Total: ~9 hrs (including overnight marinade)

Source: Suvir Saran, Food & Wine

Ingredients

Chops + marinade (overnight)

  • 8 lamb rib chops (about 2 1/2 lbs)
  • 3/4 cup whole-milk Greek yogurt
  • 1/4 cup heavy cream
  • 3 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
  • 1 (3-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and minced
  • 4 large garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 Tbsp malt vinegar
  • 1 Tbsp garam masala
  • 1 Tbsp ground cumin
  • 1 Tbsp paprika
  • 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper
  • 1/4 tsp ground mace (optional)
  • 1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
  • 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to season

Basting oil

  • 2 Tbsp vegetable oil

Finish

  • 3 Tbsp unsalted butter, melted

Steps

  1. Score one side of each chop with three diagonal slashes, about 1/4 inch deep.
  2. Whisk together yogurt, cream, lemon juice, ginger, garlic, malt vinegar, garam masala, cumin, paprika, cayenne, mace (if using), nutmeg, and salt. Add chops, turn to coat, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
  3. Remove chops from refrigerator. Add oil to marinade, toss with chops, and let stand at room temperature 30 minutes.
  4. Grill over moderately high heat for 8 minutes, turning once. Brush with melted butter and grill 2 more minutes per side for medium-rare. Season with salt and serve.

Beef

General

★ Four Peppercorn Crusted Rotisserie Rib Roast

Serves 4–6

Best served with Horseradish Sauce.

Source: Lauren Muhlheim (family recipe, December 2020)

Ingredients

Peppercorn crust

  • 2 tsp black peppercorns
  • 2 tsp white peppercorns
  • 2 tsp green peppercorns
  • 1 tsp pink peppercorns
  • 1 tsp salt

Roast

  • 1 boneless beef rib roast (3 1/2 to 4 lbs)

Steps

  1. Place peppercorns in a zip-lock bag and crush with a rolling pin until coarsely ground. Stir in salt.
  2. Coat the roast all over with the peppercorn-salt mixture.
  3. Cook on rotisserie: 18–20 min per lb for rare (140°F internal), 25–30 min per lb for medium (160°F), or 35–40 min per lb for well done (170°F).
  4. Remove from rotisserie and slice 1/4 inch thick. Serve with Horseradish Sauce.

The Best Passover Brisket

Serves 12 | Prep: 15 min | Cook: 3 hrs 30 min | Total: 3 hrs 45 min

Source: Phoebe Lapine, Feed Me Phoebe

Ingredients

Brisket

  • One 5-lb brisket
  • 8 garlic cloves, each cut lengthwise into 4 pieces
  • Sea salt and black pepper
  • 1 Tbsp olive oil
  • 1 qt beef stock

Caramelized onions

  • 2 Vidalia or sweet onions, thinly sliced

Sauce

  • 1 cup ketchup
  • 1/4 cup coconut sugar or brown sugar
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1/4 tsp cayenne
  • 1/2 tsp dried thyme or rosemary
  • 2 bay leaves

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 500°F. Trim fat cap to an even 1/4-inch layer. Using a paring knife, make vertical incisions all over the meat and insert a piece of garlic into each. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper. Place in a large braiser, Dutch oven, or rimmed metal baking dish fat-side up and brown in the oven, about 10 minutes per side.
  2. Remove pan from oven and pour in beef stock. (If using Pyrex, let the pan cool a few minutes first to prevent shattering.) Turn oven down to 350°F, cover tightly with a lid or foil, and braise for 1 hour.
  3. While the brisket braises, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low. Add onions and sauté, stirring occasionally, until soft and caramelized, about 30 minutes.
  4. Remove brisket from oven. Whisk ketchup, sugar, paprika, smoked paprika, cayenne, thyme or rosemary, and bay leaves into the pan juices. Arrange caramelized onions on top of the meat. Cover and return to oven for 2–3 more hours. (2 hours for sliceable brisket; 3 hours for falling-apart, pulled-style.)
  5. Transfer brisket to a cutting board and slice against the grain. Return slices to the sauce and serve. Can be made 1–2 days ahead and reheated gently.

Brenda's Brisket

Best made a day ahead — brisket is much easier to slice when cold, and the fat can be skimmed from the surface before reheating.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Grandmother Brenda

Ingredients

Brisket

  • 1 brisket, 3–4 lbs (prefer 4 lbs)

Rub and glaze

  • 2 packages (1.4 oz each) onion soup mix
  • Ketchup, enough to coat both sides generously

Vegetables

  • 2–3 onions, sliced
  • 3–4 carrots, cut into large chunks

Steps

  1. Rub onion soup mix into brisket on both sides. Spread ketchup over both sides.
  2. Place brisket fat-side-up on a large sheet of heavy-duty foil in a roasting pan. Scatter onions and carrots around the meat.
  3. Wrap tightly in foil. Cover pan.
  4. Bake at 300°F for 4–5 hours, until very tender.
  5. For best results: cool completely, then refrigerate overnight. Slice cold (much easier than slicing warm). Skim any solidified fat from the surface. Return sliced meat to the pan, pour the fat-free pan juices over the top, cover, and reheat at 325°F until warmed through.

Cranberry-Chili Brisket

A sweeter, saucier brisket — the cranberry and chili sauce make a rich, fruity gravy. As with all brisket, easier to slice cold and best reheated in its juices.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Grandmother Brenda

Ingredients

Brisket

  • 1 brisket, about 4 lbs

Sauce

  • 1 jar (12 oz) chili sauce
  • 1 can (14 oz) whole berry cranberry sauce
  • 1 package (1.4 oz) onion soup mix

Vegetables

  • 1 onion, sliced
  • 1 bag (12 oz) baby carrots

Steps

  1. Mix chili sauce, cranberry sauce, and onion soup mix together in a bowl.
  2. Place brisket on a large sheet of heavy-duty foil in a roasting pan. Pour sauce mixture over and around brisket.
  3. Lay onion slices on top; scatter carrots around the meat.
  4. Wrap tightly in foil. Bake at 350°F for about 4 hours, until very tender.
  5. Cool, refrigerate, slice cold, skim fat. Reheat covered in juices (see Brenda's Brisket).

★ Sous Vide Beef Back Ribs

Serves 6–8 | Prep: 20 min | Sous vide: 24 hrs | Finish: 10 min | Total: ~24.5 hrs

Season with Steak Seasoning Rub (3× batch) before the sous vide, and serve alongside Cherry Barbecue Sauce.

Source: Sip Bite Go, Two Kooks in the Kitchen, Went Here 8 This (Family hybrid)

Ingredients

Rub

  • Steak Seasoning Rub — 3× batch for 2 racks (see recipe)

Ribs

  • 2 racks beef back ribs (~7–8 lbs total; also sold as beef spare ribs)

Optional dripping glaze

  • ½ cup drippings from the sous vide bags, strained
  • 1 tsp Dijon mustard
  • 2 Tbsp maple syrup or brown sugar
  • 1 tsp cornstarch

To serve

  • Cherry Barbecue Sauce (see recipe), warmed

Steps

  1. Make a 3× batch of the Steak Seasoning Rub. Remove the silver skin membrane from the underside of each rack: slide a knife tip under the tissue at one end of a bone, grab it firmly with a paper towel, and peel the membrane off in one sheet. Pat ribs dry and rub generously all over. Vacuum seal each rack flat in its own bag.
  2. Fill your sous vide container and set the circulator to 150°F. Submerge the sealed bags and cook for 24 hours.
  3. Remove ribs from bags. To make the glaze, reserve ½ cup drippings; otherwise discard. Pat ribs very dry with paper towels — the drier they are, the better the char.
  4. Optional glaze: Strain reserved drippings into a small saucepan. Refrigerate or freeze for 20–30 minutes until fat starts to congeal; skim and discard fat. Add Dijon, maple syrup, and cornstarch; whisk to combine. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer about 5 minutes until thickened and glossy.
  5. Heat grill to high. Grill ribs 2–3 minutes per side until nicely charred. (If using the glaze, brush on both sides before and during grilling.) Slice between the bones and serve with Cherry Barbecue Sauce on the side.

Hearty Beef Stew With Red Onions and Ale

Serves 6 | Total: 3 hours

Tastes even better a day or two later; can be frozen for up to two months. Serve over mashed potatoes, noodles, or polenta.

Source: Melissa Clark, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Beef

  • 2 lbs boneless beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch chunks
  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • 1–2 Tbsp all-purpose flour
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 1 Tbsp olive oil, plus more as needed

Onions

  • 3 medium red onions (2 sliced into half-moons; 1 cut into ½-inch wedges for Step 6)

Aromatics

  • 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
  • 1 Tbsp tomato paste
  • 1 tsp ground coriander
  • ¼ tsp ground allspice

Liquid

  • 2 cups beef or chicken stock (preferably homemade)
  • 1 cup ale or beer (nonalcoholic is fine)
  • 1 cup water
  • 1 rosemary sprig

Vegetables

  • 3 carrots, sliced
  • Red onion wedges (from Step 2 prep)

Finish

  • 1 Tbsp cider vinegar or sherry vinegar, plus more to taste

Garnish

  • Chopped fresh chives
  • Flaky sea salt
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Steps

  1. Season beef all over with salt and pepper. Set aside while you prepare the onions.
  2. Peel onions. Cut 2 of them in half root to stem, then thinly slice crosswise into half-moons. Cut the third onion root to stem into ½-inch wedges; set wedges aside for Step 6.
  3. Dust beef cubes lightly with flour. Heat butter and 1 Tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high. Working in batches (do not crowd the pan), sear beef until dark all over, 5–6 minutes per batch. Transfer to a bowl as they brown. Add more oil and adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.
  4. Stir in sliced onions; raise heat to medium-high if you lowered it. Cook, stirring occasionally, until pale golden and soft, 10–15 minutes. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant and lightly golden at the edges, 2–3 minutes more.
  5. Make a well in the center of the onions. Stir in tomato paste, coriander, and allspice; cook, stirring, until paste is darkened, about 1 minute. Stir in stock, ale, 1 cup water, and rosemary sprig. Return beef and any accumulated juices to the pot; bring to a simmer. Partly cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
  6. Give the beef a stir, then add reserved onion wedges. Simmer 15 minutes, then add carrots. Continue simmering until meat, onions, and carrots are tender, 30–45 minutes more.
  7. If sauce seems thin, use a slotted spoon to transfer meat and vegetables to a platter; cover with foil to keep warm. Discard rosemary. Return pot to stove and simmer until thickened, 5–10 minutes. Stir in vinegar. Taste and adjust salt and vinegar. Spoon sauce over meat; garnish with chives, flaky sea salt, and more black pepper.

French

Dijon and Cognac Beef Stew

Serves 4–6 | Total: about 3 hours

Slow-cooker variation: render salt pork and sear flour-dusted beef in a sauté pan, then transfer to slow cooker with onions, shallots, carrots, mushrooms, and red wine. Deglaze pan with Cognac, then add 1 cup (not 2) stock, Dijon, and 1 Tbsp Pommery mustard; transfer to slow cooker. Cook on low 6–8 hours. Stir in remaining 3 Tbsp Pommery mustard before serving.

Source: Regina Schrambling, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Aromatics

  • 1/4 lb salt pork, diced
  • 1 large onion, finely diced
  • 3 shallots, chopped
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter, plus more as needed

Beef

  • 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
  • 2 Tbsp all-purpose flour
  • Kosher salt and black pepper

Braising liquid

  • 1/2 cup Cognac
  • 2 cups beef stock
  • 1/2 cup Dijon mustard
  • 1 Tbsp Pommery mustard (or other whole-grain Dijon)

Add-ins

  • 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into half-moon slices
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 1/2 lb mushrooms, stemmed, cleaned, and quartered
  • 3 Tbsp Pommery mustard (remaining)
  • 1/4 cup red wine

Steps

  1. Place salt pork in a Dutch oven over low heat and cook until fat is rendered. Remove and discard solids. Raise heat, add onion and shallots, and cook until softened but not browned, 10–15 minutes. Transfer to a bowl with a slotted spoon.
  2. Add 2 Tbsp butter to the pot if needed to augment fat. Dust beef cubes with flour, season with salt and pepper, and shake off excess. Working in batches, brown beef over medium-high until well browned and almost crusty on all sides; transfer to the bowl with onions. Repeat.
  3. Add Cognac to the empty pot and cook, stirring, until the bottom is deglazed. Add stock, Dijon mustard, and 1 Tbsp Pommery mustard; whisk to blend. Return meat and onions to pot. Reduce heat, partly cover, and simmer gently until meat is very tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
  4. Add carrots and continue simmering until tender, about 30 minutes. Meanwhile, heat 2 Tbsp butter in a medium skillet over medium-high and sauté mushrooms until browned.
  5. Stir mushrooms into the stew along with the remaining 3 Tbsp Pommery mustard and red wine. Simmer 5 minutes, taste, and adjust seasoning. Serve hot.

Chinese

★ Asian Braised Short Ribs

Serves 6 | Prep: 30 min | Cook: 6 hrs (slow cooker) | Total: ~6.5 hrs

Source: Williams-Sonoma Kitchen

Ingredients

Short ribs

  • 2 Tbsp whole Chinese five spice (ground in spice grinder)
  • 4 lbs bone-in beef short ribs
  • 2–3 Tbsp olive oil

Aromatics and braising liquid

  • 1 large yellow onion, cut into 1/4-inch slices
  • 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
  • 1/3 cup plum wine
  • 1/3 cup soy sauce
  • 1/3 cup rice vinegar
  • 1/4 cup sesame oil
  • 1 Tbsp chili garlic paste
  • 2 Tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  • Zest of 1 orange, peeled into 1/2-inch strips
  • Juice of 1 orange
  • 1/4 cup sugar dissolved in 3/4 cup boiling water

To serve

  • Steamed rice

Steps

  1. Grind Chinese five spice in a spice grinder. Season short ribs all over with ground five spice; shake off excess.
  2. In a heavy sauté pan over medium-high heat, warm 1 Tbsp olive oil. Working in batches, brown ribs on all sides, 10–12 minutes total, adding more oil as needed. Transfer to a slow cooker.
  3. Add more oil to pan if needed. Reduce heat to medium, add onion and garlic, and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 5 minutes. Add plum wine and stir to deglaze, scraping up browned bits. Increase heat to medium-high and cook until wine is reduced by half, 2–3 minutes. Transfer to slow cooker along with soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, chili garlic paste, ginger, orange zest, orange juice, and sugar mixture. Cover and cook on high for 6 hours.
  4. Skim fat from the surface. Serve ribs and sauce over steamed rice.

American

Nancy's Flank Steak

Steak quantity, thyme amount, and parsley quantity not specified on original card; adjust to taste.

Source: Family recipe, attributed to Grandmother Nancy

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 1-2 lb flank steak
  • Soy sauce (enough to cover and marinate)

Grill

  • Crumbled dried thyme to taste

Sauce

  • 1 cup hearty red wine
  • 1 cube (1/2 cup) butter
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, to taste

Steps

  1. Marinate flank steak for 3 hours in soy sauce.
  2. Pierce steak liberally and sprinkle with crumbled thyme.
  3. Grill over hot coals.
  4. Heat 1 cup hearty red wine in a small saucepan. Melt butter into wine. Add parsley.
  5. Slice steak diagonally and ladle sauce over top.

Ground Beef

General

Taco Night!!

Makes 12 tacos | Active: 35 min | Total: 3½ hrs

Source: Molly Baz, The Club

Ingredients

Aromatics and spice mix

  • 1 large onion, roughly chopped
  • 6 cloves garlic, roughly chopped
  • 1/4 cup fresh ginger, roughly chopped (from a 3- to 4-inch piece; no need to peel)
  • 1 large bunch cilantro, stems thinly sliced, leaves reserved for serving
  • 1 Tbsp ground cinnamon
  • 2 1/2 tsp ground turmeric
  • 2 tsp ground cardamom
  • 1 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, plus more to taste
  • 1/2 tsp ground cloves
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Ragù

  • 2 lbs (80% lean) ground beef
  • 2 Tbsp olive oil, plus more as needed
  • 1 1/2 cups whole milk
  • 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth, plus more as needed
  • One (28-oz) can crushed or chopped tomatoes
  • 1 Tbsp honey
  • Apple cider vinegar, to taste

Fennel-apple slaw

  • 2 Granny Smith apples, thinly sliced into half moons
  • 1 large bulb fennel, preferably with fronds, halved and thinly sliced crosswise
  • 1/3 cup apple cider vinegar
  • 1 Tbsp honey

To serve

  • One (12-count) package hard taco shells
  • Sour cream, for serving

Steps

  1. Roughly chop onion, garlic, and ginger. Thinly slice cilantro stems; reserve leaves for serving. In a small bowl, mix cinnamon, turmeric, cardamom, Aleppo pepper, cloves, and 1 Tbsp salt.
  2. Break ground beef into 4 pieces and shape into rough balls. Season all over with 1 Tbsp plus 1 tsp salt.
  3. Heat a large Dutch oven over high heat for 2 full minutes. Add olive oil, swirl to coat, and add beef. Sear without moving until deeply browned and crusty on the underside, 6–10 minutes. Flip and cook until the second sides are deeply golden and a fond has formed on the bottom, 4–6 minutes more. (Meat will not be cooked through at this point.)
  4. Remove meat to a plate. Add more olive oil if the pot is dry. Reduce heat to medium-high and add onions, garlic, ginger, and cilantro stems. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until translucent and just starting to turn golden, 5–8 minutes.
  5. Return meat and any accumulated juices to the pot. Sprinkle the spice mix over everything and stir, breaking meat into roughly ping-pong–sized balls, until fragrant, 2–3 minutes.
  6. Add milk, chicken broth, tomatoes, and 1 Tbsp honey. Stir, scraping the bottom to release the fond. Bring to a low boil, then partially cover and reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally and adding splashes of broth as needed to maintain a saucy, chili-like consistency, until meat is tender and sauce is reduced, 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours 15 minutes. (Going 2½–3 hours makes the meat even more tender — add more broth as needed.) Remove from heat and season to taste with salt, Aleppo pepper, and a big splash of apple cider vinegar. Keep warm. Do ahead: can be made up to 2 days ahead; rewarm gently on the stovetop.
  7. While the ragù braises, make the slaw: combine sliced apples, fennel, half the reserved cilantro leaves, and fennel fronds (roughly chopped, if you have them) in a large bowl. Dress with 1/3 cup apple cider vinegar and 1 Tbsp honey; toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper. Keep chilled until serving.
  8. Preheat oven to 375°F. Place taco shells on a baking sheet and bake until just warm, 4 minutes.
  9. Fill shells with ragù and a dollop of sour cream. Top with cilantro leaves and fennel-apple slaw. Serve immediately.

Sweet Potato Shepherd's Pie

Serves 6 | Total: ~50 min

For a 9"×13" pan, double the recipe.

Source: Shira Rosenbluth's mother

Ingredients

Sweet potato topping

  • 5–6 sweet potatoes, peeled
  • 1½ tsp salt
  • 2–3 Tbsp mayonnaise
  • Oil, for brushing

Meat filling

  • 1 Tbsp oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 1 lb ground beef
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ½ tsp onion powder
  • ½ tsp paprika
  • ¼ tsp salt
  • ¼ tsp pepper
  • 1 Tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 Tbsp teriyaki sauce
  • 2 Tbsp Marsala wine
  • 2 Tbsp tomato paste
  • ½ cup water
  • 1 cup frozen peas and carrots

Steps

  1. Place sweet potatoes in a pot with water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer until fork tender. Drain, reserving ½ cup of the cooking water. Season with salt, mayonnaise, and 2 Tbsp of the reserved water; mash until smooth. Add more water and salt to taste.
  2. Preheat oven to 400°F.
  3. Heat oil in a large frying pan over medium flame. Add onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add ground beef and sauté until no longer pink.
  4. Add garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt, pepper, soy sauce, and teriyaki sauce; mix well to incorporate. Add Marsala wine, tomato paste, water, peas and carrots; mix well and cook 3 minutes.
  5. Transfer meat mixture to a 9" round pan. Top with mashed sweet potatoes. Using a fork, make a design on the surface. Lightly brush the top with oil. Bake uncovered at 400°F for 25 minutes.

Taco Soup

Serves 4–6

Ground beef or turkey also works well.
Jalapeños and garlic powder can be added with the canned goods for more heat.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Susan Muhlheim

Ingredients

Chicken

  • 1 lb ground chicken
  • 1/4 cup chopped onion
  • Garlic powder to taste

Canned goods

  • 1 (16-oz) can tomatoes with liquid
  • 1 (16-oz) can kidney beans with liquid
  • 1 (17-oz) can corn with liquid
  • 1 (8-oz) can tomato sauce

Seasoning

  • 1 package taco seasoning

To serve (optional)

  • Avocados
  • Grated cheese
  • Sour cream
  • Taco chips
  • Jalapeños

Steps

  1. Brown ground chicken and onion (and garlic powder if using). Drain.
  2. Add all remaining canned goods and taco seasoning. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 10–15 minutes.
  3. Garnish with avocados, grated cheese, sour cream, and taco chips if desired.

Korean-inspired

Korean Beef Bowl

Serves 4 | Active: 20 min | Total: 25 min

Source: Khin's Kitchen, Glebe Kitchen, Chef Savvy (Family hybrid)

Ingredients

Sauce

  • 3 Tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  • 2 Tbsp brown sugar
  • 1 1/2 Tbsp mirin
  • 1 1/2 Tbsp gochujang
  • 2 tsp sesame oil
  • 1/4 tsp black pepper

Creamy gochujang drizzle

  • 3 Tbsp mayonnaise
  • 1 Tbsp sour cream
  • 1–2 tsp gochujang, to taste
  • 1 tsp rice wine vinegar

Beef and aromatics

  • 1 Tbsp vegetable oil
  • 1/2 large sweet onion, finely diced
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
  • 1 1/2 lbs lean ground beef

To serve

  • Steamed white rice
  • 3 green onions, thinly sliced
  • 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
  • Kimchi

Steps

  1. Whisk all sauce ingredients together in a small bowl. Set aside.
  2. Stir together mayo, sour cream, gochujang, and rice wine vinegar until smooth. Refrigerate until serving.
  3. Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Add onion and cook, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, 3–4 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute more.
  4. Add ground beef, breaking into small pieces, and cook until browned and cooked through, 4–5 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
  5. Pour sauce over beef and stir to combine. Simmer 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened.
  6. Spoon over rice. Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds. Drizzle with creamy gochujang sauce. Serve with kimchi on the side.

Fish

General

Dry-Brined Salmon

Serves 4 | Prep: 5 min | Marinate: 8 hrs – 2 days | Cook: 15 min | Total: ~8.5 hrs+

Marinating with Shio Koji — a fermented rice-and-koji paste — acts as a rich dry brine: it firms the flesh, prevents albumin leakage, and makes the skin virtually nonstick and chip-crisp. Even a short 30–45-minute rest improves the fish.
Works with any type of salmon; especially dramatic with leaner coho or sockeye.

Source: J. Kenji López-Alt, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Salmon and marinade

  • 4 (5- to 7-oz) skin-on salmon fillets
  • ¼ cup Shio Koji paste (about 1 Tbsp per fillet)

Cooking oil

  • Neutral oil for cooking

Broiling oil

  • Small amount of neutral oil

To serve

  • Extra-virgin olive oil
  • Lemon wedges

Steps

  1. Smear Shio Koji paste over the flesh side of each fillet. Place fillets flesh-side down in a Pyrex dish. Transfer to the refrigerator (uncovered or loosely covered with foil) and marinate at least 8 hours and up to 2 days. Before cooking, scrape off the Shio Koji and pat fillets very dry with paper towels.
  2. To cook under the broiler, skip to Step 4. To cook on the stovetop, coat each fillet with a thin film of oil on all sides. Heat a skillet large enough to hold the fillets over medium-low for 2 minutes.
  3. Add fillets skin-side down; press down for the first few minutes to keep skin flat and in contact with the pan. Cook, moving fillets occasionally, until skin is brown and crisp, 4–5 minutes total. (If the fillet doesn't release, give it another 15–30 seconds.) Flip and cook until as done as you like: 100–105°F for medium-rare, 130–135°F for well done. Remove from pan and rest 5 minutes, skin-side up. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and a lemon wedge.
  4. To cook under the broiler: adjust a rack 6 inches below the broiler element. Heat broiler to high. Rub a small amount of oil all over each fillet and arrange skin-side up on a rimmed baking sheet.
  5. For medium-rare, broil until skin is brown, crisp, and charred in spots, 4–5 minutes. (For more well done, increase distance to 8 inches and cook 7–8 minutes total.) Rest 5 minutes, skin-side up. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and a lemon wedge.

Baked Lemon Salmon with Creamy Dill Sauce

Serves 4 | Prep: 10 min | Rest: 10 min | Cook: 15 min | Total: 35 min

Source: Jaclyn, Cooking Classy

Ingredients

Salmon

  • 4 (6-oz) salmon fillets
  • 2 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1½ tsp lemon zest
  • 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Creamy dill sauce (make ahead)

  • ⅓ cup fat-free plain Greek yogurt
  • 3 Tbsp full-fat mayonnaise
  • 1 clove garlic, finely minced
  • 1 Tbsp chopped fresh dill
  • 2–3 tsp milk (to reach desired consistency)
  • ½ tsp honey
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Whisk together olive oil, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a small bowl. Grease a 13×9-inch baking dish. Place salmon fillets in the dish, season one side with salt and pepper, flip, drizzle with lemon mixture, and gently rub over the fillets. Season tops with salt and pepper. Let rest at room temperature 10 minutes.
  2. Bake 12–16 minutes, until cooked through (cook time varies with fillet thickness and desired doneness). Serve warm topped with Creamy Dill Sauce.
  3. Make the sauce: In a bowl, mix together Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, garlic, dill, honey, and enough milk to reach desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to serve; let come to room temperature about 20 minutes before serving so it's not ice-cold over warm salmon. Keeps refrigerated for a few days — also makes an excellent vegetable dip.

Sriracha Maple Salmon

Serves 4 | Active: 10 min | Total: 16 min

Source: Ree Drummond, Food Network (The Pioneer Woman)

Ingredients

Fish and vegetables

  • 4 (6-oz) skinless salmon fillets
  • 3 medium zucchinis, cut into 1-inch rounds
  • 3 Tbsp olive oil

Sauce

  • ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce
  • ¼ cup maple syrup
  • 3 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
  • 3 Tbsp rice wine vinegar
  • 2 Tbsp Sriracha
  • 1 tsp cornstarch
  • 4 cloves garlic, grated
  • 3 green onions, sliced — whites and greens separated

To serve

  • Cooked rice

Steps

  1. Turn oven to broil. Position rack in the upper third of the oven.
  2. Arrange salmon fillets flesh-side up on one side of a large baking dish; place zucchini on the other side. Drizzle both with olive oil.
  3. Whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, rice wine vinegar, Sriracha, cornstarch, garlic, and the white parts of the green onions in a small bowl. Pour sauce over salmon and zucchini. Broil 7 minutes. Remove from oven, spoon sauce over salmon, and flip zucchini. Return to broiler and cook until salmon is cooked through and sauce has thickened, 6–7 minutes more.
  4. Spread cooked rice on a large platter. Arrange salmon on top and zucchini alongside. Spoon over remaining sauce from the baking dish. Garnish with the reserved green onion tops. Serve.

Fish and Chips with Malt Vinegar Mayonnaise

Serves 4 | Special equipment: deep-fry thermometer

Key: beer and club soda must be ice-cold. Chill the batter if prepping ahead.
Corn flour (more finely ground than cornmeal) is available at Latin markets, natural-foods stores, and bobsredmill.com.

Source: Adam Evans, Bon Appétit (September 2013)

Ingredients

Malt Vinegar Mayonnaise (up to 1 day ahead)

  • 1 large egg yolk
  • 2 Tbsp malt vinegar, divided
  • 1 cup vegetable oil
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Frying oil

  • Vegetable oil for frying (about 4 cups)

Batter

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more for seasoning
  • ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper, plus more
  • 12 oz (or more) chilled light lager
  • 1 cup chilled club soda
  • 1 Tbsp malt vinegar

Fish and dredging flour

  • 1 cup corn flour or all-purpose flour
  • 1½ lb cod, haddock, or pollack, cut into long 1½"-wide strips

To serve

  • French fries
  • Old Bay seasoning
  • Flaky sea salt (such as Maldon)
  • Chopped fresh dill
  • Lemon wedges

Steps

  1. Make the mayonnaise: Whisk egg yolk and 1 Tbsp malt vinegar in a small bowl. Whisking constantly, very slowly drizzle in vegetable oil — drop by drop at first — until mayonnaise is thickened and smooth. Whisk in remaining 1 Tbsp vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and chill. (Can be made 1 day ahead.)
  2. When ready to fry, fit a large pot with a deep-fry thermometer; pour in oil to measure 3 inches. Heat over medium-high until thermometer registers 375°F.
  3. Meanwhile, whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, 1 tsp salt, and ½ tsp pepper in a large bowl. Whisking constantly, slowly add beer, club soda, and 1 Tbsp vinegar, adding more beer if batter is too thick (it should be the consistency of thin pancake batter).
  4. Place corn flour in a shallow bowl. Season fish with salt and pepper. Working in batches (returning oil to 375°F between batches), dredge fish in corn flour, shaking off excess; dip in batter, letting excess drip back into bowl; and fry until golden brown and crisp, about 2 minutes per side. Transfer to a paper towel–lined baking sheet.
  5. Season fish and fries with Old Bay, flaky sea salt, and dill. Serve with malt vinegar mayonnaise and lemon wedges.

Italian

Sole with Lemon-Caper Sauce

Serves 2–4 | Total: 20 min (all active)

Source: Giada De Laurentiis, Food Network (Giada Entertains)

Ingredients

Fish

  • 4 fillets of lemon sole
  • 1¼ tsp kosher salt
  • ⅓ cup all-purpose flour, for dredging
  • 2 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter

Sauce

  • ¼ cup capers, drained and rinsed
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • ½ cup chicken stock
  • ¼ cup freshly squeezed lemon juice (from about 1½ lemons)
  • ½ tsp Calabrian chili paste
  • ½ tsp chopped fresh oregano
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter (remaining)

Finish

  • 2 Tbsp chopped fresh Italian parsley

Steps

  1. Pat sole fillets dry with paper towels. Season evenly with 1 tsp salt. Heat a medium skillet over high heat; add 1 Tbsp olive oil and 1 Tbsp butter. When butter is fully melted and bubbles have subsided, dredge 2 fillets in flour, shaking off excess. Add to skillet; reduce heat to medium-high. Cook until beginning to brown around the edges, 2–3 minutes. Flip gently and cook 30 seconds more. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 Tbsp butter, and fish.
  2. With all 4 fillets out of the skillet, add capers and garlic and cook over medium heat, stirring, until fragrant, about 15 seconds. Add chicken stock and lemon juice; stir, scraping up any browned bits. Season with remaining ¼ tsp salt. Simmer about 2 minutes to reduce slightly. Finish by stirring in the remaining 2 Tbsp butter, Calabrian chili paste, and oregano. Spoon sauce over fish, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

Baked Trout St. Helena

Serves 2-4

Original card called for "1 or more trout" with unscaled quantities; scaled here for 2 fish.

Ingredients

Fish

  • 2 whole fresh trout, cleaned
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • 4 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley (divided)

Sauce and basting

  • 2 cans (14-16 oz each) solid-pack tomatoes
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 3/4 cup dry white wine

Steps

  1. Season trout inside and out with salt, pepper, and half the parsley.
  2. Place fish in baking dish. Cover with tomatoes, olive oil, remaining parsley, and garlic.
  3. Bake at 400 degrees for 30-40 minutes until fish flakes easily, basting periodically with the white wine during baking.

French

★ Smoked Salmon Niçoise Salad

Serves 2–4 | Active: 15 min | Total: 45 min

Can also be made with high-end jarred tuna in oil in place of the smoked salmon.

Source: Molly Yeh, Food Network (Girl Meets Farm)

Ingredients

Roasted potatoes

  • 1 lb rainbow fingerling potatoes, quartered
  • 1 Tbsp olive oil
  • ½ tsp kosher salt + freshly ground black pepper

Haricot verts and eggs

  • 8 oz haricot verts, trimmed
  • 1 Tbsp olive oil
  • ¼ tsp kosher salt + freshly ground black pepper
  • 4 large eggs

Dressing

  • ½ cup white wine vinegar
  • ¼ cup Dijon mustard
  • 2 tsp fresh thyme leaves, chopped
  • ½ small red onion, finely chopped
  • ¼ cup olive oil

Salad

  • 1 head Boston, Bibb, or butter lettuce, leaves separated
  • One 4- to 6-oz smoked salmon fillet, broken into large chunks (or high-end jarred tuna in oil)
  • 16 cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 1 cup niçoise or kalamata olives

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F.
  2. Toss quartered potatoes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt, and a few grinds of pepper on a baking sheet. Roast 15 minutes.
  3. Meanwhile, toss haricot verts with 1 Tbsp olive oil, ¼ tsp salt, and pepper on one side of a second baking sheet. Place eggs on the other side. After potatoes have roasted 15 minutes, add the second baking sheet to the oven. Continue roasting until potatoes are golden and easily pierced with a fork and green beans are tender-crisp, about 15 minutes more.
  4. Immediately transfer eggs to a bowl of ice water and let sit 10 minutes. Peel and quarter.
  5. Whisk vinegar, Dijon, thyme, and red onion in a medium bowl. Whisking constantly, slowly drizzle in ¼ cup olive oil until emulsified.
  6. Divide lettuce among serving plates. Arrange potatoes, haricot verts, salmon (or tuna), eggs, cherry tomatoes, and olives on top. Drizzle with dressing, sprinkle with salt and a few grinds of pepper.

Vietnamese

★ Fast Vietnamese Caramel Bluefish

Serves 4 | Total: 20 min

Can be made with any rich, flaky fish such as sea bass — not just bluefish.

Source: Melissa Clark, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Fish

  • 4 (6-oz) skin-on bluefish fillets (or any rich, flaky fish such as sea bass)
  • 1 Tbsp peanut, grapeseed, or safflower oil

Sauce

  • 1 stalk lemongrass (or substitute a 2-inch strip of lemon or lime zest, peeled with a peeler — no bruising needed)
  • ⅓ cup light brown sugar
  • 2 Tbsp Asian fish sauce
  • 1½ Tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
  • ½ tsp black pepper

Garnish

  • Sliced scallions
  • Thinly sliced jalapeño
  • Fresh cilantro
  • Cooked rice (optional)

Steps

  1. Brush fish all over with oil. Remove outer layer of lemongrass stalk and cut stalk into 2-inch lengths; using the butt of a kitchen knife, pound and bruise stalks all over.
  2. Place lemongrass pieces, sugar, fish sauce, soy sauce, ginger, and black pepper in a large skillet. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat; reduce sauce 1–2 minutes until syrupy.
  3. Add fish skin-side down. Simmer, basting frequently with pan sauce, for 2 minutes. Carefully turn fish and continue cooking until just cooked through, 2–3 minutes more.
  4. Transfer to a serving plate. Garnish with scallions, jalapeño, and cilantro. Drizzle with additional sauce. Serve over rice if desired.

Japanese

Spicy Tuna Salad with Crispy Rice

Serves 4 | Prep: 5 min | Cook: 30 min | Total: 35 min

Source: Ali Slagle, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Rice

  • 1½ cups sushi rice, rinsed well
  • 2 cups water
  • 1 Tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar
  • 2 tsp granulated sugar
  • 1 tsp kosher salt (Diamond Crystal)

Tuna salad

  • 3 scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced
  • 2 Persian or mini seedless cucumbers, thinly sliced
  • 4 (5-oz) cans water-packed tuna, drained
  • ⅓ cup mayonnaise
  • 1½ Tbsp Sriracha, plus more to taste
  • 2 tsp soy sauce
  • 2 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar

Cucumber salt

  • Pinch of kosher salt

Oil for crisping

  • 3 Tbsp neutral oil (such as grapeseed), plus more as needed

Steps

  1. In a large nonstick skillet with a lid, stir together 2 cups water, rice, 1 Tbsp rice vinegar, sugar, and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then cover, reduce heat to low, and cook until rice is tender, 18–20 minutes.
  2. Meanwhile, thinly slice scallions and cucumbers. In a large bowl, stir together scallions, tuna, mayonnaise, Sriracha, soy sauce, and remaining 2 tsp rice vinegar. Taste and add more Sriracha for heat. Refrigerate until rice is ready (or up to 5 days).
  3. Sprinkle cucumbers with a pinch of salt.
  4. Crisp the rice: make 4–5 small holes in the rice in the skillet, then pour oil down the sides of the pan and into the divots. Increase heat to medium and cook until rice is browned at the edges, 4–7 minutes. (Lift the rice to check.) If you don't see oil bubbling in the holes, add a teaspoon or two more oil.
  5. Divide rice, crispy-side up, among bowls or plates. Serve with a scoop of spicy tuna and the cucumbers alongside.

Broiled Cod in Miso Sauce

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 6 tablespoons white miso paste
  • 1/2 cup sugar
  • 1/4 cup mirin (sweet Japanese rice wine)
  • 1/4 cup sake

Fish

  • 4 (6-oz) black cod or sea bass fillets, about 3/4" thick

Steps

  1. Mix miso paste, sugar, mirin, and sake in a shallow baking dish. Add fish and turn to coat. Marinate 2-4 hours.
  2. Remove fish from marinade. Broil until opaque in center, approximately 3 minutes per side.

American

Soy-Salmon with Cilantro-Coconut Chutney

Serves 4

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 3/4 cup beer
  • 1/2 cup low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 1/8 teaspoon salt
  • 1/8 teaspoon pepper
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 4 (6-ounce) salmon fillets

Cilantro-Coconut Chutney

  • 1 cup fresh cilantro leaves
  • 1/3 cup shredded sweetened coconut
  • 1/4 cup water
  • 2 tablespoons lime juice
  • 1 tablespoon minced seeded jalapeno pepper
  • 1 teaspoon minced peeled gingerroot
  • 2 teaspoons curry powder
  • 1/8 teaspoon salt
  • 1 garlic clove, minced

Steps

  1. Combine marinade ingredients in 11x7-inch baking dish. Add salmon, turning to coat. Cover and marinate in refrigerator 1 hour, turning occasionally.
  2. Meanwhile, make chutney: place all chutney ingredients in food processor and process until smooth. Makes about 2/3 cup.
  3. Remove salmon from marinade, discard marinade. Grill 5 minutes on each side until fish flakes easily.
  4. Serve with Cilantro-Coconut Chutney (about 2 1/2 tablespoons per serving).

General

Stuffed Eggplant Creole

Serves 4

Crawfish, ground beef, or tofu can be substituted for shrimp.
Lowfat sour cream or plain nonfat yogurt both work well.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Susan Muhlheim

Ingredients

Eggplant

  • 2 small eggplants (1 lb each)

Filling

  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  • 1 lb shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • 1 garlic clove, crushed
  • 1/4 cup finely chopped onion
  • 1/4 cup finely chopped green pepper
  • 1/4 cup finely chopped celery
  • 1 (14-oz) can tomatoes, undrained
  • 1/4 teaspoon dried thyme
  • Salt and Tabasco to taste
  • 1 cup dried bread crumbs, divided
  • 1/2 cup lowfat sour cream or plain nonfat yogurt

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F. Cut eggplants in half lengthwise. Place in a large pan, cover with water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 15 minutes. Drain and cool.
  2. Scoop out pulp from eggplant, leaving a 1/4-inch shell intact. Set pulp aside.
  3. In a skillet, heat vegetable oil. Sauté garlic with shrimp. Add onion, green pepper, and celery; cook 5 minutes over low heat, stirring occasionally.
  4. Stir in tomatoes, salt, thyme, and Tabasco. Add half the bread crumbs, then the eggplant pulp and sour cream; stir well.
  5. Stuff mixture into the 4 eggplant shells. Top with remaining bread crumbs.
  6. Place in a baking dish and bake 30 minutes.

Shrimp with Orzo and Peas

Serves 2–4 | Total: ~20 min

Source: Adapted from Pampered Chef, 29 Minutes to Dinner

Ingredients

Shrimp

  • ½ lb shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • 1 Tbsp vegetable oil
  • ¼ tsp salt
  • ¼ tsp pepper
  • ⅛ tsp sugar

Orzo

  • 2 cups chicken broth
  • 1 cup white wine
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • 8 oz orzo

Finish

  • 1 cup frozen peas
  • 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
  • 1 Tbsp unsalted butter

To serve

  • 1 Tbsp lemon zest, grated
  • 1 Tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped
  • Freshly grated Parmesan (optional)

Steps

  1. In a large bowl, toss shrimp with salt, pepper, and sugar. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook shrimp 3 minutes. Turn and remove from heat; let stand 1 minute until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from skillet.
  2. Add broth, wine, garlic, and orzo to the skillet. Bring to a boil. Cover and cook on medium-low until orzo is tender, 10–12 minutes.
  3. Return shrimp to skillet; add peas, butter, and lemon juice. Cover and let stand 3–5 minutes until heated through. Remove from heat and top with lemon zest and parsley. Serve with freshly grated Parmesan if desired.

Spicy Grilled Shrimp

Serves 4 | Total: 20 min

Source: Mark Bittman, NYT Cooking (1999)

Ingredients

Paste and shrimp

  • 1 large clove garlic
  • 1 Tbsp coarse salt
  • ½ tsp cayenne
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 2 Tbsp olive oil
  • 2 tsp fresh-squeezed lemon juice
  • 1½–2 lbs large shrimp (15–18 per pound), peeled, rinsed, and dried

To serve

  • Lemon wedges

Steps

  1. Start a charcoal or gas grill, or heat the broiler. Make the fire as hot as it will get and put the rack close to the heat source.
  2. Mince garlic with salt; mix with cayenne and paprika, then make into a paste with olive oil and lemon juice. Smear paste all over shrimp. Grill or broil 2–3 minutes per side, turning once. Serve immediately or at room temperature with lemon wedges.
  3. NOTE: For best results, make sure your paprika is fresh — if it doesn't taste vibrant and smoky, it's time to buy more.

Bacon-Wrapped Scallops with Chili Butter

Serves 6–8 | Prep: 15 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: 35 min

Source: Ree Drummond, The Pioneer Woman

Ingredients

Scallops and bacon

  • 2 lbs large scallops
  • ½ lb bacon, cut into thirds or halves
  • Wooden skewers

Chili butter

  • 1 stick (8 Tbsp) unsalted butter
  • 2 tsp chili powder
  • Dash of cayenne

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 425°F. Wrap a piece of bacon around each scallop and secure with a wooden skewer.
  2. Cook on a drip pan for 20 minutes, until bacon is sizzling and brown. (Alternatively: broil for 15 minutes, until bacon is sizzling and brown.)
  3. Melt butter; stir in chili powder and cayenne. Drizzle over scallops before serving.
  4. NOTE: Can also be cooked on the grill.

Italian

Shrimp Scampi with Linguini

Serves 4–6 | Prep: 15 min | Cook: 25 min | Total: 40 min

Source: Tyler Florence, Food Network (Food 911)

Ingredients

Pasta

  • 1 lb linguini

Shrimp and aromatics

  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 2 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • 2 shallots, finely diced
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • Pinch Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes (optional)
  • 1 lb shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Sauce

  • ½ cup dry white wine
  • Juice of 1 lemon
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 2 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

To serve

  • ¼ cup finely chopped fresh parsley
  • Extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling

Steps

  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add linguini and cook 6–8 minutes until not quite done (it will finish in the sauce). Drain.
  2. Meanwhile, melt 2 Tbsp butter with 2 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sauté shallots, garlic, and red pepper flakes (if using) until shallots are translucent, 3–4 minutes. Season shrimp with salt and pepper; add to pan and cook until pink, 2–3 minutes. Remove shrimp and set aside.
  3. Add wine and lemon juice to the pan; bring to a boil. Add remaining 2 Tbsp butter and 2 Tbsp olive oil; when butter has melted, return shrimp to the pan along with parsley and drained pasta. Toss well; season with salt and pepper. Drizzle with olive oil and serve immediately.

Sea Scallops with Red Peppers and Tomatoes

Serves 4

Source: Family recipe, attributed to Grandmother Brenda

Ingredients

Scallops

  • 1 1/2 lbs sea scallops, cut crosswise in half
  • 1/4 cup milk
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Flour for dredging

Sauce

  • 4 tablespoons olive oil (divided)
  • 1 sweet red pepper, cored, seeded, cut into 2" julienne pieces
  • 1 cup ripe plum tomatoes, seeded, peeled, cut into 1/2" pieces

Finish

  • 2 tablespoons finely chopped shallots
  • 1 tablespoon finely chopped garlic
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 4 tablespoons chopped parsley

For serving

  • Cooked rice

Steps

  1. Soak scallops in milk with salt and pepper for about 20 minutes.
  2. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in skillet. Add red pepper and tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, cook and stir until soft, 2-3 minutes. Set aside.
  3. Drain scallops and dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
  4. Heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil over high heat. Cook scallops in a single layer until golden.
  5. Add shallots, garlic, and lemon juice, shaking the pan. Cook 30 seconds.
  6. Add pepper and tomato mixture, stir and toss 2 minutes. Add parsley. Serve immediately over rice.

French

Moules Marinières

Serves 4 | Prep: 45 min | Cook: 15 min | Total: 1 hour

Source: Florence Fabricant, NYT Cooking; garlic and cream option adapted from George Duran, Food Network

Ingredients

Mussels

  • 6 lbs mussels

Aromatics

  • 4 Tbsp unsalted butter, divided
  • 4 Tbsp finely minced shallots (about 2 medium shallots)
  • OPTIONAL: 2–4 garlic cloves, finely minced

Wine

  • 4 cups dry white wine

Cream (optional)

  • ½ cup heavy cream

To serve

  • Freshly ground black pepper
  • 2 Tbsp minced fresh parsley
  • Crusty bread

Steps

  1. Scrub the mussels under cold water. Pull off any beards (the fibrous tufts near the hinge). Discard any that are cracked or don't close when tapped.
  2. In a large pot (at least 8 quarts), melt 2 Tbsp of the butter over low heat. Add shallots (and garlic, if using) and sauté until soft but not browned, about 3–5 minutes.
  3. Add the wine; raise heat to medium. Add mussels, cover, and steam until they open, about 10–15 minutes.
  4. Using a slotted spoon, remove mussels from the pot; divide among warmed bowls. Discard any that did not open.
  5. FOR MOULES À LA CRÈME: Stir the cream into the remaining broth and simmer 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened.
  6. Taste the broth. If too salty, dilute with a little water. Add the remaining 2 Tbsp butter and swirl until melted. Season with pepper. Ladle broth over mussels, taking care not to disturb any sediment at the bottom of the pot.
  7. Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately with crusty bread.
  8. TIP: After the meal, shuck and refrigerate any leftover mussels.

Thai

Mussels with Thai Broth

Serves 4

If Thai red curry paste is unavailable, substitute: 1 tablespoon minced fresh ginger, 1 teaspoon curry powder, 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne.

Source: From Marsha Polk-Townsend, RSVP Catering

Ingredients

Broth

  • 1 cup dry white wine
  • 1/2 cup thinly slivered onion
  • 1 teaspoon minced garlic

Main

  • 32 mussels (beards pulled off), or clams scrubbed
  • 1 can (~14 oz) unsweetened coconut milk
  • 3-4 teaspoons Thai red curry paste
  • 1/4 cup slivered fresh basil leaves

Steps

  1. Bring wine with onion and garlic to a boil. Add shellfish, cover, and cook 5-7 minutes for mussels, 8-10 for clams.
  2. Mix coconut milk with 3 teaspoons curry paste.
  3. Transfer shellfish to 4 bowls. Stir coconut milk mixture into pan, add basil, heat to simmering. Ladle broth into bowls.

Stir-Fry Shrimp

Serves 4

Chicken may be substituted for shrimp (2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1" pieces; cook until no longer pink, about 7-8 minutes).

Ingredients

Stir-fry

  • 1 bunch broccoli, florets only
  • 2 tablespoons peanut oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon minced ginger or ginger powder

  • 2 red peppers, sliced

Finish

Yang Chow Slippery Shrimp

Serves 4 | Total: 25 min

Source: Los Angeles Times (Yang Chow Restaurant)

Ingredients

Shrimp and coating

  • 1 lb large shrimp, peeled, deveined, and butterflied
  • ¼ cup cornstarch

Cornstarch slurry

  • 2 tsp cornstarch
  • 2 tsp water

Frying oil

  • 2 cups oil

Sauce

  • 2 large cloves garlic, minced
  • ½ tsp minced fresh ginger
  • ½ tsp cayenne
  • 1 Tbsp tomato sauce or ketchup
  • 1 Tbsp white vinegar
  • 1 Tbsp white wine
  • 1½ Tbsp sugar
  • ½ tsp salt
  • ¼ cup water

Finish

  • 4 green onions, sliced

Steps

  1. Peel, devein, and butterfly the shrimp.
  2. Toss shrimp with ¼ cup cornstarch until completely coated.
  3. Combine 2 tsp cornstarch with 2 tsp water in a small bowl; set aside.
  4. Heat oil in a skillet or wok over medium heat until hot. Deep-fry shrimp until golden, about 45 seconds. Remove shrimp and drain the oil from the wok, leaving 1 Tbsp.
  5. Reheat wok. Add garlic, ginger, and cayenne; stir a few seconds. Add tomato sauce, vinegar, wine, sugar, salt, ¼ cup water, and the cornstarch slurry. Cook and stir until sauce thickens.
  6. Add shrimp and toss until coated. Add green onions, stir, turn out onto a platter, and serve.

American

Grilled Shrimp and Green Onion Skewers

Serves 2

Chile garlic sauce can be found in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets.

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 1/2 cup grapefruit juice
  • 1/4 cup lime juice
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil

Main

  • 6 green onions
  • 1 dozen medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • Salt and pepper to taste

Glaze
