Italian

Sheet-Pan Italian Sub Dinner

Serves 4 | Total: 25 min

All the flavors of an Italian sub — salami, radicchio, tomatoes, pepperoncini, chickpeas — roasted until caramelized and briny. Can swap in cauliflower florets, cubes of squash, or halved red potatoes for the radicchio.

Source: Ali Slagle, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Vinaigrette

  • 4 garlic cloves
  • 2 Tbsp dried oregano
  • 2 tsp kosher salt
  • ¼ cup red wine vinegar
  • ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil

Roasting ingredients

  • 1 (14-oz) can chickpeas, drained and patted dry
  • 5 oz salami (casing removed if present), cut into ½-inch pieces
  • 1 red onion, peeled, halved lengthwise, cut into ½-inch wedges
  • 1 medium head radicchio (about ¾ lb), quartered lengthwise
  • 1 cup cherry or grape tomatoes, halved
  • 8 pepperoncini peppers

To serve

  • ½ cup ricotta
  • Kosher salt and black pepper
  • Crusty bread

Steps

  1. Heat oven to 450°F. Coarsely chop the garlic, then add the dried oregano and 2 tsp salt on top and chop together until it forms a paste. Transfer to a bowl and stir in the vinegar and olive oil.
  2. Pour half the dressing into a large bowl. Add the chickpeas, salami, red onion, radicchio, tomatoes, and pepperoncini. Mix gently to coat, trying not to break up the radicchio and onion. Spread evenly on a baking sheet. Roast, tossing halfway through, until the red onions and chickpeas are golden, 15–20 minutes.
  3. Season the ricotta with salt and pepper. Serve the roasted mixture with crusty bread and a dollop of ricotta and extra vinaigrette, or assemble into sandwiches.

French

Peppered Duck Breast With Red Wine Sauce

Serves 6 | Total: ~1½ hours (including 1 hour marinate)

A steak au poivre made with duck. Fancy enough for a gathering, relaxed enough for any night you want something special. The sauce can be made ahead and reheated, thinned with a little broth.

Source: David Tanis, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Duck and marinade (up to 1 day ahead)

  • 3 Muscovy duck breasts (about 1 lb each)
  • Salt
  • 1 Tbsp freshly crushed black peppercorns (about 1 tsp per breast)
  • 4 garlic cloves, sliced
  • Fresh thyme sprigs

Sauce

  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter, divided
  • Reserved duck tenderloins (from Step 1)
  • 1 large shallot, sliced
  • 1 Tbsp tomato paste
  • 1 small thyme sprig
  • 2 cups unsalted chicken broth
  • ¼ cup + 2 Tbsp medium-bodied red wine
  • 1 Tbsp Cognac or brandy
  • 2 tsp potato starch

Steps

  1. Remove the tenderloins (the thin strips on the undersides of the duck breasts) and reserve for the sauce. With a sharp knife, trim away any gristle from the undersides and any excess fat. Score the skin in a diamond pattern, cutting through the fat but not into the meat. Lightly sprinkle salt on both sides, then rub 1 tsp crushed black peppercorns all over each breast. Sprinkle with the garlic and a few thyme sprigs, cover, and leave at room temperature for 1 hour. (For deeper flavor, refrigerate for several hours or overnight, then return to room temperature before cooking.)
  2. Heat 1 Tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the shallot and reserved duck tenderloins and let them brown well, stirring occasionally, 5–8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and thyme sprig and let fry for 1 minute.
  3. Add the broth and ¼ cup wine, raise heat to a brisk simmer, and reduce to about 1¼ cups, about 10 minutes. Strain the sauce and return to heat. Add the remaining 2 Tbsp red wine and the Cognac or brandy and cook 1 minute more. Dissolve the potato starch in 2 Tbsp cold water, then stir into the sauce. Whisk in the remaining 1 Tbsp butter. Season with salt.
  4. Remove and discard the garlic and thyme from the breasts. Heat a large, heavy skillet over medium-high. When hot, lay in the duck breasts skin-side down and let sizzle. Lower heat to medium and cook for a total of 7 minutes, checking to ensure the skin isn't browning too quickly. Turn over and cook another 3 minutes for rare, 4–5 minutes for medium-rare. Transfer to a warm platter and rest 10 minutes. Slice crosswise at a slight angle and serve with the sauce.

Vegetarian Mains

Vegetables

General

★ Lentil Chili

Serves 12 (about 1 cup each)

You'll never miss the meat in this super-delicious chili -- it's a great way to serve a crowd.

Source: Low Fat & Loving It (cookbook)

Ingredients

Aromatics

  • 1/3 cup olive oil
  • 1 medium onion, cut into 1/2-inch chunks
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 medium carrot, peeled and coarsely chopped

Chili base

  • 7 cups water
  • 1/3 cup tomato paste
  • 2 cups (about 12 oz) brown lentils, rinsed
  • 1 green pepper, cut into 1/2-inch chunks
  • 1 sweet red pepper, cut into 1/2-inch chunks

Beans and tomatoes

  • 1 (19-oz) can red kidney beans, rinsed and drained
  • 1 cup canned garbanzo beans, rinsed and drained
  • 2 cups canned whole tomatoes in puree

Seasoning

  • 1/3 cup chili powder
  • 4 teaspoons ground cumin
  • 1/4 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes (or more to taste)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Steps

  1. Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot. Sauté the onion, garlic, and carrot over medium heat until the carrot is tender, about 5 minutes.
  2. Add the water, tomato paste, lentils, green and red peppers, and the kidney and garbanzo beans. Add the tomatoes, breaking them up against the side of the pot. Stir in the chili powder, cumin, and Aleppo pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to moderate.
  3. Cover and cook 45 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Add more water if necessary.
  4. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve alone or over plain white rice.

Latin/South American

Slow Cooker Vegan Mole Chili

Serves 6 | Prep: 25 min | Cook: 5 hours | Total: ~5 hr 25 min

Rich, hearty vegan chili with mole-inspired depth. Greek yogurt is a great topping but omit to keep strictly vegan.
Tofu note: Freeze the entire tofu block until firm (overnight works — keep a block or two in the freezer as a habit). Thaw in the refrigerator, then drain as usual. Slice into 4–5 slabs and gently press out extra moisture between two plates. Finely dice per the recipe. Frozen-and-thawed tofu becomes sponge-like and soaks up the slow-cooked flavors.

Source: Emily Stoffel, The Pig & Quill

Ingredients

Dried chilies

  • 3 oz dried ancho chilies

Spice paste

  • ¼ cup light cooking oil (such as avocado)
  • 3 Tbsp chili powder
  • 1 Tbsp cacao powder
  • 1½ tsp Mexican oregano
  • 1 tsp cinnamon
  • 1 tsp cumin
  • 1 tsp paprika

Chili base

  • 1 medium red onion, finely diced
  • 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and finely diced
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced
  • 14 oz block tofu, frozen, thawed, drained, and finely diced (see note)
  • 1 can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
  • 3 bay leaves
  • ¼ cup coconut sugar
  • 1 tsp sea salt
  • 1½ oz good dark chocolate (at least 70%)
  • 3 cups mushroom stock (or vegetable stock)

To serve

  • Cilantro (optional)
  • Greek yogurt (optional; omit if strictly vegan)
  • Quinoa, rice, or other grain

Steps

  1. Remove stems and seeds from the ancho chilies. Place in a bowl, cover with very hot tap water, and steep covered for 20 minutes.
  2. Meanwhile, heat the oil in a small saucepan or skillet. Add the chili powder, cacao, oregano, cinnamon, cumin, and paprika; heat until bubbling and very fragrant, about 60 seconds. Remove from heat and set aside. Use this time to dice your veggies and prepare the tofu (see note).
  3. When the chilies have finished steeping, drain, reserving ¼ cup soaking liquid. Add chilies and reserved liquid to a food processor and blend until nearly smooth.
  4. Combine all the veggies, tofu, chickpeas, processed chilies, and spice paste in the slow cooker. Add the bay leaves, coconut sugar, salt, chocolate, and stock. Stir well. Cook on High for 5 hours, or until the vegetables have all but dissolved. Adjust salt to taste. Serve with grain and toppings of choice.

Italian

Eggplant Involtini

Serves 4 | Total: 1 hour

A lighter, weeknight-friendly take on eggplant parmesan — no breading, no frying. The eggplant is roasted or grilled into silky planks, rolled around a three-cheese filling, and baked in homemade tomato sauce. If you don't want to make the sauce, 3 cups of good store-bought sauce works fine.

Source: https://smittenkitchen.com/2022/09/eggplant-involtini/

Ingredients

Eggplant

  • 2 medium eggplants (about 1 pound each), tops trimmed
  • Olive oil, for brushing
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Tomato sauce

  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, to taste
  • ½ teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1 (28-ounce) can whole or crushed tomatoes

Filling

  • 1 cup ricotta
  • 4 ounces mozzarella, coarsely grated
  • ¼ cup grated Parmesan (of the ½ cup total)
  • Finely grated zest from half a lemon
  • ½ teaspoon kosher salt
  • Freshly ground black pepper

To finish

  • ¼ cup grated Parmesan (remaining)
  • Juice from half a lemon
  • Fresh basil leaves

Steps

  1. Prep and cook the eggplant:
    • Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut the eggplants into generous ¼-inch-thick lengthwise planks. Arrange on parchment-lined baking sheets, brush both sides with olive oil, and season well with salt and pepper.
    • To roast: Bake 10–12 minutes on the first side, flip, and roast another 8–10 minutes, until browned on each side.
    • To grill: Grill over high heat until dark marks appear, about 8 minutes on the first side and 5 on the second.
    • Set aside to cool.
  2. Make the sauce:
    • Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in an 11- to 12-inch ovenproof pot over medium. Add the garlic, salt, Aleppo pepper, and oregano; cook 1 minute.
    • Add the tomatoes (it will splatter — be careful) and stir. Simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Taste and adjust seasoning; blend if you prefer a smoother texture.
    • Ladle out 1 cup sauce and set aside for serving. If your pot isn't ovenproof, transfer the remaining sauce to a 2-quart baking dish.
  3. Make the filling: In a bowl, combine the ricotta, mozzarella, ¼ cup Parmesan, lemon zest, ½ teaspoon salt, and a few grinds of pepper.
  4. Assemble the rolls:
    • Place about 1 tablespoon of filling at the end of each eggplant plank (a little less on smaller ones), using all the filling.
    • Roll into a cigar and place seam-side down in the sauce.
  5. Bake: Brush the tops lightly with olive oil. Bake uncovered about 30 minutes, until bubbly at the edges and browned on top.
  6. Squeeze the lemon juice over the top and scatter with fresh basil. Serve with the reserved sauce and extra Parmesan on the side.

Eggplant Parmesan

Serves 6–8 | Prep: 20 minutes | Cook: 40 minutes | Total: 1 hour

Source: https://www.loveandlemons.com/eggplant-parmesan/

Ingredients

Eggplant

  • 2 large eggplants, cut into ¼-inch-thick rounds

Egg wash

  • 3 large eggs, beaten

Panko coating

  • 1½ cups panko breadcrumbs
  • 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese (of the 1¼ cups total)
  • 2 teaspoons dried oregano
  • 2 tablespoons fresh thyme leaves
  • ½ teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • Freshly ground black pepper
  • Extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling

Assembly

  • 28 ounces marinara sauce
  • 2 large fresh mozzarella balls, thinly sliced (or one package shredded mozzarella)
  • ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese (remaining from the 1¼ cups total)
  • Extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling
  • Sea salt, for sprinkling

To serve

  • ⅓ cup fresh basil leaves

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F and line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. Set up the breading stations:
    • Beat the eggs in a shallow bowl.
    • In a second shallow bowl, combine the panko, 1 cup Parmesan, oregano, thyme, Aleppo pepper, salt, and several grinds of black pepper.
  3. Bread and bake the eggplant:
    • Dip each eggplant slice in the egg wash, then press into the panko mixture to coat on all sides.
    • Arrange in a single layer on the baking sheets. Drizzle with olive oil.
    • Bake 18–25 minutes, until tender and golden brown. (Use convection setting if available for extra crispness.)
  4. Assemble and bake:
    • Spread ½ cup marinara in the bottom of a 9×13-inch baking dish.
    • Layer half the eggplant, then 1 cup marinara, then half the mozzarella. Repeat with the remaining eggplant, remaining marinara, and remaining mozzarella.
    • Top with the remaining ¼ cup Parmesan, a drizzle of olive oil, and a few pinches of sea salt.
    • Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
  5. Turn the oven to broil and broil for 2–4 minutes, until the cheese is browned in spots. Remove from the oven, top with fresh basil, and serve.

Moroccan/North African

Moroccan Eggplant with Couscous

Serves 6 (serving size: 2 cups)

Source: Printed clipping

Ingredients

Spice mixture

  • 2 teaspoons curry powder
  • 2 teaspoons ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon pepper

Vegetables

  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 8 cups (1/2-inch) cubed peeled eggplant (about 1 1/2 lbs)
  • 2 1/3 cups chopped tomato
  • 1 1/2 cups chopped onion
  • 1 cup chopped carrot
  • 1 cup chopped green cabbage
  • 1 tablespoon minced peeled gingerroot
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced

Liquid and couscous

  • 2 cups tomato juice
  • 1 cup orange juice
  • 1 cup water
  • 2 cups uncooked couscous

Steps

  1. Combine the 5 spices in a small bowl; stir well.
  2. Heat oil in an ovenproof Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add spice mixture, then eggplant, tomato, onion, carrot, cabbage, ginger, and garlic. Sauté 3 minutes.
  3. Add tomato juice, orange juice, and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 2 minutes.
  4. Remove from heat; stir in couscous. Cover and bake at 350°F for 20 minutes.

Tofu

General

Tofu Stir Fry

Serves 2 | Prep: 20 min | Cook: 15 min | Total: 35 min

Source: Kahnita Wilkerson, Tasty

Ingredients

Sauce

  • 2 garlic cloves, minced (of 4 total)
  • 2 tsp fresh ginger, grated
  • 1 Tbsp honey
  • 1 tsp sriracha
  • ¼ cup lime juice
  • ¼ cup reduced-sodium soy sauce

Tofu

  • 1 block extra-firm tofu

Stir fry

  • 2 Tbsp sesame oil
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced (remaining)
  • 1 cup white onion, sliced
  • 1 cup carrot, sliced
  • 1 cup red bell pepper, sliced
  • ½ cup edamame, frozen, thawed
  • 3 cups soba noodles, cooked
  • 1 Tbsp sesame seeds

Garnish

  • Green onion, chopped

Steps

  1. In a medium bowl, mix together 2 cloves of garlic, the ginger, honey, sriracha, lime juice, and soy sauce. Set aside.
  2. Wrap the tofu in a dish towel, then place a plate on top. Let drain for 10–15 minutes, then remove the plate, unwrap the tofu, and slice into cubes.
  3. In a wok or large frying pan, heat the sesame oil over medium heat. Add the tofu and pan-fry for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  4. Add the remaining 2 cloves of minced garlic and the onion and stir until softened, about 1 minute.
  5. Add the carrot, bell pepper, and edamame and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 2–3 minutes.
  6. Add the soba noodles, reserved sauce, and sesame seeds. Cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until warmed through. Remove from heat.
  7. Garnish with green onions and serve.

Sesame Ginger Tofu and Veggie Stir Fry

Serves 3 | Prep: 25 min | Cook: 15 min | Total: 40 min

Source: Marzia, Little Spice Jar

Ingredients

Tofu and coating

  • 14 oz extra-firm tofu
  • 1 Tbsp cornstarch
  • ½ tsp kosher salt

Sauce

  • 1 Tbsp sesame oil
  • 1½ Tbsp grated ginger
  • 1½ Tbsp minced garlic
  • 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
  • 3 Tbsp soy sauce (or GF tamari)
  • ¼ tsp Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 3 Tbsp brown sugar
  • 1 Tbsp cornstarch
  • 2 Tbsp water

Stir fry

  • 3 Tbsp avocado oil
  • 2½ cups green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
  • 1 cup baby carrots, cut lengthwise

To serve (optional)

  • Rice, quinoa, noodles, or cauliflower rice

Steps

  1. TOFU: Drain tofu. Place on a plate with a folded tea towel, then top with another tea towel, another plate, and a heavy cast iron skillet or metal cans (or use a tofu press). Let drain 15–20 minutes or up to 1 hour. Cut into ¾–1 inch cubes and toss in 1 Tbsp cornstarch and ½ tsp salt in a zip-top bag until coated.
  2. SAUCE: While the tofu is pressing, combine all sauce ingredients in a blender until completely smooth. (Shortcut: if using garlic paste and ginger paste, simply whisk together in a bowl.) Set aside.
  3. CRISPY TOFU: In a wok or large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, add 2 Tbsp avocado oil. Add tofu and fry for 3–7 minutes, flipping as needed to brown on all sides. Add 2 Tbsp of the prepared sauce and cook until the sauce coats and caramelizes on the tofu, about 2–3 minutes. Remove to a plate.
  4. STIR FRY: Add the remaining 1 Tbsp avocado oil to the pan if needed. Add the veggies and cook for 3–4 minutes, tossing to desired doneness. Add the tofu back to the skillet. Stir the sauce to recombine, then pour it in. Stir to coat. Cook 1–2 minutes more until the tofu soaks up the sauce.
  5. Serve warm with rice, quinoa, noodles, cauliflower rice, or on its own. Best eaten fresh; the tofu loses crispness as it sits.

West African

Baked Tofu With Peanut Sauce and Coconut-Lime Rice

Serves 4 | Total: ~45 min

The peanut sauce is inspired by West African groundnut stews. Fish sauce adds umami but is optional; omit it to keep the dish vegan. Peanut sauce can be made 2–3 days ahead and refrigerated.

Source: Yewande Komolafe, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Pickled peppers

  • 4 Tbsp lime juice (of ⅔ cup total)
  • ½ tsp kosher salt
  • 8 baby bell peppers or 1 medium bell pepper (any color), stemmed and thinly sliced lengthwise
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Coconut-lime rice

  • 1 cup long-grain rice (jasmine or basmati)
  • ½ cup full-fat coconut milk
  • 1 cup water
  • Salt

Peanut sauce

  • 4 Tbsp lime juice (remaining from the ⅔ cup)
  • 1 cup smooth, natural peanut butter
  • 1 Tbsp red miso
  • 1 Tbsp grated ginger
  • 1 Tbsp fish sauce (optional)
  • 2 tsp chopped habanero pepper (stem and seeds removed) or 1 Tbsp sambal
  • 2 Tbsp peanut or vegetable oil
  • 1 Tbsp buckwheat honey or molasses (+ 1 Tbsp more for dressing in Step 5)
  • ¾ cup water

Tofu

  • 2 (14-oz) packages extra-firm tofu, drained and sliced crosswise ¼-inch thick
  • Peanut or vegetable oil, for brushing pan and drizzling
  • Salt

To serve

  • Zest of 1 lime
  • 3 cups peppery greens (arugula, mizuna, or baby mustard greens)
  • 2 scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced

Steps

  1. Heat oven to 450°F and lightly brush a large rimmed sheet pan with oil.
  2. In a small bowl, stir 4 Tbsp lime juice with ½ tsp salt until dissolved. Add the sliced peppers and a few cracks of black pepper. Set aside to quick-pickle.
  3. In a small pot, combine the rice with 1 cup water and the coconut milk. Season with salt and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over medium-low until just tender, 12–15 minutes. Remove from heat; keep covered until serving.
  4. In a medium bowl, whisk together the remaining 4 Tbsp lime juice, peanut butter, miso, ginger, fish sauce (if using), habanero (or sambal), 2 Tbsp oil, 1 Tbsp honey, and ¾ cup water until smooth. Season to taste with salt.
  5. Arrange tofu in a single layer on the oiled baking sheet; season with salt. Spoon about 2 Tbsp peanut sauce over each piece, coating the top and letting it run down the sides. Drizzle with a little oil and roast until the glaze is set, deep brown, and caramelized along the edges, 18–20 minutes. Add the remaining lime juice and 1 Tbsp honey to the leftover sauce in the bowl to make the dressing; set aside.
  6. Divide the greens among bowls. Stir the lime zest and half the scallions into the rice, then fluff with a fork. Top greens with rice, then the tofu. Spoon the peanut dressing over everything and garnish with the drained pickled peppers and remaining scallions.

Mushroom

Mushrooms Florentine

Serves 8–10

Can be assembled a day ahead and refrigerated until ready to bake. To serve 4, halve all ingredients and use a greased 10-inch round or 8×8 casserole.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Sue Karp

Ingredients

Mushrooms

  • 2 lbs small fresh mushrooms, stems removed
  • Butter, for sautéing

Spinach base

  • 4 packages (10 oz each) frozen chopped spinach, defrosted and squeezed very dry
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 1/2 cup butter, melted
  • Garlic salt, to taste

Cheese

  • 2 cups grated cheddar, divided

Steps

  1. Sauté mushroom caps in butter over medium-high heat, bottom-side down, until lightly browned. Remove from pan; drain on paper towels.
  2. Defrost spinach; squeeze out all water thoroughly (very important — spinach should be quite dry).
  3. Combine spinach, onion, a generous pinch of garlic salt, and melted butter in a bowl; mix well.
  4. Grease a 9×13 casserole. Spread spinach mixture evenly over the bottom.
  5. Sprinkle with 1 cup of cheddar.
  6. Arrange mushroom caps over the spinach, cap-side down.
  7. Sprinkle with a little more garlic salt. Cover with remaining cup of cheddar.
  8. Bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes, until cheese is melted and beginning to brown.

Oven Polenta with Roasted Mushrooms and Thyme

Serves 4 | Total: ~55 min

A "no-stir" oven polenta — the oven does the work while the mushrooms roast on the rack above. For an indulgent touch, stir a little heavy cream mixed with a finely grated garlic clove into the finished polenta.

Source: Claire Saffitz, Bon Appétit

Ingredients

Mushrooms

  • 1½ lbs mixed mushrooms (crimini, shiitake, oyster, and/or maitake), torn into 1-inch pieces
  • 4 thyme sprigs, plus thyme leaves for serving
  • 6 garlic cloves, smashed
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
  • ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil

Polenta

  • 4½ cups water
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • Kosher salt
  • 1 cup polenta

Polenta — finish

  • 4 oz Parmesan, finely grated, plus more for serving

Mushrooms — finish

  • 1 Tbsp red wine vinegar

To serve

  • Flaky sea salt
  • Thyme leaves
  • More Parmesan

Steps

  1. Place racks in upper and lower thirds of oven; preheat to 325°F. Combine mushrooms, thyme sprigs, and garlic on a large rimmed baking sheet. Season generously with kosher salt and pepper; drizzle with olive oil. Toss to coat, then spread in an even layer. (Don't crowd the mushrooms or they'll steam instead of crisping.) Transfer to the upper rack.
  2. Bring 4½ cups water to a simmer in a large ovenproof saucepan over medium-high heat. Add butter and a generous pinch of kosher salt; whisk to melt. Gradually whisk in the polenta (adding slowly prevents clumps). Return to a boil, immediately cover the pot, and transfer to the lower rack. Bake, shaking the mushroom pan occasionally, until polenta is tender, 25–30 minutes.
  3. Remove polenta from oven. Raise oven temperature as high as it will go (but don't broil). Continue roasting mushrooms until crispy around the edges, 5–10 more minutes.
  4. Uncover the polenta and whisk vigorously, scraping the bottom, until smooth and thick. Gradually whisk in the Parmesan until melted and incorporated. Season with kosher salt and pepper. Cover and keep warm over low heat.
  5. Remove mushrooms from oven; drizzle with red wine vinegar. Toss to coat and let cool slightly.
  6. Divide polenta among bowls and top with mushrooms, thyme leaves, flaky sea salt, and more Parmesan.

Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms with Crispy Goat Cheese

Serves 4 | Prep: 15 min | Cook: 45 min | Total: 1 hour

Use large portobello mushrooms roughly 4 inches wide with slightly deeper caps — they're easier to stuff. Two mushrooms per serving makes a hearty main; one per person if serving as a side. For gluten-free, substitute gluten-free breadcrumbs.

Source: Laura Davidson, A Beautiful Plate

Ingredients

Marinara

  • 1 Tbsp olive oil
  • 4 garlic cloves, roughly chopped
  • 2 Tbsp tomato paste
  • 2 dried bay leaves
  • 1 Tbsp dried oregano
  • 1 (28-oz) can Italian crushed tomatoes
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Mushrooms

  • 8 large (4-inch wide) portobello mushrooms, stems trimmed
  • Extra-virgin olive oil
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Spinach

  • 1 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1 shallot, finely sliced
  • 6 oz baby spinach
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Breadcrumb topping

  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 1 shallot, finely diced
  • ½ cup panko breadcrumbs
  • 1 garlic clove, finely minced
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Assembly

  • 4 oz goat cheese, cold from the fridge

Steps

  1. MARINARA: Warm 1 Tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir continuously for 30 seconds — do not let it brown. Add the tomato paste; stir over low heat for 1 minute. Add the bay leaves, oregano, and crushed tomatoes. Stir, bring to a low simmer, cover, and cook 30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. (Can be made well ahead; reheat before using.)
  2. MUSHROOMS: Preheat oven to 450°F with rack in center. Lightly brush a sheet pan with olive oil. Place portobellos stem-side up, brush lightly with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast 15–25 minutes (check after 10 minutes), until tender. Drain any moisture that collects in the caps. Transfer to a large plate.
  3. SPINACH: Heat olive oil in a sauté pan over medium-low heat. Add the sliced shallots and sauté 3–4 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the spinach, raise heat to medium-high, and sauté until just wilted, stirring continuously. Season with salt and pepper; set aside.
  4. BREADCRUMBS: Melt the butter in a small sauté pan over medium heat. Once sizzling, add the diced shallots and a pinch of salt; cook 1–2 minutes. Add the panko and minced garlic; toast 3–4 minutes, stirring constantly, until very light golden. Transfer to a shallow bowl and season with salt and pepper.
  5. Reduce oven to 425°F. Line the same sheet pan with parchment paper (or set a baking rack inside the pan so mushrooms don't sit in released juice).
  6. Arrange mushrooms stem-side up on the pan, touching each other. Fill each with a large spoonful of marinara. Top with the sautéed spinach.
  7. Slice the goat cheese into ½-inch thick slices (roughly ½ oz each — it may crumble a bit). Press both sides of each slice into the panko topping and place on top of a mushroom. Sprinkle remaining breadcrumbs over.
  8. Bake at 425°F for 10–15 minutes until heated through, breadcrumbs are golden brown, and the goat cheese just begins to soften. Watch closely so the breadcrumbs don't burn. Serve immediately.

Truffle Mushroom Risotto

Serves 4 | Prep: 20 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: 40 min

A go-to "fancy" dinner that's actually easy. The risotto should flow like slow-moving lava, not form a stiff ball. Black truffle puree is available at specialty grocery stores and online.

Source: Jenny Goycochea, So Much Food

Ingredients

Risotto base

  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter (of 4 oz / 1 stick total, divided)
  • 2 small shallots, finely minced
  • 1½ cups arborio rice
  • ½ cup dry white wine

Broth

  • 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth, warmed

Mushrooms

  • 1 Tbsp unsalted butter + 1 Tbsp neutral oil
  • 12 oz cremini mushrooms, quartered
  • Salt and freshly cracked pepper

Finish

  • Remaining 5 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 2 Tbsp black truffle puree
  • ½ cup mascarpone
  • ⅔ cup freshly grated Parmesan, plus more for garnish
  • Salt and freshly cracked pepper

Garnish

  • Chopped chives
  • Extra Parmesan

Steps

  1. Heat 2 Tbsp butter over medium heat in a wide-bottomed skillet or pan with at least 3-inch sides. Add shallots and cook 2–3 minutes until softened. Add rice and stir to coat all grains in butter. Toast about 1 minute. Add wine and stir continuously.
  2. Once the wine is absorbed, add 1 cup warm broth, stirring constantly. Once absorbed, add another cup. Continue adding broth 1 cup at a time, stirring and waiting for each addition to absorb, until the rice is just slightly al dente. (The pan bottom exposed when you drag your spoon across it tells you it's time to add more broth.)
  3. While the rice cooks, heat 1 Tbsp butter and 1 Tbsp neutral oil in a cast iron skillet over medium-high. Add mushrooms and let sear without stirring until golden brown on one side. Stir and cook 2–3 minutes more. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
  4. When the rice is done, turn off the heat. Stir in ⅔ of the cooked mushrooms, the truffle puree, remaining 5 Tbsp butter, mascarpone, and Parmesan. Stir until all the cheese and butter has melted. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
  5. Ladle risotto into bowls. Top with the remaining mushrooms, extra Parmesan, and chopped chives.

Roasted Portobellos With Pesto

Serves 4 | Total: 30 min

Uses Christy's Pesto (Adapted) already in this cookbook (see Noodles section). Homemade or store-bought pesto both work. Serve with rice or noodles tossed with butter for a simple meal. These reheat well a few hours later.

Source: Martha Rose Shulman, NYT Cooking

Ingredients

Mushrooms

  • 8 medium (roasting size) portobello mushrooms
  • 1 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • Salt and freshly ground pepper

Fill

  • ¼ cup pesto (see Christy's Pesto (Adapted) in this cookbook)

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Remove the stems from the mushrooms and carefully scrape away the gills using a spoon. Toss with the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place rounded-side down on a lightly oiled baking sheet. Roast 8–10 minutes, until beginning to soften and release liquid. Remove from oven and fill each cap with pesto. Return to the oven and roast until thoroughly softened, about 10 more minutes. Serve immediately.

Vegetable Sides

General

Sautéed Mushrooms

Serves 6 | Prep: 10 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: 30 min

The classic steak topping — also great over chicken, pork chops, or grain bowls. Have patience: let the mushrooms release all their moisture before they begin to brown. Leftovers keep in the fridge up to 10 days; reheat on the stovetop with a little extra butter.

Source: Sommer Collier, A Spicy Perspective

Ingredients

Mushrooms and fat

  • 2 lbs button mushrooms, halved
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 2 Tbsp olive oil

Aromatics

  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • Salt and pepper to taste

Glaze

  • 1½ Tbsp fresh thyme leaves
  • ¾ cup dry sherry

Steps

  1. Place a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add the butter and olive oil. Once the butter has melted, add the mushrooms.
  2. Let the mushrooms sear for 5 minutes, stirring to flip them. Add the garlic and salt and pepper to taste. Sear another 5 minutes to develop a rich caramelized color.
  3. Stir in the thyme leaves and sherry. Lower heat to medium-low and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms have absorbed the sherry and only a small amount of moisture remains in the pan.
  4. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Serve warm over steak, chicken, pork chops, or as a side dish.

Central/Eastern European

Potato Latkes

Makes about 12 latkes

Keep finished latkes warm in a 250°F oven while frying subsequent batches.
The original notes you can use more flour or matzo meal as needed to hold the batter together.
Variation: Pour the same batter into a well-greased muffin pan and bake 45 minutes at 350°F.

Source: "Celebration: The Book of Jewish Festivals," ed. Naomi Black (Jonathan David Publishers, 1989)

Ingredients

Batter

  • 6 medium potatoes, grated
  • 1 onion, grated
  • 2 eggs
  • 2 tablespoons flour or matzo meal (more as needed)
  • 1 teaspoon salt

For frying

  • Vegetable oil

Steps

  1. Grate the potatoes into a mixing bowl. Squeeze out the liquid or drain in a colander for a few minutes. Grate the onion into the potatoes.
  2. Add the eggs and mix. Add the flour and mix. Add the salt and stir until you have a smooth batter that drops heavily from the spoon.
  3. Heat enough vegetable oil in a frying pan to cover the latkes amply. Drop the batter from a tablespoon into the hot oil, making pancakes about 3 inches in diameter. Do not allow the oil to smoke; let it come back up to temperature after every few latkes and after replenishing the oil.
  4. Fry until brown on the underside, then turn and brown the other side. Lift out and drain on paper towels. Keep warm in a 250°F oven while frying remaining batches.

Mediterranean/Greek

Potatoes Gratin (Low Calorie)

Serves 6–8 | Prep: 10 min | Cook: 1 to 1 1/4 hours

Low-calorie version using skim milk and eggs rather than cream.

Source: Family recipe card

Ingredients

Potatoes

  • 2 large garlic cloves, halved lengthwise
  • 3 lbs new potatoes, unpeeled, scrubbed, and very thinly sliced

Custard

  • 3 1/3 cups skim milk
  • 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • Salt and pepper to taste

Topping

  • 6 tablespoons grated parmesan cheese

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Rub the inside of a 9x14x2-inch Pyrex dish with the cut side of the garlic. Thinly slice the garlic and toss with the potatoes.
  2. Layer potatoes in the Pyrex dish. Mix together milk, eggs, salt, and pepper. Pour mixture over potatoes.
  3. Bake 1 to 1 1/4 hours. Every 15 minutes, remove from oven and, using a knife or wooden spoon, press down the top layer of potatoes that has gotten crusty and fold it into the rest.
  4. When golden and potatoes are tender, sprinkle with parmesan and return to oven. Bake until a golden crust forms, about 10–15 minutes.

Rice

General

Indian Style Rice

4 to 6 | Prep: 15 minutes, plus 30 minutes soaking | Cook: about 25 minutes (rice cooker)

If you don't have whole cardamom pods or a cinnamon stick, use a pinch each of ground cardamom and ground cinnamon added with the turmeric.
Adapted for a rice cooker — rather than boiling the rice separately and draining it (the original stovetop method), the sautéed spice mixture is stirred into the rice cooker with the water and rice.

Source: Simply Recipes, by Elise Bauer, adapted for a rice cooker

Ingredients

Rice

  • 2 cups Jasmine or Basmati rice
  • 3 cups water
  • 2 teaspoons salt

Whole spices

  • 2 cloves
  • 2 green cardamom pods
  • One 2-inch piece cinnamon

Aromatics

  • 3 tablespoons vegetable oil (or ghee)
  • 1/2 teaspoon dark mustard seeds
  • 1/2 teaspoon cumin seeds
  • 1/4 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 1 medium onion, chopped
  • 3 garlic cloves, chopped
  • 1/4 teaspoon turmeric

Steps

  1. Rinse the rice in a sieve under cool running water until the water runs clear. Soak in cool water 30 minutes, then drain well.
  2. Sauté: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes; cook until the seeds begin to pop, about 30 seconds.
  3. Add the onion and cook until it begins to brown, 5 to 7 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 2 to 3 minutes more. Stir in the turmeric.
  4. Rice cooker: Add the drained rice, the cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, and the sautéed onion mixture to the rice cooker. Add the water and salt; stir to combine. Cook on the regular rice cycle.
  5. Fluff the rice with a fork, picking out the whole cloves, cardamom pod, and cinnamon stick as you find them (or leave them in and warn guests).

American

Rice with Dill

May be reheated.

Ingredients

Aromatics

  • 3 tablespoons butter
  • 1/2 cup minced onion
  • 1 can water chestnuts, sliced

Rice

  • 1 1/2 cups Jasmine or Basmati rice
  • 2 1/2 cups chicken broth

Seasoning

  • Salt to taste
  • Pepper to taste
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill
  • 1/2 bay leaf
  • Few drops Tabasco sauce to taste

Steps

  1. Oven method: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Melt butter in oven-proof casserole over medium heat. Add onion and water chestnuts; cook and stir until softened, about 3 minutes. Add rice and stir to coat with butter. Add chicken broth and stir to ensure no lumps. Add dill, bay leaf, Tabasco, salt, and pepper. Cover with a close-fitting lid and bring to a boil. Transfer to oven and bake for 17 minutes. Remove cover, discard bay leaf, and serve.
  2. Rice cooker method: Melt butter in skillet over medium heat. Add onion and water chestnuts; cook and stir until softened, about 3 minutes. Add rice and stir to coat with butter, about 1 minute. Transfer rice mixture to rice cooker. Add chicken broth and all seasonings (dill, bay leaf, Tabasco, salt, and pepper). Cook on standard rice setting. When done, remove and discard bay leaf, and serve.

Noodles

Italian

General

BIG Noods alla Gin with Sungold Tomatoes

4 to 6 | Prep: 40 minutes | Total: 50 minutes

Fresh lasagna sheets are called for here for their fun, floppy volume on the plate, but any pasta shape — fresh or dried — works well.
Vodka can stand in for the gin.

Source: The Club, by Molly Baz

Ingredients

Prep

  • 2 pints Sungold or cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 1 yellow onion, finely chopped
  • 6 garlic cloves, sliced

Sauce

  • 3 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • Kosher salt
  • 3 ounces double concentrated tomato paste (about 3/4 of a tube)
  • 1 tablespoon chopped Calabrian chilies
  • 1/4 cup gin or vodka
  • 1/4 cup heavy cream
  • 1 1/2 ounces (about 3/4 cup) finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano

Pasta

  • 12 ounces fresh lasagna sheets (or any pasta shape, fresh or dried)

To finish

  • Handful of basil
  • Olive oil, for drizzling
  • More grated Parmigiano-Reggiano

Steps

  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
  2. Prep: Cut the tomatoes in half. Finely chop the onion and slice the garlic.
  3. Sungold sauce:
    • Heat the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and a big pinch of salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden, about 10 minutes.
    • Add the garlic and cook 2 minutes more.
    • Stir in the tomato paste and Calabrian chilies. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomato paste starts to caramelize and turn a deeper red, about 5 minutes.
    • Stir in the gin and cook until fully evaporated, about 1 minute.
    • In a small measuring cup, stir 1/4 cup of the hot pasta water into the cream to temper it (this warms the cream so it doesn't break the sauce). Stir the tempered cream into the sauce.
    • Stir in the Parmesan. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
  4. Cook the pasta: Add the lasagna sheets to the boiling water, tearing them in half and separating them as you add them; stir to keep them from sticking. Cook about 1 minute less than the package directions. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
  5. Add the noodles and the remaining tomatoes to the pot of sauce. Return to medium heat and cook, stirring gently so as not to break up the noodles, until the tomatoes just begin to wilt, 1 to 2 minutes. Loosen with pasta water as needed.
  6. Divide among bowls; top with basil, a drizzle of olive oil, and more Parmesan.

Artichoke Pesto Pasta with Fried Peppercorns

4 | Total: 30 minutes

The fried peppercorns are worth making extra of — Molly Baz notes they're a great crispy, spicy garnish on all sorts of dishes.

Source: The Club, by Molly Baz

Ingredients

Prep

  • 2 to 3 lemons (1 1/2 for peel and juice; remaining 1/2 to 1 lemon reserved for finishing)
  • 1 large bunch flat-leaf parsley, leaves and tender stems picked (about 2 cups packed)
  • 1 large or 2 small garlic cloves
  • 2 ounces Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated (about 3/4 cup), divided
  • One 14.5- to 16-ounce jar marinated artichokes (preferably Mezzetta), drained, brine reserved

Pesto

  • 1/3 cup olive oil
  • 3/4 cup (2 ounces) blanched almonds
  • 2 teaspoons kosher salt

Pasta

  • 1 pound mezzi rigatoni
  • Kosher salt, for the pasta water

Fried peppercorns

  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 2 tablespoons black peppercorns
  • Kosher salt, to taste

To finish

  • One 8-ounce ball burrata
  • More grated Parmigiano-Reggiano

Steps

  1. Prep: Remove the peel from 1 1/2 lemons in long strips with a vegetable peeler; squeeze 1/4 cup juice from the lemons (reserve more lemon for finishing).
  2. Pesto: In a food processor, process the lemon peels until finely chopped. Add the parsley and process until roughly chopped. Add the garlic, artichokes, artichoke brine, olive oil, almonds, half the Parmesan, and the salt; process until a coarse pesto forms. Taste; add lemon juice if needed.
  3. Cook the pasta: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil. Add the rigatoni and cook to al dente, 1 to 2 minutes less than the package directions. Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain.
  4. Fried peppercorns (meanwhile, as the pasta boils):
    • Add the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil to your smallest skillet. When shimmering, add the peppercorns. Toast, swirling the pan, until fragrant and slightly darkened, about 2 minutes.
    • Remove from heat and let rest in the oil until they stop popping. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate with a slotted spoon.
    • Let cool, then roughly chop. Season generously with salt.
  5. Plate it up: Return the pasta to the pot and add the pesto. Set over medium-low heat. Add 1/2 cup of the reserved pasta water and the remaining Parmesan; toss vigorously until the sauce emulsifies and coats the pasta. Add more pasta water or lemon juice to loosen if needed.
  6. Divide among plates and top with torn burrata, a final grating of Parmesan, and the fried peppercorns.

★ Lemon Fusilli with Arugula

4 to 5 | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 30 minutes | Total: 40 minutes

Source: Food Network, by Ina Garten, from Barefoot Contessa at Home

Ingredients

Lemon cream sauce

  • 1 tablespoon good olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon minced garlic (2 cloves)
  • 2 cups heavy cream
  • Zest and juice of 2 lemons
  • Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

Broccoli

  • 1 bunch broccoli, cut into florets

Pasta

  • 1 pound dried fusilli pasta

To finish

  • 1/2 pound baby arugula (or 2 bunches common arugula, leaves cut in thirds)
  • 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan
  • 1 pint grape or cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 1 remaining lemon, sliced 1/4-inch thick

Steps

  1. Lemon cream sauce: Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat; add the garlic and cook 60 seconds. Add the cream and bring to a boil. Add the lemon zest and juice; simmer over low heat until thickened, about 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
  2. Meanwhile, cook the broccoli florets in a pot of boiling salted water 3 to 5 minutes, until tender but still firm. Drain and set aside.
  3. Pasta:
    • Bring a large pot of water to a boil; add 1 tablespoon salt and the pasta. Cook according to the package directions, about 12 minutes. Drain.
    • Return the pasta to the pot. Immediately add the cream mixture and cook over medium-low heat 3 minutes, until most of the sauce is absorbed.
  4. Pour the hot pasta into a large bowl; add the arugula, Parmesan, tomatoes, and cooked broccoli.
  5. Cut the remaining lemon in half lengthwise, slice 1/4-inch thick crosswise, and add to the pasta.
  6. Toss well, season to taste, and serve hot.

Christy's Pesto (Adapted)

Six 2-person servings

Walnuts can be swapped for pine nuts or pecans, or a mix of the two.

Source: Family recipe card ("Christy's Pesto, Adapted")

Ingredients

  • 6 cloves garlic
  • 4 cups fresh basil leaves (about 2 bunches, stemmed)
  • 3/4 cup olive oil
  • 1 cup chopped walnuts
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese
  • 1 tablespoon warm water

Steps

  1. Mince the garlic in a food processor.
  2. Add the basil and pulse until finely chopped.
  3. With the processor running, add the olive oil, walnuts, salt, Parmesan, and warm water; process until smooth.
  4. Portion into individual packages (3 heaping tablespoons each) and freeze.

Italian

Brie Linguine

6 | Prep: 15 minutes, plus 2–3 hours resting

A very intense pasta, best served as a side dish.
Flavored fresh pasta — red pepper, basil, or spinach — provides wonderful color and taste.

Source: More Than a Tea Party (cookbook), Brunch and Luncheon chapter, p. 105

Ingredients

Sauce (2–3 hours ahead)

  • 4 large, ripe tomatoes, peeled and coarsely chopped
  • 1 small red onion, coarsely chopped
  • 3 garlic cloves, finely minced
  • 1/2–3/4 cup fresh basil leaves, well washed and dried
  • 1/2 cup olive oil
  • 3/4 pound Brie cheese, rind removed and broken into chunks
  • 2 ounces Prosciutto, cut into thin strips
  • 1–2 teaspoons salt
  • 1–2 teaspoons freshly ground black pepper
  • 4 sun-dried tomatoes, well-chopped (optional)

Pasta

  • 1 pound linguine

Garnish

  • Freshly grated Parmesan cheese

Steps

  1. Sauce: In a large bowl, mix together the tomatoes, onion, garlic, basil, olive oil, Brie, Prosciutto, salt, pepper, and sun-dried tomatoes (if using). Cover and let sit at room temperature for at least 2–3 hours before serving.
  2. Cook linguine in boiling salted water until al dente. Drain.
  3. Toss pasta with tomato-Brie mixture, correct seasoning, and garnish generously with Parmesan. Serve immediately.

★ Pasta with Sausage, Basil, and Mustard

Serves 4 | Active: 10 min | Total: 20 min

Source: Nigel Slater, Food & Wine (September 2002)

Ingredients

Pasta

  • 1 lb penne, rigatoni, or medium shells

Sausage + sauce

  • 1 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • 8 hot Italian sausage links, casings removed, meat crumbled (about 1 1/2 lbs); or substitute one 1-lb roll sweet Italian or sage sausage (such as Jimmy Dean)
  • 3/4 cup dry white wine
  • 3/4 cup heavy cream
  • 3 Tbsp grainy mustard
  • Pinch of Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes

Finish

  • 1 cup fresh basil, thinly sliced

Steps

  1. Cook pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water until al dente. Drain.
  2. Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet over moderately high heat. Add sausage meat and brown, breaking up as it cooks, about 5 min.
  3. Add wine and simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, until reduced by half, about 5 min.
  4. Add cream, mustard, and Aleppo pepper; simmer 2 min.
  5. Remove from heat. Add drained pasta and basil; toss to coat. Serve immediately.

Nuala's Pasta

Serves 2–3

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Nuala O'Connor

Ingredients

Pasta

  • 1/2 lb tubular pasta (rigatoni or penne)

Ricotta sauce

  • 3/4 cup part-skim ricotta, at room temperature
  • 3 scallions, finely chopped
  • 1 tablespoon chopped parsley or fresh basil
  • 1/3 cup grated parmesan cheese
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg
  • Pinch cayenne pepper

Steps

  1. Bring ricotta to room temperature. Place in a large serving bowl.
  2. Add scallions, parsley or basil, grated parmesan, salt, nutmeg, and cayenne to ricotta; mix.
  3. Cook pasta. When ready, stir 1/4 cup pasta cooking water into the ricotta mixture. Drain pasta and toss with ricotta.

Three Cheese Manicotti

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Susan Muhlheim

Ingredients

Shells

  • 8 manicotti shells

Filling

  • 2 eggs, beaten
  • 1 cup shredded mozzarella
  • 1 1/2 cups ricotta cheese
  • 1/2 cup grated parmesan
  • 1/4 cup chopped parsley
  • 1/2 teaspoon oregano
  • Dash of pepper

Sauce and topping

  • Spaghetti sauce (jarred or homemade)
  • 1 cup shredded mozzarella (reserved for topping)

Steps

  1. Cook manicotti shells; rinse in cold water.
  2. Stir together eggs, 1 cup mozzarella, ricotta, parmesan, parsley, oregano, and pepper. Spoon filling into manicotti shells.
  3. Pour spaghetti sauce into the bottom of a rectangular baking dish (just cover the bottom). Arrange stuffed manicotti in dish. Pour remaining sauce over shells. Sprinkle reserved mozzarella on top.

Lisa's Pasta

Serves 4–6

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Lisa Sullivan; subtitled "Angel Hair Tomato Basil Toss"

Ingredients

Sauce base

  • 1/2 cup olive oil
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/4 cup sliced green onions

Tomatoes and herbs

  • 3 large tomatoes, peeled and diced
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon coarse ground black pepper

Pasta and finish

  • 1/2 lb angel hair pasta
  • Grated parmesan cheese, for serving

Steps

  1. In a large skillet, heat olive oil. Add garlic and green onions; stir-fry 1 minute.
  2. Stir in tomatoes, basil, salt, and pepper; cook 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
  3. Cook angel hair pasta; drain. Toss hot pasta with tomato mixture immediately. Serve sprinkled with parmesan.

Linguine with Clams and Wild Mushrooms

Serves 4

Ingredients

Mushrooms

  • 6 tablespoons olive oil (divided)
  • 1 lb mixed fresh wild mushrooms (oyster and/or shiitake), stems trimmed, caps sliced

Clams

  • 6 large garlic cloves, minced
  • 1/4 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 1 cup dry white wine
  • 5 lbs clams (about 24 littlenecks)

Finish

  • 1 lb linguine
  • 2 bunches fresh chives or 1 bunch green onions, chopped
  • Salt and pepper to taste

Steps

  1. Heat 3 tablespoons oil over high heat. Saute mushrooms until beginning to brown, about 5 minutes. Transfer to plate using slotted spoon.
  2. Add remaining 3 tablespoons oil and garlic to pot. Saute until tender, about 3 minutes.
  3. Add Aleppo pepper, then wine and clams. Cover and cook until clams open, about 8 minutes.
  4. Cook linguine in a large pot of boiling salted water until just tender but firm to bite. Drain and transfer to large bowl.
  5. Spoon mushrooms over pasta, then top with clam mixture, discarding any unopened clams. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with chives.

Linguine with Mussels

Ingredients

Aromatics

  • 2 teaspoons olive oil
  • 1/2 cup chopped fennel bulb
  • 1/2 cup finely chopped onion
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced

Sauce

  • 1 cup diced tomato
  • 1 cup dry vermouth
  • 3 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
  • 1 tablespoon tomato paste
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/8 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes

Finish

  • 28 fresh mussels, scrubbed and debearded
  • 2 tablespoons water
  • 2 teaspoons cornstarch
  • 2 cups hot cooked linguine (about 4 oz uncooked)

Steps

  1. Heat oil over medium heat. Add fennel, onion, and garlic; saute 5 minutes.
  2. Add sauce ingredients and bring to boil.
  3. Add mussels, cover, and cook 3 minutes until shells open. Remove from heat. Discard any unopened shells. Reserve 10 shells with meat intact; remove meat from the rest.
  4. Combine water and cornstarch; add to tomato mixture and boil 2 minutes, stirring.
  5. Serve 1 cup pasta per plate topped with 1 cup sauce and 5 mussels in shells.

Middle Eastern/Persian

Spiced Meatballs with Pappardelle

Serves 4 | Total: 1 hr 15 min

Source: Molly Baz, The Club

Ingredients

Sauce

  • 3 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 1 large yellow onion, finely chopped
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 1 tsp Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 1 (28-oz) can crushed tomatoes
  • 2 Tbsp red wine vinegar
  • Kosher salt

Meatball mixture

  • 1 large egg
  • 2 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • 1 cup panko breadcrumbs
  • 1 1/2 tsp garam masala (or baharat or hawaij)
  • 1 1/2 tsp ground turmeric
  • 1 Tbsp kosher salt, plus more
  • 1/3 cup golden raisins or currants
  • 3 garlic cloves, finely grated
  • 1 bunch dill, coarsely chopped (reserve a handful for garnish)
  • 1 bunch cilantro, coarsely chopped (reserve a handful for garnish)

Beef

  • 1 lb ground beef (80/20)

Finish

  • 1/2 cup water
  • 1 Tbsp unsalted butter
  • 1 lb fresh pappardelle or other fresh long pasta

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F. In a large Dutch oven over medium heat, melt 3 Tbsp butter. Add onion, cinnamon stick, Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, and a big pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, until onions begin to soften, 5–6 minutes. Add crushed tomatoes and red wine vinegar. Cover with a tight-fitting lid and transfer to oven for 20 minutes.
  2. Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk together egg and olive oil. Add panko, garam masala, turmeric, salt, raisins, and grated garlic; mix well. Coarsely chop dill and cilantro (reserving a handful of each for garnish) and stir into the panko mixture. Scoop out 3/4 cup of this mixture and spread on a small rimmed baking sheet; toast in the oven until golden and crisp, stirring once, 9–14 minutes. Let cool. (These are your breadcrumbs.)
  3. Add ground beef to the remaining panko mixture and work with your hands until evenly combined. Divide into 8 equal portions and roll into balls.
  4. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Remove Dutch oven from oven, uncover, and stir in 1/2 cup water. Nestle meatballs in the sauce, turning once to coat. Return lid slightly ajar and bake until meatballs are just cooked through and bouncy, 12–16 minutes. Remove from oven and keep covered.
  5. Transfer meatballs to a plate. Cook pappardelle per package directions until just al dente. Use tongs to transfer pasta into the sauce, add 1 Tbsp butter, and toss to coat, adding pasta water as needed. Divide pasta and sauce among bowls, top with meatballs, toasted breadcrumbs, and fresh herbs.

Asian

Thai

Fried Drunken Noodles with Chicken (Phad Kii Maw Gai)

Serves 6

Scaled to 6 servings. The book's original recipe listed "serves 4" but the full quantities were more consistent with 10–12; this is half of the full recipe.
Krachai (also called fingerroot or lesser ginger) is a Thai rhizome available at Asian grocery stores. Substitute extra fresh ginger in a pinch.
Use holy basil (Thai holy basil / bai krapao), which is distinct from Thai sweet basil.
Adjust chilli quantity to taste — the recipe is designed to be quite spicy.

Source: "A Passion for Thai Cooking" by Sompon and Elizabeth Nabnian, p. 69

Ingredients

Aromatics

  • 90ml (6 tablespoons) vegetable oil, divided
  • 5 cloves garlic, roughly chopped
  • 2 shallots, roughly chopped
  • 1 big green chilli, sliced
  • 1 big red chilli, sliced
  • 3 medium chillies, roughly chopped

Chicken and aromatics

  • 150g (5 oz) chicken, thinly sliced
  • 30g (1 oz) krachai (fingerroot / lesser ginger), shredded
  • 10g fresh young green peppercorns
  • 15g (1/2 oz) dried shrimps

Vegetables

  • 1 small tomato, cut into wedges
  • 3–4 long beans, sliced
  • 2 baby corn, each sliced into 3
  • 75g (2-1/2 oz) straw mushrooms, quartered
  • 50g (1-3/4 oz) carrots, sliced

Noodles and eggs

  • 175g (6 oz) large flat rice noodles
  • 1/4 teaspoon sweet soy sauce
  • 2 eggs, beaten

Sauce

  • 30ml (2 tablespoons) oyster sauce
  • 15ml (1 tablespoon) soy sauce
  • 30ml (2 tablespoons) fish sauce
  • 1/4 teaspoon sugar

Finish

  • 50g (1-3/4 oz) peanuts, roasted and crushed
  • 15g holy basil leaves

Steps

  1. Heat 30ml (2 tablespoons) of the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the garlic, shallots, and all the chillies; fry for 1 minute.
  2. Add the chicken; stir-fry until the outside turns white, 2–3 minutes.
  3. Add the krachai, green peppercorns, and dried shrimps; stir-fry for 2 more minutes.
  4. Turn the heat down. Add the tomato, long beans, baby corn, mushrooms, and carrots; cook 3 minutes. Turn off the heat and set the vegetable mixture aside.
  5. Heat the remaining oil in the wok over high heat. Add the noodles and sweet soy sauce; stir-fry 1 minute, stirring continuously. Turn the heat down, add the eggs, and stir to cook.
  6. Add the reserved vegetable-and-chicken mixture; stir over high heat to combine. Add the sauce and stir-fry to combine.
  7. Add the peanuts and basil leaves, stir once, and serve.

Japanese

Stir-Fried Udon Noodles With Pork and Scallions

Serves 4 | Total: 25 min

Source: Claire Saffitz, Bon Appétit (April 2019)

Ingredients

Noodles + cabbage

  • 4 cups very coarsely chopped green cabbage (about 1/4 medium head)
  • 2 (7-oz.) packages instant udon noodles, flavor packets discarded

Stir-fry

  • 2 Tbsp vegetable oil, divided
  • 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  • 8 oz ground pork
  • 5 scallions, white and pale green parts coarsely chopped, dark green parts thinly sliced (kept separate)
  • 2 tsp finely grated peeled ginger
  • 1 tsp Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes
  • 1/3 cup mirin (sweet Japanese rice wine)
  • 1/3 cup soy sauce
  • 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds, plus more for serving

Steps

  1. Heat 1 Tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook cabbage, tossing often, until edges are browned, about 4 min. Reduce heat to low and continue cooking until thickest parts are tender, about 4 min more. Remove from heat.
  2. Place udon noodles in a large heatproof bowl; cover with 6 cups boiling water. Let sit 1 minute, stirring to separate, then drain. Toss noodles with sesame oil. Add reserved cabbage to bowl.
  3. Wipe out skillet. Heat remaining 1 Tbsp vegetable oil over medium-high. Add pork, spreading across the pan; cook undisturbed until underside is browned, about 3 min. Break up meat and continue cooking until no longer pink, about 1 min. Add scallion whites and pale greens, ginger, and Aleppo pepper; cook, tossing, until scallions soften and skillet starts to brown, about 1 min.
  4. Add noodle-cabbage mixture, mirin, and soy sauce. Cook, tossing constantly and scraping up browned bits, until noodles are coated, about 45 seconds. Remove from heat; toss in dark scallion greens and 1 Tbsp sesame seeds.
  5. Divide among bowls and top with more sesame seeds.

Baking

Savory

General

72-Hour Pizza Dough

Makes 3 pizzas (~283g each)

Source: The Gourmandise School (The Pizza Class)

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

  • 350 ml water
  • ½ Tbsp dry yeast
  • 500g bread flour (or strong all-purpose, like King Arthur)
  • 3 tsps kosher salt (Diamond Crystal preferred)
  • 350 ml water
  • 1 teaspoon dry yeast
  • 500g bread flour (or strong all-purpose, like King Arthur)
  • 3 tsps kosher salt (Diamond Crystal preferred)

Steps

  1. In a large bowl, combine the water and yeast. Add the flour and salt and mix with one hand until it just forms a smooth dough. Cover and let rise at room temperature for 12–24 hours. It will nearly double in size.
  2. After this initial ferment, place the dough in the fridge for another 12–48 hours.
  3. Remove the dough from the fridge and lightly flour your counter. Divide the dough into 3 portions of about 283 grams each. Gently purse one of your dough balls so that just one seam at the bottom of the dough remains, much like a balloon you'd blow into.
  4. Move to a part of your counter that is un-floured and give the dough a gentle rub, seam side down, on that area. Place the dough ball on a floured part of the counter to rest for 4 hours (closer to 3½ hours on a warm day). Repeat with the remaining dough balls; once all have been pre-shaped, lightly flour the tops and cover them. Place them a couple of inches apart to give them room to get slack again.
  5. Preheat your oven to 450°F with a baking steel or pizza stone inside. For best results, preheat for at least 45 minutes to 1 hour. Alternatively, if using a pizza oven (e.g. Ooni), preheat according to its instructions until it reaches 700–900°F.
  6. Shape your pizzas most of the way before placing them on a floured peel or baking sheet turned upside-down. Just before baking, place the pizza on the peel, finish stretching it, and add toppings. For a conventional oven: move the pizza to the stone or steel by tilting the peel slightly, shoving the pizza forward and jerking back to release it onto the hot surface. For a pizza oven: launch directly onto the hot stone and bake for 60–90 seconds, rotating once halfway through.
  1. In a large bowl, combine the water and yeast. Add the flour and salt and mix with one hand until it just forms a smooth dough. Cover and let rise at room temperature for 8–18 hours. At altitude the dough rises roughly 25–40% faster — start checking at 8 hours; you want it nearly doubled but not over-proofed and collapsing.
  2. After this initial ferment, place the dough in the fridge for another 12–48 hours.
  3. Remove the dough from the fridge and lightly flour your counter. Divide the dough into 3 portions of about 283 grams each. Gently purse one of your dough balls so that just one seam at the bottom of the dough remains, much like a balloon you’d blow into.
  4. Move to a part of your counter that is un-floured and give the dough a gentle rub, seam side down, on that area. Place the dough ball on a floured part of the counter to rest for 3–3.5 hours (closer to 3 hours on a warm day; check at 2.5 hours). Repeat with the remaining dough balls; once all have been pre-shaped, lightly flour the tops and cover them. Place them a couple of inches apart to give them room to get slack again.
  5. Preheat your oven to 450°F with a baking steel or pizza stone inside. For best results, preheat for at least 45 minutes to 1 hour. Alternatively, if using a pizza oven (e.g. Ooni), preheat according to its instructions until it reaches 700–900°F.
  6. Shape your pizzas most of the way before placing them on a floured peel or baking sheet turned upside-down. Just before baking, place the pizza on the peel, finish stretching it, and add toppings. For a conventional oven: move the pizza to the stone or steel by tilting the peel slightly, shoving the pizza forward and jerking back to release it onto the hot surface. For a pizza oven: launch directly onto the hot stone and bake for 60–90 seconds, rotating once halfway through.

Italian

Susan's Calzones

Serves 4

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Susan

Ingredients

Dough (5 hours ahead)

  • 12 Rhodes frozen dinner rolls (3 per person), defrosted and risen

Filling

  • 1 lb ground beef or ground turkey
  • About 1/2 cup spaghetti sauce, or enough to hold filling together

Cheese

  • 1 cup shredded mozzarella
  • 1/2 cup grated parmesan

Add-ins (optional)

  • Sliced olives
  • Pepperoni
  • Sautéed mushrooms

Topping (optional)

  • Additional spaghetti sauce
  • Additional grated parmesan

Steps

  1. Defrost rolls at room temperature and let rise until doubled, about 5 hours (or per package directions).
  2. Brown ground beef or turkey in a skillet over medium heat; drain fat.
  3. Mix browned meat with spaghetti sauce (enough to hold the mixture together but not soupy), mozzarella, and parmesan. Stir in any optional add-ins.
  4. On a lightly floured surface, press each group of 3 risen rolls together and roll into a rough square.
  5. Spoon filling onto one half of each square. Fold dough over to form a triangle. Press edges firmly with fork tines to seal.
  6. Place on a baking sheet. Bake at 350°F for 18 minutes.
  7. Optional: 10 minutes in, spoon additional spaghetti sauce over the top and sprinkle with parmesan; return to oven for remaining 8 minutes.

Sweet

General

Butter Pecan Coffee Cake

Serves 12–16

The key technique: butter and pecans go into the Bundt pan during preheat, so they melt and toast before the batter goes in. Invert immediately after baking so the caramelized pecan layer becomes the topping.
Vanilla-butter-nut flavoring can substitute for the vanilla and butter flavoring — use 3 tsp. Alternatively, use 2 tsp pure vanilla with no butter flavoring.

The key technique: butter and pecans go into the Bundt pan during preheat, so they melt and toast before the batter goes in. Invert immediately after baking so the caramelized pecan layer becomes the topping.
Vanilla-butter-nut flavoring can substitute for the vanilla and butter flavoring — use 3 tsp. Alternatively, use 2 tsp pure vanilla with no butter flavoring.

Source: Family recipe card

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Pan base

  • 1 stick (8 T) butter or margarine
  • 1 cup pecans

Batter

  • 1 package Duncan Hines yellow cake mix
  • 1 package Jell-O instant vanilla pudding
  • 3/4 cup vegetable oil
  • 3/4 cup water
  • 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
  • 1 tsp butter flavoring (or use 2 tsp pure vanilla with no butter flavoring)

Eggs

  • 4 large eggs, beaten

Cinnamon swirl

  • 2 tsp cinnamon
  • 1/2 cup sugar
  • 1/2 cup pecans

Pan base

  • 1 stick (8 T) butter or margarine
  • 1 cup pecans

Batter

  • 1 package Duncan Hines yellow cake mix
  • 1 package Jell-O instant vanilla pudding
  • 3/4 cup vegetable oil
  • 3/4 cup + 2 tablespoons water
  • 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
  • 1 tsp butter flavoring

Eggs

  • 4 large eggs, beaten

Cinnamon swirl

  • 2 tsp cinnamon
  • 7 tablespoons sugar
  • 1/2 cup pecans

Steps

  1. Grease and flour a Bundt pan. Place butter and 1 cup pecans in the bottom.
  2. Place pan in oven while it preheats to 350°F; leave for 6 minutes, so the butter melts and pecans toast slightly.
  3. Meanwhile, in a large mixing bowl, combine cake mix, pudding mix, oil, water, vanilla, and butter flavoring. Beat to combine.
  4. Beat eggs separately, then add to batter while mixing. Beat until smooth.
  5. Remove pan from oven after 6 minutes. Pour half the batter over the pecan-butter base.
  6. Mix together cinnamon, sugar, and 1/2 cup pecans. Sprinkle evenly over batter layer.
  7. Pour remaining batter on top. Gently swirl the surface with a knife without disturbing the bottom layer.
  8. Bake at 350°F for 60 minutes.
  9. Immediately invert onto a serving plate. Remove pan — the caramelized pecan layer will now be on top.

  2. Place pan in oven while it preheats to 375°F; leave for 6 minutes, so the butter melts and pecans toast slightly.
  3. Meanwhile, in a large mixing bowl, combine cake mix, pudding mix, oil, water, vanilla, and butter flavoring. Beat to combine.
  4. Beat eggs separately, then add to batter while mixing. Beat until smooth.
  5. Remove pan from oven after 6 minutes. Pour half the batter over the pecan-butter base.
  6. Mix together cinnamon, sugar, and 1/2 cup pecans. Sprinkle evenly over batter layer.
  7. Pour remaining batter on top. Gently swirl the surface with a knife without disturbing the bottom layer.
  8. Bake at 375°F for 50–55 minutes (check at 50 minutes with a toothpick).
  9. Immediately invert onto a serving plate. Remove pan — the caramelized pecan layer will now be on top.

Eric's Chocolate Chip Cookies

About 3 dozen cookies

Based on the classic Toll House chocolate chip cookie recipe, with a few of Eric's own touches — rolled oats and roughly chopped pecans.

Based on the classic Toll House chocolate chip cookie recipe, with a few of Eric’s own touches — rolled oats and roughly chopped pecans.

Source: Base recipe: Nestlé Toll House (https://www.verybestbaking.com/toll-house/recipes/chocolate-chip-cookies/)

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Dry ingredients

  • 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup rolled quick oats
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon salt

Creamed base

  • 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  • 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 3/4 cup packed brown sugar

Added to the creamed base

  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 2 large eggs

Folded in

  • 2 cups (12 ounces) semisweet chocolate chips
  • 1 cup pecans, very roughly chopped into big pieces

Dry ingredients

  • 2 1/4 cups + 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup rolled quick oats
  • 3/4 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon salt

Creamed base

  • 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  • 11 tablespoons granulated sugar
  • 11 tablespoons packed brown sugar

Added to the creamed base

  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 2 large eggs

Folded in

  • 2 cups (12 ounces) semisweet chocolate chips
  • 1 cup pecans, very roughly chopped into big pieces

Steps

  1. Whisk together the flour, oats, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl; set aside.
  2. Cream the butter and sugars: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar on medium-high speed until pale and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes.
  3. Add the vanilla and eggs; continue beating on medium speed until fully incorporated and the mixture looks well emulsified.
  4. With the mixer on low speed (or by hand), add the flour mixture and mix just until no dry streaks remain — the dough should be stiff.
  5. Fold in the chocolate chips and pecans by hand.
  6. Cover and refrigerate the dough for at least 1 hour (and up to 2 days) to firm up before baking.
  7. When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line baking sheets with parchment.
  8. Using an ice cream scoop, portion generous mounds of dough onto the prepared sheets, spacing them a few inches apart.
  9. Bake 11-13 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the centers still look slightly underbaked. Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring.
  1. Whisk together the flour, oats, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl; set aside.
  2. Cream the butter and sugars: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar on medium-high speed until pale and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes.
  3. Add the vanilla and eggs; continue beating on medium speed until fully incorporated and the mixture looks well emulsified.
  4. With the mixer on low speed (or by hand), add the flour mixture and mix just until no dry streaks remain — the dough should be stiff.
  5. Fold in the chocolate chips and pecans by hand.
  6. Cover and refrigerate the dough for at least 1 hour (and up to 2 days) to firm up before baking.

  8. Using an ice cream scoop, portion generous mounds of dough onto the prepared sheets, spacing them a few inches apart.
  9. Bake 10–12 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the centers still look slightly underbaked. (Check at 10 minutes — at altitude cookies spread faster and finish sooner.) Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring.

Chocolate "Birthday Cake"

One large sheet cake or a 2-layer 9-inch cake | Cook: 40-45 minutes

For a single layer, halve the butter, sugar, chocolate, flour, baking soda, salt, vanilla, and water as noted below. For 1 1/2 eggs: whisk 2 eggs together and use 3/4 of the mixture.
Don't halve the frosting, even for a single layer — a full batch is right (a half batch isn't quite enough).

For a single layer, halve all cake ingredients as noted in the standard recipe. The single-layer proportions given in the original apply — reduce each adjusted amount by half in the same way.
Don’t halve the frosting, even for a single layer — a full batch is right (a half batch isn’t quite enough).

Source: Family recipe card written by Grandmother Brenda; the single-layer/half-batch margin annotations are from Lauren

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Creamed base

  • 1 cup (2 sticks) butter [1 stick]
  • 2 cups sugar [1 cup]
  • 3 eggs [1 1/2 eggs]
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla [1 teaspoon]

Chocolate

  • 4 oz unsweetened chocolate [2 oz]

Dry ingredients

  • 2 2/3 cups flour [1 1/3 cups]
  • 2 teaspoons baking soda [1 teaspoon]
  • 1 teaspoon salt [1/2 teaspoon]

Liquid

  • Up to 2 cups water, added gradually as needed [up to 1 cup]

Frosting

  • 2 cups confectioners' sugar (be generous — you may want more)
  • 3/4 cup butter
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 2-3 oz unsweetened chocolate, melted

Creamed base

  • 1 cup (2 sticks) butter [1/2 stick for half batch]
  • 1 3/4 cups sugar [7/8 cup for half batch]
  • 3 eggs [1 1/2 eggs]
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla [1 teaspoon]

Chocolate

  • 4 oz unsweetened chocolate [2 oz]

Dry ingredients

  • 2 3/4 cups flour [1 3/8 cups]
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons baking soda [3/4 teaspoon]
  • 1 teaspoon salt [1/2 teaspoon]

Liquid

  • Up to 2 cups water, use the full amount [up to 1 cup for half batch]

Frosting

  • 2 cups confectioners’ sugar
  • 3/4 cup butter
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 2–3 oz unsweetened chocolate, melted

Steps

  1. Cream the butter; add the sugar, then the eggs and vanilla, beating well after each addition.
  2. Melt the chocolate in the microwave (20-30 second bursts, stirring between, until smooth) and add to the creamed mixture.
  3. Sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt.
  4. Add the flour mixture to the creamed mixture alternately with the water, mixing just until combined. You likely won't need the full 2 cups of water — add enough to make a smooth, pourable batter.
  5. Bake in a large buttered pan, or two buttered 9-inch round layer pans, for 40-45 minutes at 325°F.
  6. Frost after the layer(s) are completely cool, on a baking rack.
  7. Frosting: Cream the confectioners' sugar with the butter until smooth. Add the vanilla and beat well.
  8. Melt the 2-3 oz chocolate and add to the frosting; mix until smooth. Add a bit more confectioners' sugar if needed to reach a spreadable consistency.
  9. Spread over the cooled cake.
  1. Cream the butter; add the sugar, then the eggs and vanilla, beating well after each addition.
  2. Melt the chocolate in the microwave (20–30 second bursts, stirring between, until smooth) and add to the creamed mixture.
  3. Sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt.
  4. Add the flour mixture to the creamed mixture alternately with the water, mixing just until combined. At altitude, use the full 2 cups of water (evaporation is faster and the batter needs the moisture).
  5. Bake in a large buttered pan, or two buttered 9-inch round layer pans, for 35–40 minutes at 375°F. Start checking at 33 minutes.
  6. Frost after the layer(s) are completely cool, on a baking rack.

  8. Melt the 2–3 oz chocolate and add to the frosting; mix until smooth. Add a bit more confectioners’ sugar if needed to reach a spreadable consistency.
  9. Spread over the cooled cake.

Jumbo Banana-Nut Muffins

Makes 12 muffins

Recipe scaled 1.5x from original (from 9 jumbo muffins to 12). Walnuts made optional.
1 cup mashed ripe banana ≈ 2 medium bananas.

Recipe scaled 1.5x from original (from 9 jumbo muffins to 12). Walnuts made optional.
1 cup mashed ripe banana = about 2 medium bananas.

Source: Mostly Muffins (cookbook), p. 14

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Dry ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 1/2 cups whole-wheat flour
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons baking soda
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Wet base

  • 3/4 cup lightly salted butter or margarine, softened
  • 3/4 cup sugar

Eggs

  • 3 eggs

Wet additions

  • 2 cups mashed ripe banana (about 4 medium bananas)
  • 6 tablespoons (3/8 cup) milk
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla

Walnuts (optional)

  • 3/4 cup broken walnuts (optional)

Dry ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 1/2 cups whole-wheat flour
  • 1 1/4 teaspoons baking powder
  • 1 1/4 teaspoons baking soda
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Wet base

  • 3/4 cup lightly salted butter or margarine, softened
  • 10 tablespoons sugar

Eggs

  • 3 eggs

Wet additions

  • 2 cups mashed ripe banana (about 4 medium bananas)
  • 1/2 cup milk
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla

Walnuts (optional)

  • 3/4 cup broken walnuts (optional)

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease muffin cups and the edges surrounding the cups.
  2. In a large bowl, stir together the flours, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
  3. In another bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy; beat in eggs. Stir in banana, milk, and vanilla.
  4. Add dry ingredients to wet mixture and stir just to combine. Fold in walnuts if using.
  5. Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups; bake 25 to 30 minutes or until a cake tester inserted in the center comes out clean.
  6. Remove muffin tin(s) to wire rack. Cool 5 minutes before removing muffins from cups; finish cooling on rack. Serve warm or store in an airtight container at room temperature. These muffins freeze well.
  1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Grease muffin cups and the edges surrounding the cups.
  2. In a large bowl, stir together the flours, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
  3. In another bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy; beat in eggs. Stir in banana, milk, and vanilla.
  4. Add dry ingredients to wet mixture and stir just to combine. Fold in walnuts if using.
  5. Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups; bake 22–27 minutes or until a cake tester inserted in the center comes out clean. (Check at 22 minutes — the higher temp means they finish faster.)
  6. Remove muffin tin(s) to wire rack. Cool 5 minutes before removing muffins from cups; finish cooling on rack. Serve warm or store in an airtight container at room temperature. These muffins freeze well.

★ Nana's Poundcake

1 loaf or bundt cake | Cook: 90 minutes

A four-generation family recipe.

A four-generation family recipe.

Source: Family recipe, credited to Nana, via Lauren's blog post "Nana's Poundcake, Food, and Cultural Connection"

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Cake

  • 1/2 pound salted butter (2 sticks), softened
  • 1 3/4 cups sugar
  • 5 eggs

  • 2 tablespoons vanilla

Cake

  • 1/2 pound salted butter (2 sticks), softened

  1. Cream the butter and sugar.

Filled Coffee Cake

Serves 12–16 | Bake: 350–375°F for 30–40 minutes

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Nana Regina (card reads "delicious! Mother's")

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Cake batter

  • 1/2 cup butter, softened (or margarine)
  • 2 cups sugar
  • 4 eggs, well beaten
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 3 cups flour
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup milk

Filling

  • 1 cup brown sugar
  • 1 cup nuts, chopped
  • 2 tablespoons butter
  • 2 tablespoons flour
  • 1 teaspoon cinnamon

Cake batter

  • 1/2 cup butter, softened (or margarine)
  • 1 3/4 cups sugar
  • 4 eggs, well beaten
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 3 cups flour
  • 1 3/4 teaspoons baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup + 2 tablespoons milk

Filling

  • 14 tablespoons (7/8 cup) brown sugar
  • 1 cup nuts, chopped
  • 2 tablespoons butter
  • 2 tablespoons flour
  • 1 teaspoon cinnamon

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350–375°F. Grease a 9x13 pan (or tube pan).
  2. Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add well-beaten eggs and vanilla; beat well.
  3. Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl.
  4. Alternately add the flour mixture and the milk to the butter mixture in 3 additions each, beginning and ending with flour. Stir until just combined.
  5. Make filling: combine brown sugar, nuts, butter, flour, and cinnamon; mix until crumbly.
  6. Pour half the batter into the prepared pan. Spread the filling evenly over the batter. Pour remaining batter on top.
  7. Bake 30–40 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

Nut Butter Balls

About 4 dozen | Bake: 325°F for 25 minutes

Card notes 'double recipe' — these quantities are the base (single) recipe.

Source: Family recipe card (Grandmother Brenda's collection)

Ingredients

Dough

  • 2 cups flour
  • 1/4 cup sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 lb. (2 sticks) butter, softened
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla

Coating

  • 1 cup chopped nuts

Finish

  • Powdered sugar, for rolling

Steps
