Red Velvet Cake

One 6-layer cake | Bake: 350°F for 30 minutes

Uses a cooked ermine frosting (flour-and-milk based) rather than the cream cheese frosting common in modern versions.
The 2 oz. of red food coloring gives the classic deep red color.

Uses a cooked ermine frosting (flour-and-milk based) rather than the cream cheese frosting common in modern versions.
The 2 oz. of red food coloring gives the classic deep red color.

Source: Family recipe card (Grandmother Brenda; card noted as "original on paper yellow with age")

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Cocoa paste

  • 3 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder (Dutch-process; e.g. Nestlé Toll House Cocoa or Hershey's Special Dark)
  • 2 oz. red food coloring

Cake

  • 1/2 cup vegetable shortening
  • 1-3/4 cups sugar
  • 2 eggs, beaten
  • 1 cup buttermilk
  • 2-1/2 cups cake flour
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 tablespoon white vinegar

Frosting — Part 1 (cool completely before using)

  • 5 tablespoons flour
  • 1 cup milk

Frosting — Part 2

  • 1/2 cup butter, softened
  • 1/2 cup vegetable shortening
  • 1 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 tablespoons vanilla

Cocoa paste

  • 3 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder (Dutch-process; e.g. Nestle Toll House Cocoa or Hershey’s Special Dark)
  • 2 oz. red food coloring

Cake

  • 1/2 cup vegetable shortening
  • 1 2/3 cups sugar
  • 2 eggs, beaten
  • 1 cup + 2 tablespoons buttermilk
  • 2 1/2 cups + 2 tablespoons cake flour
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 3/4 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 tablespoon white vinegar

Frosting — Part 1 (cool completely before using)

  • 5 tablespoons flour
  • 1 cup milk

Frosting — Part 2

  • 1/2 cup butter, softened
  • 1/2 cup vegetable shortening
  • 14 tablespoons granulated sugar
  • 2 tablespoons vanilla

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour cake pans.
  2. In a small bowl, mix cocoa powder and red food coloring into a paste. Set aside.
  3. Cream shortening and sugar until light. Add beaten eggs; mix well. Add the cocoa-coloring paste; blend.
  4. Add salt and vanilla. Alternately add buttermilk and flour in 3 additions each, beginning and ending with flour. Mix well.
  5. Fold in baking soda and vinegar (the mixture will bubble slightly). Do not overmix.
  6. Pour into well-greased pans. Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes. Cool completely. Split each layer horizontally to make 6 thin layers total.
  7. Frosting Part 1: Cook flour and milk together in a saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly, until very thick (paste consistency). Set aside to cool completely.
  8. Frosting Part 2: Cream butter, shortening, and granulated sugar until light. Add vanilla. Add the cooled flour-milk paste to the creamed mixture. Beat at high speed until light and fluffy, like whipped cream.
  9. Frost between layers and on the outside of the cake.

Blintz Soufflé

Serves 6–8 | Bake: 350°F covered 1 hour, then uncovered 10 minutes

Marsha Firestone's smaller version — uses 2 packages of blintzes and a smaller casserole dish.
Frozen cheese blintzes from the store work perfectly.

Marsha Firestone’s smaller version — uses 2 packages of blintzes and a smaller casserole dish.
Frozen cheese blintzes from the store work perfectly.

Source: Family recipe, courtesy of Marsha Firestone (noted on card as smaller recipe for small casserole)

🏔 High altitude version

Ingredients

Pan and blintzes

  • 1 stick (1/2 cup) butter
  • 2 packages (about 12) frozen cheese blintzes

Custard

  • 6 eggs
  • 2/3 cup sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla
  • 1 teaspoon orange juice
  • 1-1/2 cups sour cream

Pan and blintzes

  • 1 stick (1/2 cup) butter
  • 2 packages (about 12) frozen cheese blintzes

Custard

  • 6 eggs
  • 9 tablespoons sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla
  • 1 teaspoon orange juice
  • 1 1/2 cups sour cream

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F.
  2. Melt butter in a casserole dish. Arrange frozen blintzes in a single layer on top.
  3. Beat eggs with sugar, vanilla, orange juice, and sour cream until smooth. Pour evenly over blintzes.

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
  2. Melt butter in a casserole dish. Arrange frozen blintzes in a single layer on top.
  3. Beat eggs with sugar, vanilla, orange juice, and sour cream until smooth. Pour evenly over blintzes.
  4. Bake covered at 375°F for 45–50 minutes.

★ Brenda's Noodle Kugel

Can be assembled up to 2 days ahead and refrigerated — hold the topping until ready to bake.

Source: Family recipe card, credited to Brenda

Ingredients

Noodles

  • 1 lb. extra-wide egg noodles

Filling (mix together)

  • 8 oz. cream cheese, softened
  • 1 cup sour cream
  • 1 stick (1/2 cup) butter, softened
  • 1/2 cup sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 3 eggs
  • 1 package golden raisins

Topping

  • 1/2 stick (1/4 cup) butter, melted
  • 1 1/2 cups corn flakes

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a large Pyrex casserole dish.
  2. Cook noodles according to package instructions. Drain thoroughly.
  3. Mix the filling ingredients together until combined, then fold in the drained noodles. Transfer to the prepared casserole.
  4. Bake uncovered at 350°F for 30–45 minutes. Remove from oven and let cool.
  5. Mix the melted butter with the corn flakes and spread over the cooled casserole.

Min Cohen's Inscrutable Apple Cake

Serves 8–10 | Bake: 375°F for 40–45 minutes

Grandmother Brenda wrote on the card: "I never made this because I do not understand it -- but Perhaps Renee will tell you -- It was a delicious cake!"
Steps reconstructed from the ingredient list and standard apple tart method.

Source: Mrs. Min Cohen's recipe, transcribed by Grandmother Brenda

Ingredients

Pastry (30–60 minutes ahead)

  • 2 cups flour
  • 3/4 cup vegetable shortening
  • 2 egg yolks
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 7 tablespoons cold water

Filling

  • 7–8 apples, sliced thin
  • 1 cup sugar
  • Lemon juice to taste
  • 1 teaspoon cinnamon

Glaze

  • 1 cup powdered sugar
  • 1 tablespoon flour
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 2 tablespoons milk

Steps

  1. Make pastry: combine flour and shortening; add egg yolks, salt, and cold water. Mix until just combined. Knead briefly, then refrigerate 30–60 minutes.
  2. Preheat oven to 375°F. Roll pastry out very thin. Use about 2/3 to line a baking pan; reserve the rest for the top.
  3. Make filling: toss sliced apples with sugar, a squeeze of lemon juice, and cinnamon.
  4. Spread apple filling over the pastry. Cover with remaining rolled-out pastry.
  5. Bake at 375°F for 40–45 minutes until golden.
  6. Make glaze: beat powdered sugar, flour, vanilla, and milk until smooth. Drizzle over warm cake.

American

Apple Pie

Makes 1 pie

Source: From Susan Muhlheim

Ingredients

Crust

  • 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/3 cup shortening
  • 3-4 tablespoons water

Filling

  • 5 apples of at least 3 different varieties, peeled and sliced into 8 pieces each
  • 3/4 cup brown sugar (divided)
  • 1/2 cup flour
  • 2 tablespoons margarine or butter

Steps

  1. Crust: Stir together flour and salt. Cut in shortening until pieces are the size of peas. Add water gradually, tossing with fork, until all is moistened. Roll out pastry to approximately 12" diameter on floured surface. Mold edges to pie plate.
  2. Toss sliced apples with 1/4 cup of the brown sugar. Arrange in pie crust.
  3. Combine remaining brown sugar and flour; cut in margarine until crumbly. Sprinkle mixture over apples.
  4. Bake at 375 for 40 minutes.

Regina's Coffee Cake

Source: Family recipe, attributed to great-grandmother Regina Pachter

Ingredients

Cake batter

  • 1 stick butter, room temperature
  • 1 cup sugar
  • 2 eggs
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 cup sour cream

Filling

  • 1/2 cup brown sugar
  • 1/2 cup chopped pecans

Brenda's Chocolate Chip Cookies

Dry

Wet

  • Salt and pepper

Steps

  1. Whisk together all ingredients in a small bowl until smooth. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Steak Seasoning Rub

Makes enough for 4 large steaks | Total: 5 min

We use a 3× batch for 2 racks of Sous Vide Beef Back Ribs.
Keeps in an airtight jar in a cool, dry place for up to 3 months.

Source: Sommer Collier, A Spicy Perspective

Ingredients

  • 1 Tbsp kosher salt
  • 1 Tbsp brown sugar, packed
  • 2 tsp smoked paprika
  • 2 tsp ground ancho chile pepper (or chili powder)
  • 1 tsp dried thyme
  • 1 tsp black pepper
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ½ tsp onion powder
  • ½ tsp ground mustard
  • ½ tsp ground cumin

Steps

  1. Mix all ingredients together in a small bowl until combined.
  2. Use immediately, or store in an airtight jar in a cool, dry place for up to 3 months. Rub generously over all sides of the meat before cooking; let rest at least 20 minutes before grilling or searing.

American

Creamy Louisiana Marinade

Makes about 7/8 cup; enough to marinate 1 1/2 lbs

Use with fish, seafood, poultry, veal, or vegetables.

Source: From Cheryl Zando

Ingredients

Marinade

  • 1/2 cup mayo
  • 1/2 teaspoon Creole or grainy mustard
  • 2 teaspoons fresh lemon juice
  • 2 green onions, green and white parts, minced
  • 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 teaspoon minced fresh rosemary (or 1/4 teaspoon dried)
  • 1 teaspoon minced fresh basil (or 1/4 teaspoon dried)
  • 1 teaspoon minced fresh oregano (or 1/4 teaspoon dried)
  • 1/2 teaspoon paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • 1/4 teaspoon cayenne
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Steps

  1. Mix all ingredients together. Make marinade one day ahead to allow flavors to blend.
  2. Coat food with marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 3 hours (better if overnight).

Latin/South American

Authentic Chimichurri

Serves 8 | Total: 10 min (ideally rests 2 hrs)

Source: Karina Carrel, Cafe Delites

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup olive oil
  • 2 Tbsp red wine vinegar
  • 1/2 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
  • 3–4 cloves garlic, finely chopped or minced
  • 2 small red chilies (or 1), deseeded and finely chopped (about 1 Tbsp)
  • 3/4 tsp dried oregano
  • 1 tsp coarse salt
  • 1/2 tsp pepper

Steps

  1. Finely chop garlic and chili.
  2. Mix all ingredients together in a bowl until well combined.
  3. Let sit at least 5–10 minutes before serving (ideally 2 hours for fuller flavor). Use to baste meats while grilling, or serve as a condiment.

Italian

Sun-Dried Tomato Cream Sauce

Increase garlic to taste.
Serve over pasta or chicken.

Source: Family recipe card

Ingredients

Roux

  • 1 tablespoon butter
  • 1 garlic clove, pushed through a press (increase to taste)
  • 2 tablespoons flour

Sauce

  • 3/4 cup chicken broth
  • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • 2 tablespoons sun-dried tomato slivers in oil
  • 1/4 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes

Steps

  1. In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds.
  2. Stir in flour and cook 1 minute.
  3. Stir in broth, cream, sun-dried tomatoes, thyme, salt, and Aleppo pepper. Bring to a boil and cook 1 minute.
  4. Pour into a measuring cup and serve over pasta or chicken.

French/Continental

Béarnaise Sauce

Makes about 3/4 cup

A typed clipping from Nana Regina's collection. Serve immediately — Béarnaise does not reheat well.

Source: Printed clipping, original source unknown (collected by Nana Regina)

Ingredients

Reduction

  • 1/4 cup dry white wine
  • 2 tablespoons white wine vinegar or sherry vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon minced shallot
  • 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt

Sauce

  • 4 teaspoons chopped fresh tarragon, divided
  • 3 egg yolks
  • 3/4 cup (1-1/2 sticks) unsalted butter, melted and kept warm
  • 1/8 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

Steps

  1. Make the reduction: combine wine, vinegar, shallot, and salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer; cook until reduced to about 1 tablespoon of liquid, 4–5 minutes. Cool slightly and strain through a fine-mesh strainer, pressing on the solids.
  2. Set up a double boiler: fill a medium pot with 2 inches of water and bring to a simmer. Rest a heatproof bowl over the pot. Add the strained reduction and egg yolks to the bowl.
  3. Whisk constantly until the mixture becomes pale, thick, and ribbony, about 2–3 minutes.
  4. Remove from heat. Whisking constantly, drizzle in warm melted butter in a very thin, slow stream until fully emulsified.
  5. Stir in 3 teaspoons of the chopped tarragon and the black pepper. Taste and adjust salt. Garnish with remaining 1 teaspoon tarragon.
  6. Serve immediately, or keep warm by setting the bowl over warm (not simmering) water.

Pickling

Dill Pickles

Makes 4 (8-oz) or 2 (16-oz) jars | Prep: 10 minutes | Chilling: 1–5 days

Chips are lightly pickled after 1 day; spears take 2 days. The best flavor develops around day 5 or 6 — worth the wait. Keep refrigerated for several weeks.

Source: https://www.loveandlemons.com/dill-pickles-recipe/

Ingredients

Cucumbers and aromatics

  • 12–14 Persian cucumbers, or 8–10 small pickling cucumbers
  • 4 garlic cloves, halved
  • 2 teaspoons mustard seeds
  • 2 teaspoons peppercorns
  • Fresh dill sprigs, a few per jar

Brine

  • 2 cups water
  • 2 cups distilled white vinegar
  • ¼ cup cane sugar
  • 2 tablespoons sea salt

Steps

  1. Prep the cucumbers: For spears, slice lengthwise into quarters. For chips, thinly slice crosswise.
  2. Pack the jars: Divide the cucumbers among 4 (8-oz) or 2 (16-oz) jars. Divide the garlic, mustard seeds, peppercorns, and dill sprigs evenly among the jars.
  3. Make the brine and fill:
    • Combine the water, vinegar, sugar, and salt in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar and salt dissolve, about 1 minute.
    • Let cool slightly, then pour over the cucumbers. Set aside to cool to room temperature.
  4. Refrigerate: Chips are lightly pickled after 1 day and grow more flavorful from there. Spears are lightly pickled after 2 days; best flavor develops around day 5 or 6. Keeps in the fridge for several weeks.

Quick Pickled Green Onions

Makes about 8 servings | Prep: 15 minutes | Pickling: 2 hours minimum (best after 24–48 hours)

Ready to eat after 2 hours, but the flavor deepens significantly after 24–48 hours. Keeps refrigerated up to 1 month as long as the onions stay fully submerged in brine.

Source: https://www.forkintheroad.co/quick-pickled-green-onions/

Ingredients

Green onions and aromatics

  • 1 bunch green onions (about 10), roots trimmed
  • 1-inch piece fresh ginger
  • 2 whole garlic cloves
  • 2 teaspoons ground mustard
  • 1 teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes (optional)

Brine

  • 2 cups water
  • 1 cup rice vinegar (or white wine vinegar, apple cider vinegar, or plain white vinegar)
  • 1 tablespoon salt
  • 1 tablespoon sugar

Steps

  1. Prep the green onions:
    • Cut off the roots.
    • Either slice into thin rounds for sprinkling, or cut each green onion in half lengthwise and then into 2–4-inch spears for layering on salads, burgers, and sandwiches.
  2. Pack the jar: Add the green onions to a large jar. Add the ginger, garlic, ground mustard, and Aleppo pepper (if using).
  3. Make the brine:
    • Combine the water, vinegar, salt, and sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve.
    • Pour the hot brine over the green onions until completely submerged. Close the lid tightly.
  4. Let the jar cool to room temperature on the counter, then refrigerate. Ready after 2 hours, best after 24–48 hours. Keeps up to 1 month refrigerated.

Quick Pickled Red Onions

Makes about 8 servings | Prep: 5 minutes | Total: 15 minutes

Great on burgers, grain bowls, salads, sandwiches, or a cheese board. Ready to eat in just 15 minutes, and keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

Source: https://www.kitchentreaty.com/quick-pickled-red-onions/

Ingredients

Red onion

  • 1 medium red onion, peeled, halved, and sliced as thinly as possible

Brine

  • 3/4 cup apple cider vinegar (or white vinegar)
  • 1/2 cup water
  • 2 teaspoons granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt

Steps

  1. Slice the onion as thinly as possible and pack into a quart-size mason jar.
  2. Make the brine: Add the vinegar, water, sugar, and salt to a small saucepan. Bring just to a boil over high heat, stirring to dissolve.
  3. Carefully pour the hot brine over the onions. Press the onions down with a spoon to make sure they are fully submerged.
  4. Let sit at room temperature for 15 minutes, then serve. Store covered in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, keeping the onions submerged in liquid.

★ Pikliz

Makes 1 quart | Prep: 30 min | Ready after: 3 days' pickling

The traditional Haitian accompaniment to Pork Griot. Also wonderful with rice and beans, roast chicken, or any dish that needs a spicy, vinegary punch. Keeps refrigerated for at least 3 weeks.

Source: Patrick Celestin, adapted by Melissa Clark (NYT Cooking)

Ingredients

Pickle

  • 2 cups thinly sliced green cabbage
  • 1 medium onion, halved and thinly sliced
  • 1 large carrot, peeled and coarsely grated (1 cup)
  • 1/2 medium bell pepper (green, red or yellow), seeded and thinly sliced (1 cup)
  • 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  • 4 Scotch bonnet or habanero chiles, seeded and very thinly sliced
  • 4 garlic cloves, finely chopped
  • 1 1/4 tsp kosher salt
  • 12 black peppercorns
  • 4 whole cloves

Brine

  • 1 1/2 cups cane vinegar, cider vinegar or white vinegar
  • Juice of 1/2 lime

Steps

  1. Combine cabbage, onion, carrot, bell pepper, scallions, chiles, garlic, salt, peppercorns, and cloves in a large bowl. Toss well.
  2. Pack tightly into a 1-quart jar with a tightfitting lid. Pour vinegar and lime juice over vegetables, pressing down until completely submerged. Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 days before opening. Keeps for at least 3 weeks refrigerated.

Desserts

General

★ Lauren's Banana Pudding

Serves 10–12 | Prep: 15 min | Rest: 1 hr (pudding) + overnight | Total: ~1.25 hrs active

Inspired by Magnolia Bakery.

Source: Lauren Muhlheim

Ingredients

Pudding base (1 hour ahead)

  • 1½ cups cold water
  • 1 (14 oz) can sweetened condensed milk
  • ⅔ cup instant vanilla pudding powder (or 1 whole box)

Whipped cream

  • 3 cups heavy cream

Assembly

  • 1 box vanilla wafers
  • 3–4 bananas, sliced

Steps

  1. Whisk together cold water, sweetened condensed milk, and pudding powder until smooth. Let sit until congealed, about 1 hour.
  2. In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream until soft peaks form.
  3. Fold pudding mixture into the whipped cream. In a large serving bowl, start with a layer of vanilla wafers, then sliced bananas, then pudding. Repeat layers until ingredients are used up. Refrigerate overnight so wafers soften.

Fresh Cranberry Mold

Fills one small mold; triple the recipe for a large mold.
Using only 1 cup water per Jell-O package (instead of 2) gives a firmer, more concentrated mold.

Source: Family recipe card, attributed to Grandmother Brenda

Ingredients

Jell-O base

  • 2 packages red Jell-O, made with only 1 cup boiling water per package (2 cups total); chill until slightly thickened

Fruit mixture

  • 1/2 lb fresh cranberries
  • 1 apple, unpeeled
  • 1 orange, unpeeled
  • 1 cup sugar
  • 1 cup crushed pineapple with juice

Nuts

  • 1 cup pecans

Steps

  1. Make Jell-O using only 1 cup boiling water per package. Let cool until slightly thickened.
  2. Put cranberries, apple (with peel), and orange (with peel) through a meat grinder. Mix all — juice included — with sugar and crushed pineapple.
  3. Fold fruit mixture into the thickened Jell-O. Stir in pecans.
  4. Pour into mold(s). Refrigerate until fully set.

Thai

Mango with Sticky Rice (Khao Neow Mamuang)

Serves about 8

Scaled to 1 mango. The original recipe used 2 mangoes and was labeled "serves 6" in the book, but the full-recipe quantities are more consistent with 16–18 dessert portions. This half-batch serves about 8.
The sweet sticky rice can be made in advance but should be eaten the same day.
Use glutinous (sticky) rice only — regular rice will not work.

Source: "A Passion for Thai Cooking" by Sompon and Elizabeth Nabnian, p. 136

Ingredients

Rice

  • 300g (2 cups) sticky rice (glutinous rice), soaked in water at least 3 hours or overnight

Thick coconut sauce

  • 250ml (1 cup) thick coconut milk
  • 100g (1/2 cup) sugar
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Thin coconut sauce

  • 60ml (1/4 cup) thin coconut milk
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • Pinch of salt

To serve

  • 1 mango
  • 1-1/2 teaspoons sesame seeds, roasted

Steps

  1. Steam the soaked sticky rice for 15–20 minutes until cooked.
  2. While the rice steams, mix the thick coconut sauce ingredients together in a bowl.
  3. Transfer the cooked rice to a bowl while still hot. Add the thick coconut sauce and combine thoroughly. Leave to rest 30–50 minutes so the rice fully absorbs the coconut milk.
  4. Mix the thin coconut sauce ingredients together and set aside.
  5. When ready to serve, divide the sticky rice into portions. Peel the mango and slice thinly. Lay mango slices on top of the rice. Pour the thin coconut sauce over the mango and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

Drinks

Melon Ball

Makes 1 drink

Source: The Kitchn

Ingredients

  • 2 oz Midori
  • 1 oz vodka
  • Fresh-squeezed orange juice, to top
  • Fresh melon balls, for garnish (optional)

Steps

  1. Fill a glass with ice. Add Midori and vodka.
  2. Top off with orange juice.
  3. Garnish with melon balls, if desired.
